Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eAmbiguousOutput if the containment cannot be determined. Returns eOutOfMemory if the hit array allocation comes back null. In the event of an error, the hit array reference pointer is unchanged, and thus likely points to a null object, and the number of hits found is returned as zero.

Geometric properties query. Returns the mass properties contributed by this topology object. The mass properties are returned as an AcBrMassProps object, with an entire chain of transforms from the subentity path applied where appropriate. The density (if supplied) is used to scale the mass properties; otherwise a uniforma unity density is assumed. The achieved tolerance (if supplied), relative to the volume ,is returned as a double. If this topology object is uninitialised, eUninitialisedObejct is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. In the cases of AcBrFace, AcBrLoop, AcBrEdge, and AcBrVertex, this function is disabled and returns Acad::eNotApplicable since faces, loops, edges and vertices have no volume and mass properties. In the event of an error, the mass properties reference argument's value is unchanged.

This function returns the perimeter length of this topology object, with the maximum scale factor applied from the nested transformations. The achieved relative tolerance (if supplied) is returned as a double. If this topology object is uninitialised, eUninitialisedObejct is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. In the case of AcBrVertex this function is disabled and returns Acad::eNotApplicable since vertices have no length. In the event of an error, the length reference argument's value is unchanged.

Point containment query. Determines whether a point lies inside or outside the current object's topological boundary. If it lies outside, AcGe::kOutside is returned along with a null container object. If inside, AcGe::kInside is returned along with a copy of the current object. If the point lies on the topological boundary of the current object, AcGe::kOnBoundary is returned along with the lowest level topology object, which corresponds to a containment of the point. For example, if the point lies along an edge boundary of a face, the edge is returned. For the point and the current topology object to be in the same evaluation space, the entire inverted chain of transforms from the object ID array is applied to the point before testing for point containment. The container object is passed as a null AcBrEntity base class reference pointer for getPointContainment() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eAmbiguousOutput if the containment cannot be determined. Returns eOutOfMemory if the container entity comes back null. In the event of an error, the containment reference parameter's value is unchanged and thus is meaningless. The container object reference pointer is unchanged, and thus likely points to a null object.

Subentity path query. Returns the full subentity path in AutoCAD for the current object. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated.

This function returns the surface area of this topology object as a double, with the maximum scale factor applied from the nested transformations. The achieved relative tolerance (if supplied) is returned as a double. If this topology object is uninitialised, eUninitialisedObejct is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. In the cases of AcBrFace, AcBrLoop, AcBrEdge, and AcBrVertex, this function is disabled and returns Acad::eNotApplicable since faces, loops, edges and vertices have no area. In the event of an error, the area reference argument's value is unchanged.
Returns the validation level currently being used by this topology object.

This function returns the volume of this topology object as a double, with the maximum scale factor applied for the nested transforms. The achieved tolerance (if supplied0 is returned as a double. If this topology object is uninitialised, eUninitialisedObejct is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. In the cases of AcBrFace, AcBrLoop, AcBrEdge, and AcBrVertex, this function is disabled and returns Acad::eNotApplicable since faces, loops, edges and vertices have no volume. In the event of an error, the volume reference argument's value is unchanged.

Equivalence function. This ObjectARX function is redefined to check content equality between two topology objects. If either object is invalid or is not a topology object, the function returns kFalse. kTrue is returned when the object is valid and has been equated to another valid topology object of the same subclass. Equivalence is defined as having the same subentity path.
Validator function. kTrue is returned if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty).

The set() topology data initialiser is used to set this topology object's internal data using a subentity path in AutoCAD. This initialises an object instantiated with the default constructor and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as setting the validation level to AcBr::kFullValidation. If the subentity path is empty, or the object ID array is empty or contains any null entries, Acad::eNullObjectID is returned. If the subentity is not the right type for this topology object, Acad::eWrongSubentityType is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object is not an AcDb3dSolid, AcDbRegion, AcDbBody or derived type, Acad::eWrongObjectType is returned. If the subentity ID contains a null index or fails to map to a valid subentity, Acad::eInvalidIndex is returned. In the cases of AcBrComplex, AcBrShell, and AcBrLoop, this function is disabled an returns Acad::eNotApplicable since complexes, shells and loops do not have subentity representations in AutoCAD. In the special case of AcBrEdge, if the edge is free or otherwise unembedded (such as a wire edge), Acad::eUnsuitableTopology is returned. Singularities map to edges in AutoCAD and thus can be used to initialise an AcBrEdge for the express purpose of querying the vertex, but cannot be queried for the curve geometry or used to set a loop edge traverser. In the event of an error, this topology object's internal data is unchanged.

This function initializes the AcBrEntity object with a pointer to its internal representation and, optionally, to the corresponding subentity path. If the subentity path is not supplied, it is assumed for the purpose of determining the coordinate system that the associated solid is not database active. If the subentity pointer is null, returns Acad::eInvalidInput.

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the object to a specific subentity path in AutoCAD. This initializes an object instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eNullObjectId if the subentity path is null, or the object ID array is empty or contains a null final entry. Returns eNullSubentityId if the subentity ID is null (exception: AcBrBrep, for which a null subentity ID is the only legitimate value). Returns eWrongSubentityType if the subentity is the wrong type for the given subclass. Returns eWrongObjectType if the AutoCAD entity is not an AcDb3dSolid, AcDbRegion, or AcDbBody, or the associated database object cannot be opened. Returns eMissingTopology if the subentity ID fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. In the special case of AcBrEdge, if the edge represents a singularity (for example, the apex of a cone) or is free or otherwise unembedded (such as a wire edge), eUnsuitableTopology is returned. Singularities may be used to initialize AcBrVertex instead, but wires are currently unsupported by the AcBr library.

This prioritisation function sets the validation level to be used in all data queries that require access to the associated AutoCAD object. In general, this means any function that accessess the Brep topology. If set to kNoValidation, eBrepChanged will no longer be returned by functions called on this topology object Any query that returns a newly instantiated AcBr object uses this topology object's validation level to initialise the new object.

The AcBrFace class is the interface class for Brep faces. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to the face level of a Brep, and thus serves as a mapping between AutoCAD face subentities and AcBr. It is also used to set the first face of a global AcBrBrepFaceTraverser or the face owner of an AcBrFaceLoopTraverser. Faces are primary brep elements and thus have associated geometry (that is, surfaces). This class provides an indirect link between AcGe and AcDb3dSolid, AcDbRegion, and AcDbBody. Used By AcBrBrepFaceTraverser::setFace(), AcBrBrepFaceTraverser::getFace(), AcBrFaceLoopTraverser::setFace(), AcBrFaceLoopTraverser::getFace(), AcBrLoop::getFace()
The AcBrFaceLoopTraverser class is the interface class for face-loop traversers. It is used to get access to edges through their loop uses.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

List owner query. Returns the face owner of the loop list. The face object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getFace() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidInput if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's face-loop list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingSubentity if the face fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the face reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

List position query. Returns the current position in the face-loop list. The loop object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getLoop() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's face-loop list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if there is no loop at the current position in the face-loop list. Returns eMissingSubentity if the loop fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the loop reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific face-loop list, starting at the first loop in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eInvalidInput if the face reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the face reference object's subentity pointer was last set. Returns eMissingTopology if the face reference object's subentity path fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. Returns eUnsuitableTopology if the face is neither edge-bounded nor vertex-bounded (for example, a sphere or a true torus, where there are no loops nor boundary curve geometry).

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific face-loop list and starting position. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match the loop. The face list owner is inferred from the loop, as it is unique. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the loop reference object is uninitialised , or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the reference object was last set.

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific starting position in the face-loop list (that is, change the first loop marker from the default to the specified loop). This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for next() and done(). It must be called after setFace(), to have a valid list to set position. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's face-loop list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eInvalidInput if the loop reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the loop reference object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the loop reference object is invalidated. Returns eObjectIdMismatch if the traverser and the loop reference object do not have the same owning AutoCAD entity. Returns eMissingTopology if the loop reference object's subentity ID fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. Returns eTopologyMismatch if the loop is not in the face-loop list.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.
Calculates the area of the face.
Line containment query. Returns the relation of an external line segment to the face (inside, outside, and so on). Deprecated in favor of AcBrEntity::getLineContainment().

Orientation query. Returns a simple Boolean indicating whether the outside of the face is in the direction of the surface normal (kTrue) or in the opposite direction (kFalse), at any position. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the surface geometry is missing. In the event of an error, the orientation reference parameter's value is unchanged and is thus meaningless.
Point containment query. Returns the relation of an external point to the face (inside, outside, and so on). Deprecated in favor of AcBrEntity::getPointContainment().

The getShell() upward adjacency query returns the shell that is bounded by this face (always unique). The shell is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getShell() to set. If this face object is uninitialized, eUninitialisedObject is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. If the shell is missing, Acad::eNotInDatabase is returned. In the event of an error, the shell reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

Surface instantiation. Returns the face's underlying surface as an AcGe external bounded surface (cast to the AcGeSurface base class), with the entire chain of transforms from the object ID array applied. The surface is passed as a null AcGeSurface base class reference pointer for getSurface() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the surface geometry is missing. Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe surface comes back null. Returns eWrongObjectType if any of the associated AutoCAD database objects from the chained transforms cannot be opened. In the event of an error, the surface reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.

The getSurfaceAsNurb() model space surface query returns this face's underlying surface as a subset AcGeNurbSurface, with the entire chain of transforms from the subentity path applied. The surface is converted to a NURB (if necessary) using the supplied fit tolerance (adjusted by the inverse scale factor from the nested transforms, in order to be in the same evaluation space as this face) and is subset to the uv range that results from projecting the face's model space bounding box onto the uv parameter space grid of the surface. The achieved fit tolerance (if supplied) is returned as a double, with the maximum scale factor applied from the nested transforms. The surface is instantiated by the user and passed by reference for getSurfaceAsNurb() to set. If this face object is uninitialized, eUninitialisedObject is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. If the fitTolRequired argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default fit tolerance is used. If a negative value is supplied, Acad::eOutOfRange is returned. If the surface geometry is missing, Acad::eDegenerateGeometry is returned. If the transform has non-uniform scaling, Acad::eCannotScaleNonUniformly is returned as a warning message, along with the untransformed surface. In the event of an error, the surface and fit tolerance reference arguments are unchanged.

The getSurfaceAsTrimmedNurbs() model space trimmed surface query converts this face's underlying surface to a trimmed representation. It returns this representation as an array of AcGeExternalBoundedSurface pointers (along with the array size, as numNurbs), with the entire chain of transforms from the subentity path applied. The surface is converted to a NURB (if necessary) and split along its seams (if crossed by the face boundaries). The surface array is passed as a null AcBrExternalBoundedSurface reference pointer for getSurfaceAsTrimmedNurbs() to instantiate. It is the user's responsibility to delete the returned array of surfaces. If this face object is uninitialized, eUninitialisedObject is returned. If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set, eBrepChanged is returned. If the surface geometry is missing, eMissingGeometry is returned. In the event of an error, the surface array reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null array, and the number of nurbs is zero.

Surface type query. Used to determine the best match between the face's underlying surface and the surface types supported in AcGe. This is the same as the type returned by the converter function AcGeExternalSurface::isNativeSurface() invoked on the surface returned by AcBrFace::getSurface(), and thus serves as a shortcut for filtering surfaces by type. If the surface type is not supported as a surface type in AcGe, kExternalBoundedSurface is returned. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the surface geometry is missing. In the event of an error, the surface type reference parameter is set to kExternalBoundedSurface.

The AcBrHit class is the interface class for contexted hits generated by line containment queries. (A 'contexted' hit is one that represents a vertex in the context of line containment as applied to the topology.) This class defines the functions that are pertinent to contexted hits, and cannot be directly set by the user as the initialization requirements are only available internally at the time of a call to AcBrEntity::getLineContainment(). It is derived from AcRxObject in order to provide full-service, runtime type checking, and so on.
Assignment operator. Performs a deep replacement of all member data.
Copy constructor. Performs a deep copy of all member data.

Status query. Returns a Boolean value indicating whether the associated AutoCAD object has changed since this hit object was last set. Returns kFalse if the associated object has not changed or is non-database resident. Returns kTrue if the associated object has changed or if it is not possible to determine if it has changed (which generally indicates that the AutoCAD object has gone out of scope due to deletion).
For internal use only. This function retrieves this AcBrEntity element's internal data using an unexported type.

Associated topology query. Returns the topology object whose line containment test generated this hit object. The topology object is passed as a null AcBrEntity base class reference pointer for this function to instantiate. Returns Acad::eUninitialisedObject if this hit object is uninitialised. Returns eBrepChanged if the AutoCAD object associated with this topology object has been modified since this hit object's internal data was last set. Returns Acad::eOutOfMemory if the AcBrEntity allocation comes back null. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the associated topology object fails to map to a valid subentity ID.

Entity entered instantiation. Returns the dimensionally lowest topological entity that contains the segment along the original line bound by this hit and the next hit, or NULL if this is either the final hit in the hit array or the segment exits and then re-enters the object being tested. The entity is passed as a null AcBrEntity reference pointer for getEntityEntered() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the hit is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the AutoCAD entity associated with the line containment test that produced this hit changed since the hit path was last set. As a side effect, the hit is invalidated. Returns eAmbiguousOutput if the entity hit is not a valid brep, face or edge in the associated AutoCAD entity. Returns eOutOfMemory if the entity allocation comes back null. In the event of an error, the entity reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.
Entity hit instantiation. Returns the dimensionally lowest topological entity that contains this hit.

Point instantiation. Returns the model space point that corresponds to the hit, which is the point in space where a line is broken into segments by topological containment. The model space point is returned as an AcGe 3D point, with the entire chain of transforms from the object ID array applied. The point is passed as a null AcGePoint3d reference pointer for getPoint() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the hit is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the AutoCAD entity associated with the line containment test that produced this hit changed since the hit path was last set. As a side effect, the hit is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the point geometry is missing. Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe point comes back null. Returns eWrongObjectType if any of the associated AutoCAD database objects from the chained transforms cannot be opened, eWrongObjectType is returned. In the event of an error, the point reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.
Prioritisation Query. Returns the validation level currently being used by this hit object.

Equivalence function. This ObjectARX function is redefined to check content equality between two hit objects. If either object is invalid or is not a hit object, the function returns kFalse. kTrue is returned when the object is valid and has been equated to another valid hit object. Equivalence is defined as having the same hit path.
Validator function. kTrue is returned if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty).
For internal use only. This function is used to set this hit object's internal data using an unexported data type.

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the object to a specific hit path. This initializes an object instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eInvalidInput if the hit path reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the AutoCAD entity associated with the line containment test that produced this hit changed since the hit path reference object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the hit path reference object is invalidated. This function requires low-level data that is only available at the time of a call to AcBrEntity::getLineContainment(), so the hit path parameter is an unexported type.

Prioritisation function. Sets the validation level to be used in all data queries that require access to the associated AutoCAD object. If set to kNoValidation, ebrepChanged will no longer be returned by functions called on this hit object. Any query that returns a newly instantiated AcBr object uses this validation level to initialise the new object.

The AcBrLoop class is the interface class for brep loops. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to the loop level of a brep, which is not exposed in AutoCAD and thus cannot be directly set to anything meaningful. It is (re)set indirectly by the traversers. It is also used to set the first loop of an AcBrFaceLoopTraverser. Loops are secondary brep elements and thus have no associated geometry. They do, however, provide context for parameter space curves (via AcBrLoopEdgeTraverser).

The AcBrLoopEdgeTraverser class is the interface class for loop-edge traversers. It is used to get access to edge-bound data that requires the context of a specific face/loop usage, such as parameter curves. In order to provide the tightest coupling with radial edge traversals (that is, AcBrEdgeLoopTraverser), the face is represented by its loop boundary at the shared edge. Used By AcBrEdgeLoopTraverser::setEdgeAndLoop()
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

List position query. Returns the current position in the loop-edge list. The edge object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getEdge() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if there is no edge at the current position in the loop-edge list. Returns eMissingSubentity if the edge fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the edge reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

Orientation query. Returns a simple Boolean indicating whether the natural orientation of the edge from vertex1 to vertex2 is in the direction of the loop (kTrue) or in the opposite direction (kFalse). Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. In the event of an error, the orientation reference parameter's value is unchanged and is thus meaningless.

List owner query. Returns the loop owner of the edge list. The loop object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getLoop() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidInput if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingSubentity if the loop fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the loop reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

Oriented curve instantiation. Returns an oriented model space curve (unique to the current edge in the loop-edge list) as an AcGe external 3D curve (cast to the AcGeCurve3d base class), with the entire chain of transforms from the object ID array applied. The curve is passed as a null AcGeCurve3d base class reference pointer for getOrientedCurve() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the curve is missing. Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe curve comes back null. Returns eWrongObjectType if any of the associated AutoCAD database objects from the chained transforms cannot be opened. In the event of an error, the curve reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.

Model space query. Returns the current edge in the loop edge list's underlying curve as an oriented, subset AcGeNurbCurve2d object, with the entire chain of transforms from the edge's subentity path applied. The curve is converted to a NURB (if neccessary) using the supplied fit tolerance (adjusted by the inverse scale factor from the nested transforms, in order to be in the same evaluation space as the current edge). The oriented model space curve represents the curve edge's associated curve as a NURB oriented to flow in the direction of the loop. This is equivalent to taking the 3d NURB curve returned by AcBrEdge::getCurveasNurb() and conditionally applying the XOR'ed edge and loop-edge orientations using AcGeCurve3d::reverseParam(). Returns Acad::eUninitialisedObject if the traverser object is uninitialised. Returns ebrepChanged if the AutoCAD object has been modified since it was last set. Returns Acad::eOutOfrange if a negative fit tolerance is supplied. Returns Acad::eDegenerateGeometry if the parameter curve is missing.

Parameter curve instantiation. Returns an oriented parameter space curve (unique to the current edge in the loop-edge list) as an AcGe external 2D curve (cast to the AcGeCurve2d base class). The entire chain of transforms from the object ID array is ignored, as they are only pertinent to model space and not to parameter space. The parameter curve is passed as a null AcGeCurve2d base class reference pointer for getParamCurve() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the parameter curve is missing (this may sometimes happen if an edge crosses a seam). Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe parameter curve comes back null. In the event of an error, the parameter curve reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.

Parameter space query. Returns the current edge in the loop edge list's underlying parameter curve as an oriented, subset AcGeNurbCurve2d object, with the entire chain of transformations from the edge's subentity path ignored as they are only pertinent to mode space. The parameter curve represents the current edge's model space curve projected onto the UV parameter space grid of the surface associated with the face that is bounded by the loop owner of the edge list (always unique). The fit tolerance is currently ignored, as the internal modeler stores all paramter curves as NURBS, so we do not request a new one to be computed. The curve is subset, in its orientation with respect to the loop, to the edge's bounding vertices (i.e., the edge and loop-edge orientations are XOR'ed and used to determine te order of parameterisation). Returns Acad::eUninitialisedObject if the traverser object is uninitialised. Returns ebrepChanged if the AutoCAD object has been modified since it was last set. Returns Acad::eOutOfrange if a negative fit tolerance is supplied. Returns Acad::eDegenerateGeometry if the parameter curve is missing.

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific starting position in the loop-edge list (that is, change the first edge marker from the default to the specified edge). This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for next() and done(). It must be called after setLoop() or setLoopAndEdge(), in order to have a valid list to set position. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eUninitialized if the traverser is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eInvalidInput if the edge reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the edge reference object's subentity path was last set. Returns eObjectIdMismatch if the traverser and the edge reference object do not have the same owning AutoCAD entity. Returns eMissingTopology if the edge reference object's subentity ID fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. Returns eTopologyMismatch if the edge is not in the loop-edge list.

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific loop-edge list, starting at the first edge in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eInvalidInput if the face-loop reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the face-loop reference object's face owner was last set. As a side effect, the face-loop reference object is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if the face-loop reference object's face owner fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. Returns eUnsuitableTopology if the loop represents a singularity (such as at the apex of a cone).

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific loop-edge list and starting position. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eInvalidInput if the edge-loop reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the edge-loop reference object's subentity pointer was last set. As a side effect, the edge-loop reference object is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if the edge-loop reference object's edge owner or current loop fails to map to a valid subentity pointer.

The AcBrLoopVertexTraverser class is the interface class for loop-vertex traversers. It is used to get access to vertices that are at isolated points in a model (that is, singularities, such as the apex of a cone). Although the loop vertex is essentially a 1:1 query, it is isolated to a traverser rather than being offered as a query on the AcBrLoop class, as it represents a special case and is part of the boundary information of a face (via face-loop traversal).
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

List owner query. Returns the loop owner of the loop-vertex. The loop object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getLoop() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidInput if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side-effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingSubentity if the loop fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the loop reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

Parameter point instantiation. Returns a parameter space point (representative of a degenerate parameter space curve, which is a singularity/loop vertex) as an AcGe 2D point. The parameter point is passed as a null AcGePoint2d reference pointer for getParamPoint() to instantiate. AcGePoint2d is more representative of face boundary data than the u,v parameter pair. The entire chain of transforms from the object ID array is ignored since they are pertinent to model space, not to parameter space. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop vertex was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if either the point geometry or surface geometry is missing. Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe parameter point comes back null. In the event of an error, the parameter point reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.

List position query. Returns the loop-vertex. The vertex object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getVertex() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's loop-edge list was last set. As a side-effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if there is no loop-vertex. Returns eMissingSubentity if the vertex fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the vertex reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).

Initializer function. Used to (re)set the traverser to a specific loop-vertex. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error. Returns eInvalidInput if the face-loop reference object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty), or if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the face-loop reference object's face owner was last set. As a side-effect, the face-loop reference object is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if the face-loop reference object's face owner fails to map to a valid subentity pointer. Returns eUnsuitableTopology if there is an edge list on the loop (that is, if the loop does not represent a singularity).

List initialiser. used to set this traverser to a specific loop vertex list and starting position. This initialises a traverses instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the vertex. The loop list owner is inferred from the vertex as it is unique. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the vertex reference object is uninitialised or the associated AutoCAD object has been modifed since the vertex reference object was last set.

List position initialiser. Used to set this traverser's starting position to a specific vertex in the loop vertex list, which resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns eUninitialisedObejct if this traverser object is uninitialised. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the vertex reference object is uninitialised. Returns Acad::eWrongDatabase if the vertex is not in the loop edge list or is associated with a different AutoCAD object or revision.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

Face query. Returns the face that is bounded by the loop (always unique). The face is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getFace() to (re)set. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's subentity path was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if the face is missing. Returns eMissingSubentity if the face fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the face reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized (that is, empty).
Type query. Returns the type of this loop.

The AcBrMassProps struct contains the volume, the mass (equal to the volume unless the density is specified as anything other than unity), the centroid (center of gravity), the radii of gyration (square root of the moments of inertia divided by the rigid body mass), the rigid body moments of inertia (mass times the square of the axial radius), the products of inertia (mass times the distance from the centroid to the Y,Z plane times the distance from the centroid to the X,Z plane), the principal moments at the centroid (derived from the products of inertia), and the principal axes at the centroid.

The AcBrMesh class is the interface base class for meshes. This class defines the functions that are common to all dimensions of meshes, and cannot be instantiated as it has no meaning on its own. A mesh is a network of nodal approximations to curves, surfaces, and volumes in a brep object (or subobject), and thus has associated geometry. The geometry, however, is stored at the individual elements and nodes, as are the mappings back to the original brep topology. Each supported dimension of meshing has its own associated class. General faceting is exposed through the AcBrMesh2d subclass.

The AcBrMesh2d class is the interface class for 2D meshes. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to a two-dimensional (or faceted) mesh of either an entire solid or an individual surface. A 2D mesh is a mesh that maps to a 3D face set, and thus has associated geometry. The geometry, however, is stored at the individual elements and nodes, as are the mappings back to the original brep topology. A 2D mesh can also be thought of as a wire network, and its element set can be used to define a surface wireframe model. Nonmanifold edges and vertices from the 3D face set are ignored and are not mapped to the mesh. Degenerate elements are discarded, along with their unique nodes.
The AcBrMesh2dControl class is the interface class for 2d mesh controls. This class defines the functions that are specific to setting controls for the generation of 2d meshes.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.
The getElementShape() control query returns the element shape criteria as a dedicated AcBr::Element2dShape enum.
The getMaxAspectRatio() control query returns the maximum aspect ratio as a double.

The setElementShape() control initializer sets the element shape criteria. Element shapes can be triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons. A request for all quadrilateral elements may generate some triangles along the original edge boundaries due to node sharing constraints for adjacent elements on neighboring faces. A request for all polygonal elements will produce one element per face, with nodes and element edges corresponding to the discretisation of the boundary curves of the original face. If the elementShape argument is not supplied or is set to AcBr::kDefault, the element shape defaults to one level of triangles along the original edges, with quadrilaterals used for the interior mesh (if there is one).

The setMaxAspectRatio() control initializer sets the maximum aspect ratio of width to height for a 2d mesh element. Values between zero and one invert the aspect ratio relationship to a height to width ratio. If the maxAspectRatio argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default behavior is to minimize the number of elements required to meet the curvature-based criteria (maxAngTol and maxDistTol), for example, generate long, shallow elements along the length of a cone surface. Returns Acad::eOutOfRange if a negative value is supplied.

The AcBrMesh2dElement2dTraverser class is the interface class for mesh element traversers. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to a 2D element in the global context of a 2D mesh. It is used to seed a downward hierarchical traversal of a 2D mesh, or to traverse all of the unique 2D elements and nodes in a 2D mesh.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The getElement() list position query returns the element at the current position in the mesh element list. The element object is instantiated by the caller and passed as by reference for getElement() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. In the event of an error, the element reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The getMesh() list owner query returns the mesh owner of the mesh element list. The mesh object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getMesh() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. In the event of an error, the mesh reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The setElement() list position initializer is used to set this traverser's starting position to a specific element in the mesh element list, which resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eMeshChanged if the associated mesh object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the element reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated mesh object has been modified since the element reference object was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the element is not in the mesh element list or is associated with a different mesh object or revision. In the event of an error, this traverser's mesh element list is unchanged.

The setMesh() list owner initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific mesh element list, starting at the first element in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the mesh reference object is uninitialized. In the event of an error, this traverser's mesh element list is unchanged.

The setMeshAndElement() list initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific mesh element list and starting position. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for next() and done(). The mesh list owner is inferred from the element, as it is unique. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the element reference object is uninitialized. In the event of an error, this traverser's mesh element list is unchanged.

The AcBrMesh2dFilter class is the interface class for 2d mesh filters. This class defines the mapping between topology objects and 2d mesh controls that are used as filters on 2d mesh generation. Its main purpose is to provide a flexible, standalone type for the argument to the AcBrMesh2d::generate() mesh generation function.

The insert() function associates a specific 2d mesh control with a topology object, and adds it to the multimap. For now, only a single entry is supported, and repeated calls will overwrite previous values. The proper syntax is to supply the function with the return value of a call to make_pair(). The pair structure is defined below. This structure and the make_pair() function may be replaced in a future release of AutoCAD. struct pair { AcBrEntity* first; AcBrMesh2dControl second; pair() : first((AcBrEntity*)NULL), second(AcBrMesh2dControlDefault) {} pair( const AcBrEntity*& a, const AcBrMesh2dControl& b) : first((AcBrEntity*)a), second(b) {}};make_pair() accepts an entity and a control, combining them into a pair and returning the new pair structure instance. (You can also call a pair structure constructor directly.) inline pairmake_pair( const AcBrEntity*& entity, const AcBrMesh2dControl& control);
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The generate() mesh generation function is used to set the mesh using a filter (such as a face with associated mesh controls). This initializes a mesh object instantiated with the default constructor, and deletes any existing elements and nodes. It also indirectly sets the topology object associated with the mesh. This function is interruptible using CTRL-C. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the mesh filter contains a null or invalid topology key, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the mesh filter was last set. Returns eUnsuitableTopology if the topology key is of lower dimension than this 2D mesh object (for instance, a 1d edge or a 0d vertex). Returns Acad::eUserBreak if the mesh generation is interrupted using CTRL-C. Returns eDegenerateTopology if the mesh fails to generate elements on a specific face due to improperly formed topology such as the presence of an interior loop with no complementary exterior loop). Returns Acad::eAmbiguousOutput if the mesh fails to generate any elements. Returns Acad::eDegenerateGeometry if the mesh generates one or more degenerate elements (that is, with fewer than three nodes--the minimum for a 2D element).
The get() mesh data query is for internal use only. It retrieves this mesh's internal data using an unexported type.
The set() mesh data initializer is for internal use only. It is used to set this mesh's internal data using an unexported type.

The AcBrMeshControl class is the interface base class for mesh controls. This class defines the functions that are common to all mesh control derived classes, and cannot be instantiated as it has no meaning on its own. It is derived from AcRxObject in order to provide full service run-time type-checking, etc.
The getAngTol() control query returns the maximum angle tolerance as a double.
The getDistTol() control query returns the maximum distance tolerance as a double.
The getMaxNodeSpacing() control query returns the maximum node spacing as a double.
The getMaxSubdivisions() control query returns the maximum number of subdivisions as an unsigned 32-bit integer.

The AcRxObject::isEqualTo() equivalence function is redefined to check content equality between two mesh control objects. Returns kTrue when the object is valid and has been equated to another valid mesh control object of the same subclass. Equivalence is defined as having the same control settings.

The setAngTol() control initializer sets the maximum angle tolerance (measured in radians) between the normals evaluated at any two nodes in a mesh element. In most cases, values between 15 and 25 degrees give acceptable results. The proper value to set is generally independent of model size. Angle tolerance, in conjunction with distance tolerance, effects curvature based node spacing. If the angTol argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default behavior is to use a value that will generate a rather coarse mesh. Returns Acad::eOutOfRange if a negative value is supplied.

The setDistTol() control initializer sets the maximum allowable distance in world coordinates between a mesh element and the original geometry (as measured at the mid-edges and centroid of each element). In a 2d mesh, this is the same as the distance in world coordinates from a point on the true surface to the closest point on any of its approximating 2d elements. The proper value to set is dependent on model size. Distance tolerance, in conjunction with angle tolerance, affects curvature based node spacing. If the distTol argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default behavior is to set it to 5% of the maximum extent of the bounding box, or (in the case of non-zero maxNodeSpacing) to ignore this control entirely. If a negative value is supplied, Acad::eOutOfRange is returned.

The setMaxNodeSpacing() control initializer sets the maximum node spacing in world coordinates. Dimension-specific controls that are applied later in the mesh generation algorithm may also alter the node spacing; especially near the boundaries of the original geometry. Node spacing directly affects the size of the generated elements. The proper value to set is dependent on model size. If the maxNodeSpacing argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default behavior is to ignore distance and defer to curvature-based node spacing (setMaxAngTol and setMaxDistTol). Returns Acad::eOutOfRange if a negative value is supplied.

The setMaxSubdivisions() control initializer sets the maximum number of subdivisions in any one dimension (equivalent to the number of internal uv grid lines), which is imposed by the mesh grid overlay on the original geometry. This control is very inexact in this release due to the underlying modeler's algorithm (which applies subdivisions recursively). As a result, the actual maximum resulting subdivisions in either u or v will be somewhere between the two adjacent powers of two surrounding the specified number of subdivisions. If the maxSubdivisions argument is not supplied or is set to zero, the default behavior is based on mesh dimension and surface type (for example, for a planar face in a 2d mesh, no interior nodes are inserted).

The AcBrMeshEntity class is the interface base class for mesh objects and subobjects. This class defines the functions that are common to all mesh objects and subobjects, and cannot be instantiated as it has no meaning on its own. It is derived from AcRxObject in order to provide full service run-time type-checking for all derived mesh classes.

The brepChanged() status query returns a simple Boolean indicating whether the associated AutoCAD object has changed since this mesh object was last set. Returns kFalse if it has not changed or if the associated object is non-database resident. Returns kTrue if it has changed or if it is not possible to determine whether it has changed (which generally indicates that the AutoCAD object has gone out of scope due to deletion).

The getEntityAssociated() associated topology query returns the dimensionally lowest topology object associated with this mesh object. For a 2d mesh, it returns a face, shell or brep. For a 2d element, it returns a face. For a node, it returns a vertex, edge or face. The topology object is passed as a null AcBrEntity base class reference pointer for getEntityAssociated() to instantiate. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this mesh object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the AutoCAD object associated with the topology object has been modified since this mesh object's internal data was last set. Returns Acad::eWrongSubentityType if the associated topology object is not the right type for this mesh object.. Returns Acad::eOutOfMemory if the AcBrEntity allocation comes back null. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the associated topology object fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the topology reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.
The getValidationLevel() prioritisation query returns a dedicated ValidationType enum corresponding to the validation level currently being used by this mesh object.

The AcRxObject::isEqualTo() equivalence function is redefined to check content equality between two mesh objects. Returns kTrue if this object is valid and has been equated to another valid mesh object of the same subclass. Equivalence is defined as having the same associated topological entity and the same internal data.
The isNull() validator function tests whether this mesh object has been set to anything meaningful. Returns kTrue if it is uninitialized. Returns kFalse if it is valid/initialized.

The setValidationLevel() prioritization function sets the validation level to be used in all data queries that require access to the associated AutoCAD object. In general, this means any function that accesses the brep topology. If set to kNoValidation, eBrepChanged will no longer be returned by functions called on this mesh object. Any query that returns a newly instantiated AcBr object uses this mesh object's validation level to initialize the new object.

The AcBrNode class is the interface class for nodes in a mesh. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to the node level of a mesh, and cannot be directly set by the user as the initialization requirements are only available internally at the time of a call to AcBrMesh2d::generate().
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.
The get() node data query is for internal use only. It retrieves this mesh node's internal data using an unexported type.

The getPoint() model space point query returns this node's underlying point as an AcGePoint3d object, with the entire chain of transforms from the associated topology object's subentity path applied. The point is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getPoint() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this node object is uninitialized. In the event of an error, the point reference argument's value is unchanged.
The set() node data initializer is for internal use only. It is used to set this mesh node's internal data using an unexported type.

The AcBrShell class is the interface class for brep shells. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to the shell level of a brep topology adjacency hierarchy, which is not exposed as a subentity type in AutoCAD and thus cannot be directly set by the user; it is set indirectly by the traversers. It is also used to set the first shell of a shell list in AcBrBrepShellTraverser.

The AcBrShellFaceTraverser class is the interface class for shell face traversers. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to a face in the context of a shell. It is used to get access to downward hierarchical topological adjacencies, such as to traverse faces through their shell/face uses.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The getFace() list position query returns the face at the current position in the shell face list. The face object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getFace() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the face is missing. In the event of an error, the face reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The getShell() list owner query returns the shell owner of the face list. The shell object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getShell() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. In the event of an error, the shell reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The setFace() list position initializer is used to set this traverser's starting position to a specific face in the shell face list, which resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the face reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the face reference object was last set. Returns Acad::eWrongDatabase if the face is not in the shell face list or is associated with a different AutoCAD object or revision. In the event of an error, this traverser's shell face list is unchanged.

The setShell() list owner initializer(1) is used to set this traverser to a specific shell face list, starting at the first face in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the shell. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the shell reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the shell reference object was last set. Returns eDegenerateTopology if the shell is not face-bounded, eDegenerateTopology is returned. In the event of an error, this traverser's shell face list is unchanged.

The setShellAndFace() list initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific shell face list and starting position. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the face. The shell list owner is inferred from the face, as it is unique. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the face reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the face reference object was last set. In the event of an error, this traverser's shell face list is unchanged.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The getComplex() upward adjacency query returns the complex that is bounded by this shell (always unique). The complex is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getComplex() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this shell object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the subentity path was last set. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the complex is missing. In the event of an error, the complex reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.
The getType() shell type query returns a dedicated ShellType enum that identifies this shell as being either kShellExterior or kShellInterior.

The AcBrTraverser class is the interface base class for topology traversers. This class defines the functions that are common to all topology traversers, and cannot be instantiated as it has no meaning on its own. It is derived from AcRxObject in order to provide full-service, runtime type checking for all derived traverser classes.
Assignment (protected). Used by derived class assignment operators to reassign the base class portion of an AcBrTraverser-derived object.
Copy constructor (protected). Used by derived class copy constructors to copy the base class portion of an AcBrTraverser-derived object.

Returns a Boolean value indicating whether the associated AutoCAD object has changed since this topology object was last set. Returns kFalse if the object has not changed or is non-database resident. Returns kTrue either if the object has changed or if it is not possible to determine whether it has changed ( which generally indicates that the AutoCAD object has gone out of scope due to deletion).

Traversal status. kTrue is returned if the entire topological adjacency list has been traversed (using the next() function), as determined by the list owner and the most recently set starting position.
For internal use only. This function retrieves this AcBrEntity element's internal data using an unexported type.
Returns the validation level currently in use by this object.

Equivalence function. This ObjectARX function is redefined to check content equality between two traverser objects. If either object is invalid or is not a traverser object, the function returns kFalse; kTrue is returned when the object is valid and has been equated to another valid traverser object of the same subclass. Equivalence is defined as having the same topological adjacency list owner and list position.
Validator function. kTrue is returned if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty).

Traversal incrementor. Adjusts the traverser to point to the next object in the topological adjacency list. All lists are treated as circular, ordered lists. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated. Returns eMissingTopology if the next object in the topological adjacency list is missing.

Traversal reset. Adjusts the traverser to point to the first object in the topological adjacency list. Returns eInvalidObject if the traverser is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the traverser's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the traverser is invalidated.
The set() element data initializer is for internal use only. It is used to set this traverser element's internal data using an unexported type.

The setValidationLevel() prioritization function sets the validation level to be used in all data queries that require access to the associated AutoCAD object. In general, this means any function that accesses the brep topology. If set to kNoValidation, eBrepChanged will no longer be returned by functions called on this mesh object. Any query that returns a newly instantiated AcBr object uses this mesh object's validation level to initialize the new object.

The AcBrVertex class is the interface class for brep vertices. This class defines the functions that are pertinent to the vertex level of a brep, and thus serves as a mapping between AutoCAD vertex subentities and AcBr. Vertices are primary brep elements and thus have associated geometry (that is, points). This class provides an indirect link between AcGe and AcDb3dSolid, AcDbRegion, and AcDbBody.

The AcBrVertexEdgeTraverser class is the interface class for vertex edge traversers. It is used to seed an upward hierarchical traversal from a specific vertex, or to identify the radial edges around a vertex.
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The getEdge() list position query returns the edge at the current position in the vertex edge list. The edge object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getEdge() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the edge is missing or fails to map to a valid subentity ID. In the event of an error, the edge reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The getVertex() list owner query returns the vertex owner of the edge list. The vertex object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getVertex() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. In the event of an error, the vertex reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The setEdge() list position initializer is used to set this traverser's starting position to a specific edge in the vertex edge list, which resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the edge reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the edge reference object was last set. Returns Acad::eWrongDatabase if the edge is not in the vertex edge list or is associated with a different AutoCAD object or revision. In the event of an error, this traverser's vertex edge list is unchanged.

The setVertex() list owner initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific vertex edge list, starting at the first edge in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the vertex. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the vertex reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the vertex reference object was last set. Returns eDegenerateTopology if the vertex represents a singularity (such as at the apex of a cone). Use the vertex to set an AcBrVertexLoopTraverser instead. In the event of an error, this traverser's vertex edge list is unchanged.

The AcBrVertexLoopTraverser class is the interface class for vertex loop traversers. It is used to seed an upward hierarchical traversal from a specific vertex; to combine upward and downward hierarchical traversals for the radial faces around a vertex in conjunction with an AcBrLoopVertexTraverser; or to handle singularities (such as the apex of a cone, where there is no edge geometry). The order of loops around a vertex is persistent and is consistently counter-clockwise .
Assignment operator. Assigns to the left operand the same contents as the src object.
Copy constructor. Instantiates an object initialized to the same contents as the src object.

The getLoop() list position query returns the loop at the current position in the vertex loop list. The loop object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getLoop() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialised. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eNotInDatabase if the loop is missing. In the event of an error, the loop reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The getVertex() list owner query returns the vertex owner of the loop list. The vertex object is instantiated by the caller and passed by reference for getVertex() to set. Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged If the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. In the event of an error, the vertex reference object is unchanged and is thus likely to be uninitialized.

The setLoop() list position initializer is used to set this traverser's starting position to a specific loop in the vertex loop list, which resets the criteria for next() and done(). Returns eUninitialisedObject if this traverser object is uninitialized. Returns eBrepChanged if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the traverser was last set. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the loop reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the loop reference object was last set. Returns Acad::eWrongDatabase if the loop is not in the vertex loop list or is associated with a different AutoCAD object or revision. In the event of an error, this traverser's vertex loop list is unchanged.

The setVertex() list owner initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific vertex loop list, starting at the first loop in the list. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the vertex. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the vertex reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the vertex reference object was last set. Returns eDegenerateTopology if the vertex is not loop-bounded. In the event of an error, this traverser's vertex loop list is unchanged.

The setVertexAndLoop() list initializer is used to set this traverser to a specific vertex loop list and starting position. This initializes a traverser instantiated with the default constructor, and resets the criteria for the eBrepChanged error as well as the criteria for next() and done(). It also sets the validation level to match that of the loop-vertex. Returns Acad::eInvalidInput if the loop-vertex traverser reference object is uninitialized, or if the associated AutoCAD object has been modified since the loop-vertex traverser reference object was last set. In the event of an error, this traverser's vertex loop list is unchanged.

Line containment query. Returns the relation of an external line segment to the vertex (inside, outside, and so on). Deprecated in favor of AcBrEntity::getLineContainment().

Point instantiation. Returns the vertex's underlying point as an AcGe 3D point, with the entire chain of transforms from the object ID array applied. The point is passed as a null AcGePoint3d reference pointer for getPoint() to instantiate. Returns eInvalidObject if the object is uninitialized or invalidated (that is, empty). Returns eBrepChanged if the owning AutoCAD entity changed since the object's list owner was last set. As a side effect, the object is invalidated. Returns eMissingGeometry if the point geometry is missing. Returns eOutOfMemory if the AcGe point comes back null. Returns eWrongObjectType if any of the associated AutoCAD database objects from the chained transforms cannot be opened. In the event of an error, the point reference pointer is unchanged and thus likely points to a null object.
Point containment query. Returns the relation of an external point to the vertex (inside, outside, and so on). Deprecated in favor of AcBrEntity::getPointContainment().

AcCFile is derived from CFile, but unlike its base class, AcCFile also supports reading and writing of string data type. Whenever reading/writing of string data type is involved, conversion will take place to match input wide strings to the output format, and vice-versa. Please refer to setCharFormat() for more information on text file formats.

Constructs an AcCFile object from a file path. This constructor sets the new line expansion to false by default. Since AcCFile is derived from CFile, please refer to MSDN documentation on CFile class constructor for more information on the possible values for the nOpenFlags parameter.

Attachs a buffer, for performance. Clients can provide a buffer for output, in order to minimize the number of writes to the underlying file. This helps greatly when writing across a high latency network.
Detach the buffer. Returns true if successful.
Flushes the buffer. Returns true if successful.
Returns the character format of the file associated with this AcCFile object.

Used to determine if new line characters (n) should be expanded to carriage return-linefeed (rn) character pairs when writing the file. New line expansion is by default turned off for AcCFile object, new line characters will be treated as any other binary data when writing the file. However, the caller can choose to change this behavior by calling setExpandLF(). This method returns true if expansion of new line characters is turned on, or false otherwise.

Call this method to determine if writing of CIF strings is currently turned on. CIF string handling will only take effect when the file character format is set to AdCharFormatter::kAnsi. Its value has no effects when using other (Unicode) encoding formats. This method returns true if CIF string writing is currently turned on, or false otherwise.
Checks to see if the file has a buffer. Returns true if it does.
Reads data into a buffer from the file associated with the AcCFile object. Returns the number of bytes transferred to the buffer.

Call this method to read any existing byte order mark (BOM) from the beginning of the file associated with 'this' AcCFile object, and update the current file type. This method places the input file pointer after the BOM. The file must be opened with read permissions for this call to be successful. If a file type is previously set and the BOM is not found in the file, the file type is left unchanged. Returns true if the BOM is successfully read and the file type is set. It returns false if the BOM does not exist for the file or if there was an error during the call.

Sets the character format of the file associated with this AcCFile object. Valid character formats are: AdCharFormatter::kAnsi - ANSI character format AdCharFormatter::kUtf8 - UTF8 encoding format AdCharFormatter::kUtf16LE - UTF16 little endian encoding format AdCharFormatter::kUtf16BE - UTF16 big endian encoding format AdCharFormatter::kUtf32LE - UTF32 little endian encoding format AdCharFormatter::kUtf32BE - UTF32 big endian encoding format Returns the previous character format that was set to the file.

Enables/disables new line expansion. If this is enabled, every new line character (n) is expanded to a carriage return-linefeed (rn) character pair on file writing. New line expansion is by default turned off for AcCFile objects; new line characters will be treated as any other binary data when writing the file. Returns the previous state of the new line expansion flag.

Turns on/off CIF string writing for the file associated with the AcCFile object. CIF string handling will only take effect when the file character format is set to AdCharFormatter::kAnsi. Its value has no effects when using other (Unicode) encoding formats. Returns the previous state of CIF string writing flag (on/off).
Writes data from a buffer to the file associated with this AcCFile object. Write method throws an exception in response to several conditions, including the disk-full condition.

Call this method to write the byte order mark (BOM) to the beginning of the output file associated with this AcCFile object, based on the current file type. Returns true if the BOM is successfully written, or false otherwise. It returns false if the BOM does not get written to the file because of error conditions during the call.
