ACRX_X_CALL(a, b) When accessing protocol extension methods, you must use the x() or queryX() methods. The value returned back is a pointer to an AcRxObject, which must then be cast down to the appropriate protocol extension class. This may be written out in every use location, but in many cases the calling syntax can also be compressed into a macro. An example of the most common calling syntax in macro form is provided in the rxobject.h header file: #define ACRX_X_CALL(a,b) b::cast(a->x(b::desc())) This macro demonstrates the use of the x() method to access a protocol extension object. An example of this macro's use might be: double val = ACRX_X_CALL(pEnt, ProtExtClass)->func1(pEnt); a : Object pointer b : Protocol extension class

The AcStatusBarItem class represents an item in the status bar. The item can be a pane or a tray item. This class provides methods that support both both pane and tray item objects. For more information about pane objects, see AcPane. For more information about tray item objects, see AcTrayItem.

This function converts the client-area coordinates of the specified rectangle to screen coordinates. This function uses the status bar control window's client coordinates in the RECT structure or in the CRect object pointed to by lpRect to compute new screen coordinates. It then replaces the coordinates in the structure with the new coordinates. The new screen coordinates are relative to the upper-left corner of the system display.

If it is disabled, it does not respond to mouse-click events. The enabled state of the item is updated in the status bar on the next call to AcApStatusBar::Update().

This callback function is invoked when the user double-clicks the left mouse button on the pane or tray item, if the item is enabled to receive notifications. On the first left-mouse-down event, the OnLButtonDown() function is called. If the user presses the left mouse button again within the double-click time limit of the system, the OnLButtonDblClk() function is called. This function should be implemented so that it displays the default interface of the feature or service. This notification should be thought of as a combination select and open operation in which the resulting window hosts the main content for the feature or service. Valid nFlags values are as follows: Flag Meaning MK_CONTROL CTRL key is down MK_LBUTTON Left mouse button is down MK_MBUTTON Middle mouse button is down MK_RBUTTON Right mouse button is down MK_SHIFT SHIFT key is down

This callback function is invoked when the user clicks the left mouse button on the pane or tray item, if the item is enabled to receive notifications. This function should be implemented to do one of the following: Display the associated context menu (same behavior as OnRButtonDown)Display an interface of the feature or service such as a Properties dialog or HTML-based window with context-based optionsNothingValid nFlags values are as follows: Flag Meaning MK_CONTROL CTRL key is down MK_LBUTTON Left mouse button is down MK_MBUTTON Middle mouse button is down MK_RBUTTON Right mouse button is down MK_SHIFT SHIFT key is down

This callback function is invoked when the user clicks the right mouse button on the pane or tray item, if the item is enabled to receive notifications. This function should be implemented to display a context menu and responding to menu events. This can be done using the AcPane::DisplayContextMenu() function. Developers should provide support for the following context menu elements: Enabled and disabled statesNested menusSeparatorsCheckmarks to indicate an ON stateSame standard framework as all AutoCAD shortcut menusServices and features should provide their own settings interface for configuring service settings. No access to the AutoCAD Options dialog is provided for tray services and features. Service and feature designers should provide access to their feature's configuration settings by including a Settings' option preceded by a separator as the last item of their context menu.

This function reports whether the error is ignored by the application.
This function sets the acStIgnoreByApplication flag for this error.
This function reports whether the error is ignored by the user.
This function sets the acStIgnoreByUser flag for this error.
This function gets the plug-ins associated with this error.
This function gets the number of custom properties for this error.
This function gets the name of the property at the specified index in the error's custom property list.
This function gets the value of the specified custom property.

This function resets the error object for reuse.

The IAcStFix interface encapsulates a fix object. Fix objects are created by plug-ins. A fix object is associated with an error. An error object can have zero or more plug-in-supplied fixes. One of these fixes can be designated the recommended fix, which is used by the CheckStandards autofix feature. A fix object performs the following tasks: Provides a description of the associated error and the associated object ID of the database object.Maintains a status so the error can be skipped or ignored in additional checks.Provides a way of displaying and storing custom information in the Batch .chx file.
This function gets the object ID of the fix object.
This function gets the fix object name.
This function gets the number of custom properties for the fix object.
This function gets the name of the property at the specified index in the fix object's custom properties list.
This function gets the value of the specified custom property.
This function sets the value of the specified custom property.
This function resets the fix object for reuse.
This function gets the name of the error object associated with the fix object.
This function writes the fix to the specified XML node.
The IAcStManager2 interface is implemented as part of the Standards Framework and is for internal use only.

For internal use only. This function gets information about plug-ins that have a stamped DWS database. The arrays output by this function all have the same bounds. The elements at a particular index in one array correspond to the elements with the same index in another array. In other words, the elements at a particular index in the different arrays all describe the same plug-in.

For internal use only. This function retrieves the list of standard files used by the drawing. The function performs no validation of the retrieved DWS strings. If no DWS references are found, it sets filenameArray to null.

For internal use only. This function retrieves the aliases for an AutoCAD object. AutoCAD stores aliases defined by plug-ins in one or more tables. Each table is identifed by the string passed in szName. The meaning of an alias is not defined by the framework. This function allows plug-ins and host applications to store and retrieve information about objects.

For internal use only. This function retrieves information used to identify objects that have been marked 'ignored' by applications or users. The flags are one or more of the values in the AcStFlags enumeration.
Gets Model Space proxy for a database that can be used to iterate through its Model Space

For internal use only. This function creates an iterator for checking errors in a drawing. The iterator is created in the context of a set of plug-ins, DWS files, and a drawing to check, which are specified by the input parameters. This context is invariant over the lifetime of the iterator object. The arrays passed as input parameters are single-dimension arrays of the same length. Individual entries in these arrays can be null.
Gets Paper Space proxy for a database that can be used to iterate through its Paper Space

For internal use only. This function stores the list of standard files to use to check a drawing. The function performs no validation of the DWS strings passed. It replaces existing references in the drawing with the new references. If the input array is null, any existing references are removed from the drawing.

For internal use only. This function sets the aliases for an AutoCAD object. AutoCAD stores aliases defined by plug-ins in one or more tables. Each table is identifed by the string passed in szName. The meaning of an alias table is not defined by the framework. This function allows plug-ins and host applications to store and retrieve information on objects.

For internal use only. This function sets standards flags for an AutoCAD object. The flags are used to identify objects that have been marked ignored by applications or users. The flags are one or more of the values in the AcStFlags enumeration.

For internal use only. This function stamps a database with information about a plug-in, such as the name and version. The information is used to determine which plug-ins a DWS file needs to support it. The function instantiates each plug-in identified in pluginProgIdArray and calls the plug-in's IAcStPlugin::StampDatabase()function. If the pStampIt value returned by that call is true, this function embeds information about the plug-in.

The IAcStPlugin2 interface is implemented by a plug-in that participates in checking a drawing managed by an AcStErrorIterator2 object. The plug-in checks a drawing for errors against a set of rules defined and implemented by the plug-in, and reports errors by creating an error object that is passed to the plug-in by the Standards Framework. Optionally, the plug-in can implement code for fixing errors by creating a fix object. The plug-in also implements methods to provide information such as the plug-in version and author.
This function gets the name of the plug-in's author. This is typically a company name.
This function checks a system variable.
This function clears the plug-in state and releases any objects it has cached. It is called immediately before releasing a plug-in.
This function checks whether there are more errors in the drawing.
This function attempts to fix the specified error using the specified fix object. It takes an error object and replaces its properties with the same properties in a supplied fix object.
This function gets an array of fix objects for the specified error. The caller is responsible for releasing the objects in fixArray when they are no longer needed.
This function gets the current error.

This function gets the class names of the objects that the plug-in can check. Plug-ins use this to tell the framework which types of object they're interested in. The object types, as AcRxClass elements, are passed in the classNameArray array. The standards framework needs this information to filter out objects that are not relevant to a plug-in.
This function gets the names of the properties and fix objects for the specified error.
This function gets the recommended fix object for the specified error.
This function returns the URL from which the plug-in can be obtained.

This function returns a pointer to the plug-in's icon. Plug-in icons are 16 x 16 pixels. They are used in various UI presentations that list and describe plug-ins. Implementation of this fuction is optional. Plug-ins that implement it should load the icon using the LoadIcon() function and return the HICON from LoadIcon() to the caller in pVal.

This function initializes the plug-in. This is the only member function in which the interface is passed an IAcStManager interface. Plug-in implementations that need to use IAcStManager methods may want to cache this pointer in a class member. Otherwise, they will have to instantiate their own AcStManager objects when needed.
This function gets the name of the plug-in.
This function sets the error iterator to point to the next error in the current context.

This method sets the objects to examine when iterating over errors. The SetContext() method is called every time an object (or a list of them) is modified in an edit session, and the object type matches what your plug-in sent to the framework in GetObjectFilter(). The context can be an object list or null (which indicates that the entire drawing needs to be checked). Once the context is set, the framework calls Start(), Next(), and Done() to iterate through errors within the current context.
This method defines the context in which a plug-in will operate, specifically the drawing to check and the DWS files that should be used to check the drawing.
This function reports whether the plug-in uses the database to check the drawing.
This function initializes the error iterator mechanism for the specified error object.
This function updates the result status of the specified error.
This function gets the version of the plug-in.
This function creates a new AcStPluginInfo node below the specified node.

Returns a pointer to the internal character buffer of the string object, allowing direct access to and modification of the string contents. The returned buffer contains the entire string contents and is null terminated. The buffer is at least large enough to hold nMinBufferLength characters plus a null terminator. If nNumBufferLength is smaller than the length of the string, it is ignored and the entire string is available. If it is larger than string length, a larger buffer is allocated and you are able to modify that many characters and may grow the string. Clients should call releaseBuffer() when they're done accessing the buffer, and they should not call any other methods (except an implicit call to the dtor) before then. But it's okay if the string is destroyed without releaseBuffer() having been called.

This class represents a Symmetric constraint node in the owning AcDbAssoc2dConstraintGroup. It can be applied between two same type of constrained geometries (except spline).

Scoping container for tool and catalog framework enumerated types.
AcTcCatalog encapsulates the catalog item in the tool catalog.

AcTcCatalogItem is the base class for all catalog items. It encapsulates an item's common properties and behavior. This class is used to derive from and implement the following catalog items: ToolPackagePaletteCategoryCatalogStock Tool
This is the reactor base class for notification when a child is added to, deleted from, or detached from a catalog item. This class is meant to be derived from and cannot be instantiated.
Protected constructor. This class is meant to be derived from and cannot be instantiated.
This method is called by the catalog item when a child is added to the catalog item. Override this method to do special processing when a child is added.
This method is called by the catalog item when a child is deleted from the catalog item. Override this method to do special processing when a child is deleted.
This method is called by the catalog item when a child is deleted from the catalog item. Override this method to do special processing when a child is detached.
Enables or disables the reactor. If the reactor is disabled, it does not receive any notification. The reactor is enabled by default when it is created. Returns the previous state.
Returns a non-zero value if the reactor is currently enabled. Returns zero if the reactor is currently disabled.

Assigns the source item to this item by copying its members. Only the members of the source item are copied. The children of the source item are not copied. If this item has any children, they are not affected. To copy both this item and its children, use the Clone() function. This function uses the CopyFrom() virtual function to copy members. CopyFrom() should be overridden in all derived classes. Returns a reference to AcTcCatalogItem.
Protected constructor; for internal use only.

Appends pNewItem as the last child of this item. The child's type must be valid for this item. For example, only tools can be added as children for a palette. This function checks if the child's type is valid by calling the virtual IsValidChild() method and passing it the child item. If IsValidChild() returns true, the child is added. If it returns false, this function fails. The caller allocates the added item on the heap using new. Once the child item is added to its new parent, however, the parent assumes ownership of the child's memory. After this, the caller must not delete the pointer. The children will be deleted when the parent item is deleted. Returns the index of the added element.
Adds the reactor to the catalog item. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Adds a new target product to the target product list. The caller passes the target product's information in the ACTC_TARGET_PRODUCT_INFO structure pointed to by pProductInfo. The target product list is the list of products in which this item can be used. This list can be iterated by using the GetTargetProductCount() and GetTargetProduct() methods. If the function succeeds, the return value is the zero-based index of the target product list item.
This function checks whether an item can be refreshed. An item can be refreshed if it has source information. Returns non-zero if the item can be refreshed. Otherwise, returns zero.

Clones this item. If pClone is null, the clone is created on the heap. The item is cloned by copying its members. If bDeep is true, the item's children are cloned recursively. Otherwise, only the item itself is cloned. If bCopyId is true, the ID of this item is copied to the clone. Otherwise, a new ID is created for the clone. Because the base class implementation calls CreateObject() and CopyFrom() to clone the item and its children, derived classes do not need to implement the Clone() function. They need to implement only the CreateObject() and CopyFrom() functions. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Copies the members of source item pSrcItem to this item. Only the members of the source item are copied; its children are not copied. To copy both this item and its children, use the Clone() function. If this item has any children, they are not affected. This function should be overridden in derived classes. The derived class method should call the base class implementation first, to copy the base class members. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Creates a new item on the heap and returns a pointer to it. Derived classes should implement this function to create their own new object. This function is called by the Clone() function. If the function succeeds, the return value is a pointer to the newly created object on the heap. Otherwise, the return value is null.
Deletes all of this item's children and their descendants recursively. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Removes the specified child item from the list of children and deletes pItem. Do not use pItem after this call. To remove the child without deleting it, use the DetachChild() function. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

This function permanently deletes the image file referred to by this item. If bRecursive is true, image files belonging to the item's children are also deleted. If it is false, only the image file of this item is deleted. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

This function permanently deletes the link file if this item is a linked item. If bRecursive is true, this function also deletes the link files referenced by this item's children. Otherwise, it deletes only the link file of this item. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Permanently deletes the overlay image file of this item and, optionally, those of its children. If bRecursive is true, this function recursively deletes the overlay image files of this item's children. Otherwise, it deletes the overlay image file of this item only. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Deletes the target product whose index in the target product list is iIndex. iIndex is zero-based and may range from zero to one less than the number of target products. To find the number of target products, use the GetTargetProductCount() function. This function fails if there is no target product information, or if the index is invalid. If this function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If this function fails, the return value is zero.

Removes the specified child item from the list of children without deleting it. The detached child's parent member is set to null. After a successful call to this function, the detached child is no longer owned by this item. Therefore, the caller becomes responsible for deleting pItem. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Downloads a catalog item from the specified URL to a local directory and then loads the file into this item. The URL should point to the same type of catalog item represented by this object. For example, if this object's type is AcTcCatalog, the URL should point to a catalog file. Otherwise, this function fails. dwDownloadFlag can be one or more of the AcTc::DownloadOption enum values. If pszDownloadPath is null, the URL is downloaded to the temp directory. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Returns zero if the item could not be downloaded, or if there was an error while downloading the item.

Searches the children for an item by its name. The search is not case sensitive. Because duplicate names are allowed, this function returns the first item that matches the name. Returns the pointer to the catalog item found. Returns null if no item is found with the specified name.

Finds the catalog item contained in the specified XML file, then creates and returns an appropriate catalog item object. If the file does not contain a valid catalog item this method returns null. If bLoad is true, this method loads the file into the item after creating it. The caller is responsible for deleting the returned pointer. Currently, dwLoadOption can be set to the following AcTc::LoadOption enum value: kLoadLinks Load linked items also Returns a pointer to the newly created catalog item if the file contains a catalog item. Returns null if the file does not contain a catalog item or if the function failed.
Returns the access right for the item. The return value can be one or more AcTc::AccessRight enum values. Access rights are set with the SetAccessRight() function.
The function returns the auto refresh value. If auto refresh is set, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Returns the child at index iIndex. The returned pointer is owned by this item and should not be deleted by the caller. iIndex should be in the range of zero to the number of children minus one. Returns null if the index is out of bounds.
Gets the XML node which contains the item's custom data. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Gets file revision information for this item.

Gets the help information stored in the item. The pszFile buffer size should be at least ACTC_MAX_HELPINFO_FILE. The pszCommand buffer size should be at least ACTC_MAX_HELPINFO_COMMAND. The following commands are supported: HELP_HHWND_TOPIC pszFile points to an HTML file, a URL, or a compiled HTML Help (CHM) file. Display the topic in HTML Help window. pszData should contain the topic to display. HELP_HHWND_INDEX pszFile points to an HTML file, a URL, or a compiled HTML Help (CHM) file. Opens the HTML Help window and attempts to find the help item in the index. pszData should contain the help item. HELP_BROWSER_URL pszFile points to a URL which should be opened in a browser. The value of pszData depends on the command. See the pszCommand description for supported values. The pszData buffer size should be at least ACTC_MAX_HELPINFO_DATA. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Returns the ID of the item in pId. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Returns a pointer to an AcTcImage object. The object's width in pixels is specified by the SIZE::cx member of pSize. The height member of pSize is ignored. The returned pointer is owned by this object and should not be deleted. If an image of the specified size is not found, the image with the next larger size is returned. If a larger-sized image is not available, then the image with the next smaller size is returned. Returns null if no image is associated with the item.

Copies the local image file with absolute path of the image at the specified index to the buffer. If the image file in the item refers to a URL and the image file is not downloaded, it copies the URL. If the image file refers to a URL and the image file is downloaded locally, it copies the local image file path. iIndex may range from zero to the number of images minus one. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
Returns the image list associated with the item. Returns null if there is no image list associated with the item. The returned pointer is owned by this object and should not be deleted.

Copies the keywords of the item to the buffer. Keywords are separated by commas. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating NULL character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

If this item is a linked item, this function copies the URL of the link to pszString. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, it returns the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Gets the local file from which this item was loaded. If the item was loaded from a URL, the returned filename will point to the downloaded local file. If this item was not loaded from a file directly, then it tries to get the filename from its parents, checking the parent chain up to its root. For example, if a catalog is loaded from a file, this function returns the same filename whether it is called on the catalog object or any of its descendants. If none of the items in the parent chain was loaded from a file, the pszString output buffer returns empty. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the item name to pszString.If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Searches the child array for a child of type nType, beginning at index iIndex. If an item exists at the iIndex search starting position, that item is excluded from the search. nType can be one of the AcTc::CatalogItemType enum values. If successful, returns the pointer to the next matching child item. Returns null if there is no next child of the specified type.

This function loads the overlay image, by theme, if it is not already loaded. It returns NULL if there is no overlay image, or if the image cannot be loaded. The returned pointer is owned by this object and should not be deleted.

For local overlay images, this function copies the image file's absolute path to the buffer. If the overlay image file in the item refers to a URL and is not downloaded, this function copies the URL. If the overlay image file refers to a URL, and the file is downloaded locally, this function copies the local file path. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the text exceeds the character limit set by cbSize, it is truncated.
Returns information about the overlay image associated with the theme through pImageInfo. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Returns a pointer the parent of the item. Returns NULL if the item does not have a parent.

Copies the parent document name to pszString. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the parent document URL to the pszString buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the publisher country to the pszString buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the publisher's email address to the pszString buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the publisher name to the pszString buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the publisher's URL to the pszString buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Gets the reference path which is used to resolve the relative paths of image files and linked files while loading and saving the item. This path can be overridden using SetReferencePath(). If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string not including the terminating null character. If the text in pszString exceeds the length limit specified by cbSize, it is truncated. nFlag can be one of the AcTc::ReferencePath enum values. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
The function returns the refresh value. If refresh is enabled, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Gets the revision information for this item.
Returns a pointer to the root item if successful. Returns a pointer to this item if it is the root item.
Gets the scheme to which this catalog item belongs. Returns null if the catalog item does not belong to any scheme.

Gets the ID of the source catalog item from which this item can be refreshed. Returns false if there is no source information in the item. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Copies the URL of the source for this item to the buffer. The source URL refers to the original file (in the intranet, Internet, or local server) from which this item was downloaded. The source URL is used to refresh the item from its source. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Copies the XML tag name of the item to the buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Returns information about an entry in the target product list through the pProductInfo parameter. The target product list is the list of products in which this item can be used. This list can be iterated by using the GetTargetProductCount() method in conjunction with this method. iIndex should be in the range from zero to one less than the number of target products. If the function succeeds, it returns a non-zero value. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Returns the number of target products specified in the item, or zero if no target product is specified. The target product list is the list of products in which this item can be used. The list can be iterated by using the GetTargetProduct() method in conjunction with this method.

Gets the times of item creation, last modification, and last refresh. The caller should pass in NULL arguments for values which are not needed. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Copies the tool tip text for the item to the buffer. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Checks the root node of the specified XML file and returns the type of catalog item it contains. Return values are defined in the AcTc::CatalogItemType enumeration. Returns kItemUnknown if the file does not contain a catalog item.

Copies the item type as a string to pszString. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Gets the file or URL from which this item was loaded. If this item was not loaded from a file directly, or if this item is a child of an item which was loaded from a file or URL, then the pszString buffer will be empty. Use GetLocalFile() to get the local file from which this item or its parent was loaded. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string not including the terminating null character. If the text in pszString exceeds the length limit specified by cbSize, it is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.

Gets the XML representation of the item, including the item node and all its children. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. dwSaveOption can be one of the following AcTc::SaveOption enum values: kSaveLinksAsLinks, kSaveLinksAsEmbedded. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
Returns a non-zero value if the item has children. Otherwise, returns zero.

Inserts pNewItem as the child of this item at the index specified by iIndex. The child's type must be valid for this item. For example, only tools can be added as children for a palette. This function checks if the child's type is valid by calling the virtual IsValidChild() method and passing it the child item. If IsValidChild() returns true, the child is added. If it returns false, this function fails. The caller allocates the added item on the heap using new. Once the child item is added to its new parent, however, the parent assumes ownership of the child's memory. After this, the caller must not delete the pointer. The children will be deleted when the parent item is deleted. If iIndex is -1 or greater than the number of children, the child is added as the last child of the item. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

This function's return value indicates whether the item is a linked item. Linked items provide a reference to another XML file which contains the item. When a linked item is loaded via the Load() function with the kLoadLinks option specified, the item in the linked file is automatically loaded. Returns true if the item is a linked item, or false otherwise.

This function returns true if the item is a linked item, and if the linked file is currently loaded into this item. It returns false if the item is not a linked item, or if the linked file currently is not loaded into this item. Linked items provide a reference to another XML file which contains the item. When a linked item is loaded via the Load() function with the kLoadLinks option specified, the item in the linked file is automatically loaded.

An item is considered read only if one of the following conditions is satisfied: The access right of the item was set to kAccessRead or kAccessReadOnlyFile using SetAccessRight.The item can be refreshed, and refresh currently is enabled for the item. Returns TRUE if the item is read-only. Returns FALSE if the item is writeable.
Indicates whether this item is the root item. A root item is one that does not have a parent. Returns true if this item is a root item. Otherwise, returns false.
Indicates whether the user modified the item.

Derived classes implement this function to control which child types can be added to this item as children. The AddChild() and InsertChild() functions call this function to verify that an item is a valid type before adding it as a child. nType is one of the AcTc::CatalogItemType enum values. If the specified item type is a valid child of this item, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

This function returns a value that indicates whether this item can be used in the specified product. If this item has target product information, this function compares the specified product information to that of the item's target products. If a match is found, this function returns true. Otherwise, it returns false. If the item has no target product information, this function returns true. pszProductName can be the name returned by the AcDbHostApplicationServices::product() function. Passing an empty string to pszProductName causes this function to bypass product name validation. If pszProductName is specified, the item can be used only in the specified product. Otherwise, the item can be used if the product matches the other specified attributes. nMajorVersion can be determined from the value returned by the AcDbHostApplicationServices::versionString() function. Setting nMajorVersion to -1 bypasses product major version checking. nMinorVersion can be determined from the value returned by the AcDbHostApplicationServices::versionString() function. Setting nMinorVersion to -1 bypasses minor version checking. If nMajorVersion is -1, neither major nor minor version is checked. dwLocaleId can be the ID returned by the AcRxDynamicLinker::ProductLcid() function. dwLocaleId is used to restrict tools to specific language versions. Multiple identifiers may be specified using comma delimiters. Setting dwLocaleId to 0 bypasses locale id validation, which allows the tool to be used in all language versions.

This function loads the catalog item from an XML file. The item should be found in the XML structure's root, and the root item tag in the XML file should correspond to the item type. For example, if the item's type is Catalog, the root node's tag should be Catalog. Otherwise, the function fails. This function opens the XML file, gets the root node and calls Load(IUnknown* pUnknown, DWORD dwLoadOption = kLoadLinks), passing it the root node. pszUrl may specify a local or network file location or URL. dwLoadOption is one of the values specified in the AcTc::LoadOption enum. Any existing data in the item is discarded during a load operation. Relative paths of images and links are resolved in the following order: If the SetReferencePath() function has been used to set a reference path for this catalog item, that path is used to resolve relative paths. If no reference path is set in the catalog item, the path to the file from which the item is loaded or saved is used to resolve relative paths. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

If this catalog item is a linked item, this function loads the linked file into this item. If this item is not linked, this function fails. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Refreshes the item from its source. The item should have source information to refresh it, and the refresh option should not be disabled. Refresh fails if there is no source information or if refresh currently is disabled. This function refreshes the item by connecting to its source and downloading it. The source refers to a catalog item file in the intranet or Internet. The source file can contain this item directly in the root or in another item. For example, if this item is a tool, the source URL may point either directly to a tool file, or to a catalog file which contains the tool. This function downloads the source URL and searches the downloaded item for this item using the item's ID. If this item is found, this function refreshes it. dwRefreshFlag can be one or more of the AcTc::RefreshOption enum values. Returns non-zero if the item was refreshed successfully. Otherwise, returns zero.
Removes the reactor from the catalog item. Returns nonzero if the reactor is found and removed. Returns zero If the reactor is not found.
Resets the item by re-initializing its members to default values and deleting its children. If the function succeeds the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

This function saves the catalog item to the XML file specified by pszUrl. It opens the XML file, creates the root node, and calls the Save(IUnknown* pUnknown, DWORD dwSaveOption = kSaveLinksAsLinks) function, passing it the root node. pszUrl must specify a local or network file location. It cannot be a URL. dwSaveOption is one of the values specified in the AcTc::SaveOption enum. Relative paths of images and links are resolved in the following order: If the SetReferencePath() function has been used to set a reference path for this catalog item, that path is used to resolve relative paths. If no reference path is set in the catalog item, the path to the file from which the item is loaded or saved is used to resolve relative paths. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the access right of the item. nAccessRight can be one or more AcTc::AccessRight values. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
This function enables or disables the automatic refreshing of the item. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the URL of the help file to be used by the item. pszData can be null if pszCommand is set to HELP_BROWSER_URL. The following commands are supported: HELP_HHWND_TOPIC pszFile points to an HTML file, a URL, or a compiled HTML Help (CHM) file. Display the topic in HTML Help window. pszData should contain the topic to display. HELP_HHWND_INDEX pszFile points to an HTML file, a URL, or a compiled HTML Help (CHM) file. Opens the HTML Help window and attempts to find the help item in the index. pszData should contain the help item. HELP_BROWSER_URL pszFile points to a URL which should be opened in a browser. The value of pszData depends on the command. See the pszCommand description for supported values. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the ID of the item. ID should be a valid GUID. Otherwise the function fails. A zero GUID is not valid. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

This method rearranges the order of the items in the view. The order is stored in the user's profile file, which stores all of the UI settings for a user. The original order of the items in the catalog is not affected by this method. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the keywords of the item. Keywords are separated by commas. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the URL of the linked item. Setting a link URL automatically makes the item a linked item. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the name of the item to the value specified in pszString. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Creates a new ID and sets it in this item. If bRecursive is true, new IDs are assigned to the item's children. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the image option. Setting the image option will overwrite the current option. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.

This function sets the overlay image for the item. pImage may be null, in which case the overlay image is removed. If this function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Applies the information in pImageInfo to this object's overlay image. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets pParent as the parent of the item. Setting a parent item does not automatically add this item as a child to the parent. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the parent document name to the string pointed to by pszString. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the parent document URL to the string value pointed to by pszString. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the publisher country. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the publisher's email to the string value pointed to by pszString. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the publisher name to the string value pointed to by pszString. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the publisher's URL to the string value pointed to by pszString. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the reference path. This path is used to resolve the relative paths of image files and linked files while loading and saving the item. If no reference path is set, relative paths are resolved using the path of the file from which the item is loaded/saved. Use this method to override this default path. nFlag can be one of the AcTc::ReferencePath enum values. If the function succeeds the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
The function sets the refresh value. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the ID of the source catalog item from which this item can be refreshed. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the URL of the source for this item. The source URL refers to the original file (in the intranet, Internet, or on a local server) from which this item was downloaded. The source URL is used to refresh the item from its source. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the times of item creation, last modification, and last refresh. The caller should pass NULL arguments for values which are to be left unchanged. If the function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the tool tip text for the item. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sorts the children of this item. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

This class stores and manages a collection of catalogs. The catalogs are loaded from a semicolon-delimited list of paths set in the catalog set. This class cannot be instantiated by external applications. A pointer to this class can be obtained by using AcTcScheme::GetCatalogSet().
Protected constructor. This class cannot be instantiated by external applications. Use AcTcScheme::GetCatalogSet() to get a pointer to this class.
Adds the specified catalog to the list of catalogs. Returns the index of the added catalog if successful. Returns -1 if the function fails.
Searches the catalog set for an item ID. Returns the pointer to the catalog item with the specified ID, or null if there is no catalog item with that ID.
Gets the catalog at the specified index. Returns a pointer to the catalog at the specified index, or null if the index is out of range.
Gets the number of catalogs in the catalog set.

Gets the absolute paths where the product's workspace catalog files are stored. This list can contain multiple paths separated by semicolons. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.
Gets the scheme to which this catalog set belongs. Returns a pointer to the scheme, or null if the catalog set does not belong to any scheme.
Inserts the specified catalog in the list of catalogs at the specified index. Returns the index of the added catalog if successful, or -1 if the function fails.

Loads the catalogs from the paths set in the catalog set. Before calling this function, the catalog paths should be set using SetCatalogPath(). If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Removes and returns the catalog at the specified index. Returns the removed catalog, or null if the index is out of range.
Saves the catalogs in the catalog set. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the catalog path. The specified string can contain multiple paths separated by semicolons. LoadCatalogs() should be called to load the catalogs from this new path. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Unloads the catalogs in the catalog set. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
This is AcTcCatalog, a member of class AcTcCatalog.
AcTcCategory encapsulates the category item in the tool catalog.
This is AcTcCategory, a member of class AcTcCategory.

This function is used to download multiple URLs in a single call. It creates a catalog item object for each downloaded URL and stores the objects in the pItems array. pUrls is an input array of size nNumUrls. pItems is an output array of size nNumUrls. The pointers in pItems are allocated on the heap using new. It is the caller's responsibility to delete these pointers after using them. The elements of the pItems array correspond to the elements of pUrls. If a URL cannot be downloaded, the corresponding index in the pItems array is NULL. If pszDownloadPath is null, the URL is downloaded to the temp directory. dwItemTypes can be either one or more of the AcTc::CatalogItemType enum values, or -1. If it is -1, all item types are downloaded. Returns the number of URLs successfully loaded.
Returns the singleton AcTcManager object, or null if the AcTc library is not initialized.
AcTcImage provides functionality for loading, saving, and rendering BMP, JPG, GIF, and PNG files. The image data can be loaded and saved to a file or to an IStream object.

AcTcImageList is used to manage the images associated with a catalog item. Multiple images with different sizes can be associated with a catalog item. Images of closely matching size are used for rendering the image. The constructor of this class is protected, so it cannot be created. The pointer to this object can be obtained using AcTcCatalogItem::GetImageList().
Protected constructor; for internal use only.
Makes a copy of the image information and appends it to the image list. The function returns the zero-based index of the new image if successful, and returns -1 if it fails.
Deletes the image at the specified index. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Deletes all of the images in the image list. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Get the image to be used by the Specify Image dialog.
Retrieves the image at the index. Use the light theme by default, but override with a dark theme if possible.

If bExactMatch is FALSE, and if the image with the same size is not found, then the index of the image with the next highest size is returned. If the next highest size is not available, then the index of the image with the next lowest size is returned. For example, an image list has the following sized images: 16X16, 24X24, 32X32, and 64X64. If the index requested is for an image with a width of 30, then because the image with width 30 is not in the image list, the index of the image with the next highest width, 32X32, is returned. If the index of an image with a width of 128 is requested, then because the next highest width is not available, the index of the image with the next lowest width, 64X64, is returned. If the image list has multiple images of the same size, then the index of the first image with the size is returned.
Retrieve the image information for the item at the given index and theme. By default, this routine will return the light themed image.
Loads the image at the specified index if it is not already loaded.
This function replaces an image with a new one at the specified index and, if desired, mark for the dark theme.. The function fails if an invalid index is passed.

This function copies the information that is passed to the corresponding image at the specified index. Default is for light theme. The pImageInfo value is a pointer to an ACTC_IMAGE_INFO structure containing the information that needs to be set at the specified index.
Sets the image option. Setting the image option will overwrite the current option. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.
Updates the image and marks whether it is used for the dark theme or not.
Reinitializes an existing AcTcImage object with new Image data from the specified source object.

Converts the image to a different type. If the current image is a bitmap then the image is converted to a transparent or opaque image depending on bTransparent. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.
Gets the image as bitmap. The returned bitmap is a copy and the caller should delete the bitmap after use. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.
Gets the image as icon. The returned icon is a copy and the caller should delete the icon after use. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.

Gets the default image type to which the image will be saved. The image will be saved in this format if the Save() method is called without an image type. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.
Gets the width and height of the image; fails if the image has not been loaded. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
This function returns the image type value as an AcTc::ImageType enum. If the Image is not loaded the function returns the kImageTypeUninitialized value.
Indicates whether the image is marked for use with the dark theme.
Returns TRUE if the image is currently loaded. The function fails if the Image has not been successfully loaded.

This function will fail if the file is not found or if the file contains an unsupported image. The image has to be loaded successfully before making any calls to other member functions of the class. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

This function is used to render the loaded image. The image must be loaded before it can be rendered. The function fails if the handle to the device context is NULL, or if the image is not loaded. Styles ACTC_IMAGE_NORMAL and ACTC_IMAGE_SELECTED are mutually exclusive and cannot be combined. If they are combined, selection takes the precedence. ACTC_IMAGE_HALO and ACTC_IMAGE_SHADOW can be used in combination with the other styles. The nStyle value can be one or more of the following values: ACTC_IMAGE_NORMAL Rendered as is ACTC_IMAGE_SELECTED Image is drawn, blending 50 percent with the system highlight color, which is useful for showing the image in the selection state ACTC_IMAGE_HALO A halo is drawn around the image ACTC_IMAGE_SHADOW A drop shadow for the image is drawn If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Saves the image as specified image type. The current image may have been loaded from any image type. Returns TRUE if successful. Otherwise returns FALSE.
Marks this image as being created for dark display theme.

Sets the default image type to which the image will be saved. The image will be saved in this format if the Save() method is called without an image type. Returns true if successful. Otherwise returns false.

Initializes the AcTc library. This function should be called before using any of the functions of the AcTc library. Returns nonzero if the library was initialized successfully. Returns zero if the library initialization failed.

AcTcManager, the tool manager, contains and manages stock tool and workspace catalogs. Stock tools are stored in stock tool files (as either one stock tool per file or multiple stock tools in a catalog file). Stock tool files are stored in the stock tool catalog directory. Workspace catalogs are stored as catalog files in the workspace catalogs directory. At startup, the tool manager reads the stock tool files and loads the stock tools found in them. Then it loads the workspace catalogs from the workspace catalogs directory.
Adds the specified catalog to the list of workspace catalogs and returns the index of the added element. The function returns the index of the added element if successful, and returns -1 if it fails.

Adds the specified scheme to the manager. The scheme object is not owned by the manager and so won't be deleted by the manager. The caller is responsible for removing the scheme from the manager and deleting it. The scheme object should not be deleted by the caller until it is removed from the manager. Returns the index of the added scheme object, or -1 if it fails.
Adds the specified stock tool to the list of stock tool catalogs. The function returns the index of the added element if successful, and returns -1 if it fails.

Returns the pointer to the catalog item with the specified ID in the workspace catalogs. The function searches for the item only in the workspace catalogs. NULL is returned if there is no catalog item with the specified ID.
Returns the pointer to stock tool with the specified ID, and returns NULL if there is no stock tool with the specified ID.

Returns the pointer to the workspace catalog at the specified index. The index should be in the range of zero to one less than the number of workspace catalogs. You can get the number of workspace catalogs using the method GetCatalogCount. NULL is returned if the function fails.
Returns the number of workspace catalogs. This is equal to the number of catalog files successfully read from the workspace catalogs directory, as each file is considered as one catalog.

Returns the absolute paths where the product's workspace catalog files are stored. This can contain multiple paths separated by semicolons. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.
Finds the scheme using the specified scheme name. Returns the scheme object if it exists, or null if the specified scheme is not found.
Gets the number of schemes currently in the manager.

Returns the singleton shape catalog, which contains the shape packages. The returned catalog can be modified by adding or removing items. However, the modifications are not written to the shape catalog file automatically. To save changes, you must save the catalog explicitly by calling the SaveCatalogs() function with the enumerator kShapeCatalog.

Copies the shape catalog file name and path to the buffer. If pszFile is null, this function returns the length (in characters) of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the text length exceeds the limit defined by cbSize, it is truncated. If this function succeeds, the return value is the length (in characters) of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
Returns the shape package stored in the shape catalog whose name matches lpszName. If lpszName is null, this function returns the default shape package.

Returns the stock tool catalog at the specified index. The index should be in the range of zero to one less than the number of stock tool catalogs. You can get the number of stock tool catalogs using the method GetStockToolCatalogCount. The returned catalog item pointer may point to a stock tool, or to any container item (for example, catalog, or category) that contains stock tools. The function returns the stock tool catalog if successful, and NULL if the function fails.
Returns the number of stock tool catalogs. This is equal to the number of files successfully read from the stock tool catalogs directory, as each file is considered as one catalog.

Returns the absolute path of the location where the product's stock tool catalog files are stored. This can contain multiple paths separated by a semicolon. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
Inserts the stock tool catalog item pointed to by pCatalog at position nIndex. If nIndex is set to -1, the catalog is added after the last item. Returns the index of the inserted catalog.

Loads the workspace catalogs and stock tool catalogs. The currently loaded catalogs are discarded. The dwCatalogType value can be one or both of the following AcTc::CatalogType values: kCatalog Loads the catalogs kStockToolCatalog Loads the stock tool catalogs The dwLoadOption value can be one or both of the following AcTc::LoadOption values: kLoadLinks Loads the linked items kLoadImages Loads images while loading the item If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Removes the specified scheme from the manager. If the scheme is removed successfully, the return value is non-zero. Returns zero if the scheme was not found in the manager.

Removes the stock tool catalog at position nIndex. This function does not delete the stock tool catalog. The caller is responsible for deleting the catalog. Returns the pointer to the stock tool catalog that was removed.

Saves the workspace catalogs and stock tool catalogs. The dwCatalogType value can be one or both of the following AcTc::CatalogType values: kCatalog Saves the catalogs kStockToolCatalog Saves the stock tool catalogs kShapeCatalog Saves the shape catalog The dwLoadOption value can be one of the following AcTc::SaveOption values: kSaveLinksAsLinks Saves linked items into own linked files, preserving links. The linked items are not saved if kSaveLinksAsLinks or kSaveLinksAsEmbedded is not specified. kSaveLinksAsEmbedded Embeds all the linked items in this item and saves them into the specified file. The linked items become embedded items. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the workspace catalog path. This can contain multiple paths separated by semicolons. LoadCatalogs should be called to load the catalogs from this new path. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the shape catalog file. If the shape catalog is already loaded, this will reload the catalog from the new file. If this function succeeds,the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the stock tool catalog path. This can contain multiple paths, separated by semicolons. LoadCatalogs should be called to load the catalogs from this new path. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Unloads the workspace catalogs and stock tool catalogs. The dwCatalogType value can be one or both of the following AcTc::CatalogType values: kCatalog Unloads the catalogs kStockToolCatalog Unloads the stock tool catalogs If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
AcTcPackage encapsulates the package item in the tool catalog.
This is AcTcPackage, a member of class AcTcPackage.
AcTcPalette encapsulates the palette item in the tool catalog.
This is AcTcPalette, a member of class AcTcPalette.

This function refreshes each item in the pItems array to match the item's source. For an item to be refreshed, it must have source information, and refresh must not be currently disabled. If either of these conditions is not met, refresh fails. To refresh items, this function connects to each item's source and downloads it. The source refers to a catalog item file in either the intranet or Internet. The source file can contain the item to be refreshed directly in the root or in another item. For example, if the item to be refreshed is a tool, the source URL may point directly to a tool file or a catalog file that contains the tool. It downloads the source URL and searches the downloaded item for the item to be refreshed using the item's ID. If the item is found, the function refreshes the item. Returns nonzero if all items were refreshed successfully, or zero if refresh failed for one or more items.

This class is used to store and manage a tool palette scheme. A scheme is a collection of the following types of catalogs: Tool catalogsStock tool catalogsShape catalogs These catalogs can be loaded from catalog files that are located in multiple paths.
Searches the specified catalogs for an item ID. Returns the pointer to the catalog item with the specified ID, or null if there is no catalog item with that ID.
Gets the catalog set for the specified catalog type. Returns a pointer to a catalog set containing catalogs of the specified type, or null if the catalog type is invalid.

Copies the scheme name to pszString. If pszString is null, it returns the length, in characters, of the string, not including the terminating null character. If the string's length exceeds cbSize, the returned string is truncated. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, not including the terminating null character.
Loads the specified catalogs. The currently loaded catalogs are discarded. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Saves the specified catalogs. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the name of the scheme to the value specified in pszString. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Unloads the specified catalogs. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sorts an array of catalog items and stores the sorted items in the same array. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

AcTcStockTool represents a registered stock tool. Stock tool information is stored in a stock tool file. AcTcStockTool encapsulates the stock tool information read from the file and provides methods to manage the information.
This is AcTcStockTool, a member of class AcTcStockTool.
Creates the COM object that implements the IAcadStockTool interface. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Creates the COM object which implements the IAcadTool interface. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Creates the tool object. The returned pointer is allocated in the heap and should be deleted after use. If the function succeeds, the return value is the newly created AcTcTool pointer. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

Returns the class ID of the COM class that implements the stock tool by implementing the IAcadStockTool interface. This class ID can be used to create the COM object and get the IAcadStockTool interface. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Gets the file name (with the relative or full path) of the DLL that contains the COM object implementing the stock tool. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.

Gets the command line options of msiexec.exe that are used during the installation of the stock tool MSI file. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.

Gets the URL of the MSI file that installs the stocktool binary. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.

Sets the class ID of the COM class that implements the stock tool by implementing the IAcadStockTool interface. This class ID is used to create the COM object and get the IAcadStockTool interface. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the file name (with the relative or full path) of the DLL that contains the COM object implementing the stock tool. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the commandline options of msiexec.exe that are used during the installation of the stock tool MSI file. Do not specify the /i and /p flags in the arguments, because these flags are added by the application, depending on the extension of the URL. For MSP files, the application adds the /p flag; for MSI files, the application adds the /i flag. The application uses the module install URL and arguments for stock tool installation as in the following example: Msiexec.exe /i <url> <Arguments>Msiexec.exe /i http://pointa.autodesk.com/tools.msi /l* msi.logMsiexec.exe /p http://pointa.autodesk.com/tools.msp /l* msi.logIf the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the URL of the stock tool binary that contains the MSI file for installing the stock tool. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
AcTcTool encapsulates the tool item in the tool catalog.
Copy constructor. Only the members of the source item are copied. The children of the source item are not copied. To copy both this item and its children, use the Clone() function.

Creates the COM object that implements IAcadTool and stores its IUnknown in ppTool, and if bLoadData is true, loads the tool's data. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Enables or disables a flyout tool. Set bUseFlyout to true to enable the flyout, or false to disable it. This method should be used only for flyout tools. If the tool is not a flyout tool, this function fails. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Executes the tool, by creating the COM object that implements the IAcadTool interface and calling IAcadTool::Execute. nFlag can be one of the following ExecutionContext values: kLButtonClicked Left mouse was clicked to execute the tool kDroppedInDrawing Tool was dropped in the drawing If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Stores the shape tools that are currently visible in the shape palette in the array. These tools are pointers to the tools in the shape package associated with the tool. The pointers in the array should not be deleted. You can pass null for the first argument to get the number of active shapes to allocate the array. When this function is called, nNumItems should be set to the number of items that can be copied. Upon return, nNumItems holds the actual number of items copied to the array. If pItems is null, this function stores the number of active shapes in nNumItems and returns true. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Returns the shape package associated with the flyout tool. The returned shape package contains all the shape tools regardless of whether they are visible in the shape palette. The returned pointer should not be deleted by the caller. Use the GetActiveShapes() function to get the list of shapes that are visible in the shape palette. If the function succeeds, the return value is the pointer to the shape package associated with the tool. Returns null if this tool is not a flyout tool, or if no shape package is associated with it.
Returns the AcTcStockTool pointer associated with the tool, and returns NULL if the stock tool is not found.

Copies the stock tool file URL for downloading the stock tool file. If the function succeeds, the return value is the length, in characters, of the copied string, excluding the terminating null character.
Gets the ID of the stock tool associated to the tool. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Gets the XML node that contains the tool's custom data. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Returns the tool type. See the SetToolType() function documentation for information on tool types.
Returns true if the flyout tool is enabled. Returns false if the flyout tool is not enabled, or if the tool is not a flyout tool.

Sets the shapes that are visible in the shape palette. This function fails if the tool is not a flyout tool, if no shape package is associated with the tool, if the pItems array is empty, or if the pItems array contains items that do not exist in the shape palette associated with the tool. The pointers in pItems should point to the tools in the shape package currently associated with the flyout tool. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the current shape in the flyout tool. A tool whose ID is id should exist in the shape package associated with the tool. This function fails if the tool is not a flyout tool, if no shape package is associated with the tool, or if the specified tool does not exist in the shape palette associated with the tool. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the shape package associated with the tool. The shape package is typically obtained from the shape catalog using AcTcManager::GetShapeCatalog(). The specified shape package should exist in the shape catalog. If this tool is not a flyout tool, setting its shape package makes it a flyout tool.
Sets the stock tool file URL for downloading the stock tool file. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the ID of the stock tool associated with the tool. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the tool type. If the new tool type is kToolFlyout and no shape package is set in the tool, it sets the default shape package. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Copies the items in the array to the data source object in the format CF_ACTC_CATALOG_ITEM. Use AcTcUiPasteItems() to load the items from a data object. Returns true if the items were copied successfully; otherwise, returns false.

Displays a dialog to filter shapes. The caller uses the pActiveShapes input/output array parameter to pass in the shapes that are currently visible. After the dialog is dismissed, pActiveShapes outputs an array containing only the filtered active shapes. Returns true if the shapes were filtered successfully using the dialog.
