Handles the ON_BN_CLICKED Windows message for the path and file name radio button that is displayed when a field with a file name is selected.
Handles the ON_BN_CLICKED Windows message for the Path only radio button that is displayed when a field with a file name is selected.
Handles the ON_BN_CLICKED Windows message for the Point X check box that is displayed when a field with a point value is selected.
Handles the ON_BN_CLICKED Windows message for the Point Y check box that is displayed when a field with a point value is selected.
Handles the ON_BN_CLICKED Windows message for the Point Z check box that is displayed when a field with a point value is selected.
Called after the dialog is removed from the screen.
Handles the ON_EN_CHANGE Windows message for the preview edit control.
Handles the ON_LBN_SELCHANGE Windows message for the format list box control.
Sets the current format by selecting the format in the formats list. Returns the index of the selected format. Returns -1 if the format is not found.
Sets the style of this dialog.
Sets the text for the label of the format preview edit box. Returns true if successful or false if the function fails.

Makes the format preview edit box in the format dialog read-only or editable. By default this edit box is editable for date formats and read-only for string and other formats. Returns true if successful or false if the function fails.
Sets the display text and preview value. Returns true if successful.

Sets the field format type. It can be one of the standard format types supported by the format list. Standard format types are Date and String. Returns true if successful or false if the function fails.
This class implements a standard format list box.
Returns the index of the selected format. Returns -1 if no format is selected.
Returns the field format type. It can be one of the standard format types supported by the format list.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_DESTROY. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The method is called when the window associated with the control is destroyed. The default handler calls SetComboBox(), passing NULL, and invokes the inherited OnDestroy() handler.
Fills the formats list box with the available formats for the current format type. Returns true if successful or false if the function fails.
Sets the current format by selecting the format in the formats list. Returns the index of the selected format. Returns -1 if format is not found.

Sets the field format type. It can be one of the standard format types supported by the format list. Standard format types are Date and String. Returns true if successful or false if the function fails.
Sets persistency, which indicates whether selection information is saved to the registry.
Sets the root key under which persistency information will be saved in the registry.

This class provides the ability to generate and display thumbnails of gradient configurations, as seen on the Gradient tab of the AutoCAD Hatch dialog. This is a pure virtual interface. The developer acquires a pointer to the underlying implementation object by calling the global function createGradientThumbnailEngine(). When finished with the thumbnail engine, the developer should delete the pointer. The process of creating the thumbnails involves the following steps: Create the gradient thumbnail engine.Set the desired gradient hatch parameters such as colors and angle.Render the thumbnails.Draw each of the nine thumbnails into a Windows device context.Make any changes to the gradient parameter; render and display the thumbnails as often as desired.When finished generating thumbnails, destroy the gradient thumbnail engine.

Draws one of the nine gradient thumbnails, (0-8), into the HDC at offset [xPos, yPos]. Each thumbnail is 55x55 pixels in size. Returns Acad::eOk if successful or Acad::eNullHandle if no thumbnail engine exists.
Renders the gradient thumbnails according to the parameters set with other member functions.
Sets the angle applied to the thumbnails when rendered. Returns Acad::eOk if successful or Acad::eNullHandle if no thumbnail engine exists.
Sets the 'shifted' value applied to the thumbnails when rendered. Returns Acad::eOk if successful or Acad::eNullHandle if no thumbnail engine exists.

Gradients involve a transition from a start color to a stop color. This function sets the start color value applied to the thumbnails when rendered. Returns Acad::eOk if successful or Acad::eNullHandle if no thumbnail engine exists.

Gradients involve a transition from a start color to a stop color. This function sets the stop color value applied to the thumbnails when rendered. Returns Acad::eOk if successful or Acad::eNullHandle if no thumbnail engine exists.

Use an instance of this class to switch between default and module's resources. When the object is constructed, a new resource provider will be switched in. Upon destruction the original resource provider will be restored. For example: void MyFunc() { CAcModuleResourceOverride myResources; . . }Upon entry to this function, the module's resources will be selected. When the function returns, the default resources will be restored. A resource override can be used in any of three ways: Use the default constructor (no arguments) to switch to the module's resources. The default resources will be restored by the destructor. The module/default resources are those maintained by the DLL's CAcExtensionModule.Pass NULL (or 0) to the constructor. The DLL's resources will be selected and the resources that were in effect will be restored when the override object is destroyed.Pass a non-NULL handle to the constructor. The associated module's resources will be selected and the resources that were in effect will be restored when the override object is destroyed.
Constructs a CAcModuleResourceOverride object. Calls acDocManager->pushResourceHandle() with the input resource instance.
This is the class destructor. It restores the resource handle saved in the constructor by calling acDocManager->popResourceHandle().

CAcTcUiCatalogView is used to display the child items of a catalog item. The CAcTcUiCatalogView is associated with a catalog item whose children are displayed in the view. Each child item displayed in the view is encapsulated by a CAcTcUiCatalogViewItem object.

CAcTcUiCatalogViewItem is used to encapsulate the items displayed in CAcTcUiCatalogView. Each CAcTcUiCatalogViewItem is associated to a catalog item object AcTcCatalogItem. It reads the catalog item's image and text and renders it in the view. This object cannot be created; the catalog view creates and maintains this object.
Returns the catalog item associated with the item. Returns NULL if there is no catalog item associated with this item.
Retrieves the application-supplied double word value associated with the specified item. The double word value was the dwData parameter of a SetData() call.
Returns the upper-left corner of the item's position in client coordinates of the view. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Gets the bounding rectangle of the item in client coordinates of the view. nCode can be one or more of the following values: ACTCUI_CVIR_BOUNDS Gets the bounding rectangle of the entire item which includes the image, flyout trigger, label, spacing, and border. If text is not displayed currently text and spacing are not included in the rectangle. ACTCUI_CVIR_IMAGE Gets the bounding rectangle of the image with border. ACTCUI_CVIR_LABEL Gets the bounding rectangle of the item text. If text is not displayed currently, the rectangle has zero height. ACTCUI_CVIR_USEFULLLABEL This flag can be specified with ACTCUI_CVIR_BOUNDS or ACTCUI_CVIR_LABEL. If it is specified the size calculated is to display the full text rather than elided two line text. ACTCUI_CVIR_TRIGGER Gets the bounding rectangle of the item's trigger if the item's style is ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_FLYOUT. The rectangle will be empty if the item does not use this style. ACTCUI_CVIR_WORLDRECT Returns the rectangle in world coordinates instead of client coordinates. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Returns the current state of the item. See SetState() for the state values.

Returns the item's style. The style flag can contain the following bit flags: ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_SHOWTEXT Show text ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_RIGHTTEXT Display text on the right side of the image (for list view) ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_FLYOUT Display the item with a flyout trigger ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_FULLROW Display the item in full row ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_HIDEIMAGE Hide the item's image ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_TEXT Text item ACTCUI_CVISTYLE_SEPARATOR Separator item
Draws or removes the halo around the image border. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Highlights or de-highlights the item. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Renders the image on the specified device context. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Selects or de-selects the item. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Sets the catalog item associated to the item. If the pointer set in the view item is deleted, the view should be updated immediately by calling CAcTcCatalogView::Update(). Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Sets the 32-bit application specific value associated with the item. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Sets the state of the item. It can be a combination of one or more of the following bit values: ACTCUI_CVISTATE_HIGHLIGHTED Item is highlighted ACTCUI_CVISTATE_SELECTED Item is selected ACTCUI_CVISTATE_HALO Item is rendered with a halo around it ACTCUI_CVISTATE_FOCUSED Item has the current focus Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Derived classes can override this method to customize the context menu that is displayed by right-clicking on the view. The right-click can be on an item or on the background. The passed menu is pre-filled with standard options. Derived classes can add new options or remove standard options. See HitTest() for the hit flag values. Return true to display the customized context menu and false to suppress the context menu.
This is CAcTcUiCatalogView, a member of class CAcTcUiCatalogView.

This function is called by the catalog view to determine if the Clipboard contains data for pasting in the view. For example, this will be called to enable and disable the Paste option on the context menu. Returns true if the data object contains data for pasting into the view, or false if the data object does not contain data that can be pasted.

This function is called by the catalog view when the items are copied to the Clipboard. It provides an opportunity for derived classes to copy the item's data to the Clipboard. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Creates the catalog view window. The catalog view style (dwCatalogViewStyle argument) can be one or more of the following: ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_SELECTION Disallow selection of items. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_VIEW_BUTTON Don't display view button. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_FLYOUT Display flyout tools as normal tools (without flyout trigger). ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_SCROLLBAR Don't display scrollbar. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_TOOLTIPS Display tool tips for the items. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_MULTISELECT Allow multiple selection of items. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_EDITLABELS Enable in-place editing of item names. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_HOVERSELECT Enable hover selection. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_SHOWTEXT Show text. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_LISTVIEW List view. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_DRAGDROP Disallow drag and drop. Items cannot be dragged from the view and objects cannot be dropped in the view. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_CUT Disallow cut operation. Items cannot be cut from the view. Cut option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_COPY Disallow copy operation. Items cannot be copied to clipboard. Copy option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_PASTE Disallow paste operation. Items cannot be pasted from clipboard. Paste option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_REFRESH Disallow refresh operation. Items cannot be refreshed. Refresh option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_REMOVE Disallow remove operation. Items cannot be removed. Remove option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_RENAME Disallow rename operation. Items cannot be renamed. Rename option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_PROPERTIES Disallow properties operation. Properties option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_HELP Disallow help operation. Help cannot be invoked. Help option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_VIEWOPTIONS Disallow view operation. View options cannot be changed. View option is removed from the context menu. ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_NO_OPERATIONS Disallow all the above operations. Returns true if the view window is created successfully, or false if the view window could not be created.

Called by the base class if it does not recognize the dragged object. Override this function in the derived classes to handle drag and drop of objects not recognized by the base class. The default implementation returns DROPEFFECT_NONE. Returns the effect that would result if a drop were attempted at the location specified. It can be one or more of the following: DROPEFFECT_NONE A drop would not be allowed DROPEFFECT_COPY A copy operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_MOVE A move operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_LINK A link from the dropped data to the original data would be established DROPEFFECT_SCROLL A drag scroll operation is about to occur or is occurring in the target

Called by the base class if it does not recognize the dragged object (in DragEnter() and DragOver()). Override this function in derived classes to handle drag and drop of objects not recognized by the base class.

Called by the base class if it does not recognize the dragged object. Override this function in derived classes to handle drag and drop of objects not recognized by the base class. The default implementation returns DROPEFFECT_NONE. Returns the effect that would result if a drop were attempted at the location specified by point. It can be one or more of the following: DROPEFFECT_NONE A drop would not be allowed DROPEFFECT_COPY A copy operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_MOVE A move operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_LINK A link from the dropped data to the original data would be established DROPEFFECT_SCROLL A drag scroll operation is about to occur or is occurring in the target

Called by the base class if it does not recognize the dragged object. Override this function in derived classes to handle drag and drop of objects not recognized by the base class. The default implementation returns DROPEFFECT_NONE. Returns the drop effect that resulted from the drop attempt. It can be one or more of the following: DROPEFFECT_NONE A drop would not be allowed DROPEFFECT_COPY A copy operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_MOVE A move operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_LINK A link from the dropped data to the original data would be established

Called by the base class if the dragged object is not recognized by the base class. Override this function in derived classes to handle drag and drop of objects not recognized by the base class. The default implementation returns DROPEFFECT_NONE. Returns the drop effect that resulted from the drop attempt. It can be one or more of the following: DROPEFFECT_NONE A drop would not be allowed DROPEFFECT_COPY A copy operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_MOVE A move operation would be performed DROPEFFECT_LINK A link from the dropped data to the original data would be established

Starts in-place editing of the item name if the catalog view has the ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_EDITLABELS style. If the view does not have this style set, the function fails. If the function succeeds, the return value is a pointer to the CEdit object being used to edit the item text. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

Ends the in-place editing of the item name. If bCancel is false and the validation fails when it tries to end the editing, this function returns false and the editing is not ended. Returns true if label editing was ended successfully. Returns false if label editing is not in progress currently or if label editing could not be ended.

Call this function to ensure that an item is partially or fully visible. The view is scrolled if necessary. If the bPartialOK parameter is nonzero, no scrolling occurs if the item is partially visible. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Returns the pointer to the catalog item whose children are displayed in the catalog view. Returns null if there is no catalog item set currently.
Returns the catalog view style. See Create() for a list of possible catalog view styles.
Returns the number of columns that can fit in the view area of the catalog view. All the columns are always fully visible.
Returns the current item, which is the item in the highlighted state. Returns NULL if no item is current.

Returns the current drag-and-drop option. The drag-and-drop option specifies which items to accept when they are dropped in the view through drag and drop, or are pasted from the Clipboard. The drag-and-drop option can be one or more of the following: ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_TOOL Accept tool items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_PALETTE Accept palette items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_PACKAGE Accept package items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_CATEGORY Accept category items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_CATALOG Accept catalog items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_STOCKTOOL Accept stock tool items. ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_FILES . Accept files from File Explorer ACTCUI_DDO_ACCEPT_ALL_ITEMS Accept all the catalog items and files from File Explorer.

Gets the position of the first selected item in the view. To enumerate through the selected items, call this function to get the position and then call GetNextSelectedItem() repeatedly to get the selected item pointers. Returns a POSITION value that can be used for iteration with GetNextSelectedItem(), or NULL if no items are selected.

Returns the zero-based index of the first visible item in the client area. The returned index is always less than the number of items. If bPartialOk is true, the function returns the first fully or partially visible item. If it's false, it returns the first fully visible item. Returns -1 if no item is visible or if there is no item in the view.
Retrieves the image size of the view. Images are currently displayed in this size. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Gets the insertion mark. If no insertion mark is displayed, nIndex is set to -1. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Returns the catalog view item at the specified index. The index range should be between zero and one less than the number of items. The number of items can be obtained using GetItemCount(). Returns NULL if the index is out of bounds.
Returns the number of items in the view.
Returns the 32-bit application-specific value associated with the specified item. The double word value was the dwData parameter of a SetItemData() call.
Returns the item at the specified point. Returns NULL if there is no item at the specified point.
Returns the index of the specified item. Returns -1 if the item does not exist in the view.

This method gets the order of the items as they appear in the view. This order is stored in the user's profile file, which stores all the UI settings for a user; it is not necessarily the original order of the items in the catalog. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Gets the bounding rectangle of the item at the specified index. nCode can be one or more of the following values: ACTCUI_CVIR_BOUNDS Gets the bounding rectangle of the entire item, which includes the image, label, spacing, and border. If text is not displayed currently, text and spacing are not included in the rectangle. ACTCUI_CVIR_IMAGE Gets the bounding rectangle of the image with border. ACTCUI_CVIR_LABEL Gets the bounding rectangle of the item text. If text is not displayed currently, the rectangle has zero height. ACTCUI_CVIR_USEFULLLABEL This flag can be specified with ACTCUI_CVIR_BOUNDS or ACTCUI_CVIR_LABEL. If it is specified, the size calculated is to display the full text rather than elided two-line text. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Returns the zero-based index of the last visible item in the client area. The returned index is always less than the number of items. If bPartialOk is true, the function returns the last fully or partially visible item. If it's false, it returns the last fully visible item. Returns -1 if no item is visible or if there is no item in the view.

Gets the selected item identified by pos; then updates pos. You can use GetNextSelectedItem() in a forward iteration loop if you establish the initial position with a call to GetFirstSelectedItemPosition(). You must ensure that the POSITION value is valid. Returns the pointer to the next selected item, or NULL if the pos argument is invalid or if there is an error.
Returns the current alignment of overlay images. See the SetOverlayImageAlignment() method for possible values.
Gets the size at which overlay images are displayed in the view. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Returns the number of rows that can fit in the view area of the catalog view.
This function queries the UI scheme associated with the view. The return value is a pointer to the UI scheme. Returns null if the function fails or if the view is not asssociated with a scheme.
Returns the number of items currently selected.

Returns the item that is currently selected. If multiple items are selected, it returns the first selected item. Use GetNextSelectedItem() to enumerate all the selected items. Returns NULL if no item is currently selected.

Retrieves the rectangle of the view in which the items are displayed. This rectangle is the view's client area excluding the margins. The rectangle is in client coordinates. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Returns the index of the item at the specified point. The point should be in the client coordinates of the catalog view. The results of the test can be one or more of the following hit flags: ACTCUI_CVHT_NOWHERE Not in the view window's client area ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEM On the item; may be combined with ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEMIMAGE or ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEMLABEL ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEMIMAGE On the item's image ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEMLABEL On the item's text ACTCUI_CVHT_ITEMTRIGGER On the item's trigger if the item is a tool and the tool is a flyout tool ACTCUI_CVHT_BACKGROUND On the view background; may be combined with ACTCUI_CVHT_ABOVE, ACTCUI_CVHT_BELOW, ACTCUI_CVHT_LEFT, ACTCUI_CVHT_RIGHT ACTCUI_CVHT_ABOVE Above the viewing area (the rectangle in which the items are displayed, excluding margins) ACTCUI_CVHT_BELOW Below the viewing area (the rectangle in which the items are displayed, excluding margins) ACTCUI_CVHT_LEFT Left of the viewing area (the rectangle in which the items are displayed, excluding margins) ACTCUI_CVHT_RIGHT Right of the viewing area (the rectangle in which the items are displayed, excluding margins) Returns -1 if there is no item at the position specified by pt.
Returns true if the text of an item is currently being edited in place. Otherwise, returns false.
Reads the view-persistent data from the XML DOM node and sets all the view settings. Returns true if the function succeeds; otherwise, returns false.
This function is called by the catalog view before starting to drag the items in the view. It gives derived classes an opportunity to copy the item's drag-and-drop data to the data object.
For internal use only. Overriding this function in a derived class may affect CAdUiPaletteSet functionality if the CAdUiPaletteSet base class function is not called in the override.

This function is called by the catalog view frequently when dragging is in progress. Returns E_NOTIMPL if not implemented or S_OK if successful. DRAGDROP_S_USEDEFAULTCURSORS indicates successful completion of the method, and requests OLE to update the cursor using the OLE-provided default cursors.
Called after the drag and drop of items is finished.

The framework calls this method when the Copy option is selected from the context menu. The base class implementation copies the item data to the data object and, before setting the data object on the Clipboard, calls the virtual method Copy() so that the derived class can copy its own data to the data object. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the Cut option is selected from the context menu. The base class method provides default implementation for this command. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the Help option is selected from the context menu. The base class method provides default implementation for this command. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the Paste option is selected from the context menu. The base class method checks the data object on the Clipboard and, if it recognizes the data, pastes the data from the Clipboard. If it does not recognize the data, it calls the virtual method Paste() so that derived classes get an opportunity to handle the data. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.
The framework calls this method when the Properties option is selected from the context menu. The base class method does nothing. Override this method in the derived class to provide implementation.

The framework calls this method when the Refresh option is selected from the context menu. The base class method provides default implementation for this command. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the Remove option is selected from the context menu. The base class method provides default implementation for this command. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the Rename option is selected from the context menu. The base class method provides default implementation for this command. If special behavior is required, override this method in the derived class.

The framework calls this method when the left mouse button is clicked in the view. A pair of button down and up messages constitutes a click. The click may be on an item or on the background. Use HitTest() to find the clicked item. The base class method does nothing. nFlags can be any combination of the following values: MK_CONTROL Set if the CTRL key is down MK_MBUTTON Set if the middle mouse button is down MK_RBUTTON Set if the right mouse button is down MK_SHIFT Set if the SHIFT key is down
This function is called by the catalog view when an object is pasted from the Clipboard. It provides an opportunity for derived classes to create items using the data in the data object.

This method resets the current order of items to that of the original order in the catalog. After this call, the order of items in the view will be the same as the order of the items in the catalog. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Saves the view-persistent data to the XML DOM node. Returns true if the function succeeds; otherwise, returns false.

Scrolls the contents of the catalog view. cy is the amount of vertical scrolling in pixels. cy is divided by the height, in pixels, of the catalog view's row height, and the view is scrolled by the resulting number of rows. Horizontal scrolling is not supported. cy must be a negative value to scroll the content of the window up. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Selects an item. If the ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_MULTISELECT style is not set, then only one item can be selected at a time, and selecting an item automatically clears the currently selected item. If nIndex is -1, the function selects or clears all the items. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Use this function to select or clear a range of items. If ACTCUI_CVSTYLE_MULTISELECT style is not set, only the item at the start index is selected. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Sets the pointer to the catalog item whose children are to be displayed in the catalog view. The catalog view is not the owner of the catalog item. Hence, it will not delete the catalog item when the catalog view is destroyed. If the catalog item pointer set in the view or its children are deleted, the view should be updated immediately by calling CAcTcCatalogView::Update(). This function should be called whenever the content of the catalog item changes. Returns true if the function succeeds; otherwise, returns false.
Sets the catalog view style. See Create() for a list of possible catalog view styles. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Sets the current drag-and-drop option. The drag-and-drop option specifies which items to accept when they are dropped in the view through drag and drop, or are pasted from the Clipboard. See GetDragDropOption() for a list of possible values. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

Sets the image size for the view. Images are displayed in this size. The specified size must be within the maximum (64*64) and minimum (16*16) range. If size is outside of this range, the method will fail.

Draws or removes the insertion mark at the specified index. The insertion mark is removed if nIndex is -1. If bAfter is nonzero, the insertion mark is placed after the item. If this argument is zero, the insertion mark is placed before the item. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Sets the 32-bit application-specific value associated with the specified item. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

This method rearranges the order of the items in the view. The order is stored in the user's profile file, which stores all of the UI settings for a user. The original order of the items in the catalog is not affected by this method. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets the alignment of overlay images. nAlignment may be one of the following: ACTCUI_OVERLAY_ALIGN_TOPLEFT Display overlay image on the upper-left corner of the item's image. ACTCUI_OVERLAY_ALIGN_TOPRIGHT Display overlay image on the upper-right corner of the item's image. ACTCUI_OVERLAY_ALIGN_BOTTOMLEFT Display overlay image on the lower-left corner of the item's image. ACTCUI_OVERLAY_ALIGN_BOTTOMRIGHT Display overlay image on the lower-right corner of the item's image. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the size at which overlay images are displayed in the view. The overlay image size should be less than the current image size; otherwise, the function fails. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sorts the tools in the catalog view. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Updates the catalog view by recreating the view items from the children of the associated catalog item. Call this function when the contents of the catalog item have changed. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.

The tool palette UI module contains a global singleton object of type CAcTcUiManager, which can be obtained using the global function AcTcUiGetManager(). This object manages the tool palette UI module and contains a function to get the tool palette window pointer. It also contains helper functions to create, export, import, and find palettes.
Adds the scheme to the manager. Returns the index of the added scheme.

Adds tool filter information. Tool filters screen tools for compatibility with specific products. Only those tools whose target product list matches one of the tool filters may participate in drag and copy operations. nMajorVersion may be set to -1 if the tools do not need to be filtered on version. nMinorVersion may be set to -1 if the tools do not need to be filtered on minor version. dwLocaleId may be set to -1 if the tools do not need to be filtered on local ID. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Creates a new palette and adds it to the workspace. Specifically, this function: Creates a palette (CAcTcUiToolPalette).Creates the palette window if ACTCUI_CNPS_NOCREATEWINDOW is not specified.Creates palette catalog item (AcTcPalette).Adds the palette catalog item it to the workspace catalog if ACTCUI_CNPS_NOADD is not specified.Associates the palette catalog item with the UI palette. The dwFlags argument can be one or more of the following values: ACTCUI_CNPS_NOCREATEWINDOW Don't create the palette windows ACTCUI_CNPS_NOADD Don't add the created palete set to the workspace ACTCUI_CNPS_CREATEHIDDEN Create a hidden palette If the function succeeds, the return value is the pointer to the newly created palette. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.

Removes the tool filter at position iIndex in the manager's tool filter array. iIndex should be in the range zero to one less than the number of tool filters. Use the GetToolFilterCount() method to determine the number of filters. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
This is ExecuteTool, a member of class CAcTcUiManager.
Exports the tool palettes to the specified file. Exports both UI information and palette contents. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Finds the palette which contains the specified catalog item. The catalog item can refer to a palette or tool. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Gets the application window handle. Returns the application window handle set by SetApplicationWindow(), or NULL if the application handle is not set.

Returns a pointer to the COleDropTarget object used by the manager. If the function fails, the return value is NULL. The returned drop target pointer can be used to pass drag-and-drop messages to the UI manager so that it can handle the drag-and-drop of catalog items and so on. For example, if a palette is dropped on an application window, that window can forward the message to this drop target so that the manager will handle the palette and add it to the workspace catalog.
Returns the scheme with the given name. The return value is the pointer to the UI scheme with given name. Returns null if the function fails or if a scheme with the name is not found.
Returns the total number of schemes in the manager.

Gets tool filter information. Filters screen tools for compatibility with specific products. Only those tools whose target product list matches one of the tool filters may participate in drag and copy operations. iIndex should be in the range zero to one less than the number of filters. Use the GetToolFilterCount() method to find the number of filters. The size of the pszProductName buffer should be at least ACTC_MAX_PRODUCT_NAME. This parameter may be set to null if this value is not needed. pMajorVersion, pMinorVersion, and pLocaleId may each be set to null if their values are not needed. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Returns the number of tool filters.
Returns the tool palette window. If the function is successful, the return value is the pointer to the tool palette window. If the function fails, the return value is NULL.
Imports the tool palettes from the specified file and adds them to the tool palette window. Imports both UI information and palette contents. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Returns true if the tool palette window is visible, or false if the tool palette window is hidden.

Loads the palette sets from the XML DOM node. The XML node should point to . The current palette scheme is unloaded and all the palette sets are deleted. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Defines a point where the reactor is being notified.

Removes the scheme from the manager. The scheme is removed from the list, but the object is not deleted. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Saves the palette sets to the XML DOM node. The XML node should point to . Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Sets the application window handle to be used for creating palettes, displaying message boxes, and so on. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Sets display of the tool palette window. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
CAcTcUiPaletteView is used to display the tools contained in a palette.
This is CAcTcUiPaletteView, a member of class CAcTcUiPaletteView.

This class handles the UI schemes in tool palettes. Every tool palette set must belong to a scheme, and it cannot be part of two schemes. The palette sets in each scheme can have their own traits. Schemes exist independent of each other, and multiple schemes can coexist.

Creates a new palette set and adds it to the UI scheme. This function creates a palette set (CAcTcUiToolPaletteSet) and the palette set window. It also creates a palette (CAcTcUiToolPalette) and the palette window. A palette catalog item (AcTcPalette) is created and added to the workspace catalog. The palette catalog item is added to the workspace and is associated with the UI palette. If the function succeeds, the return value is the pointer to the newly created palette set. If the function fails, the return value is null.

Exports the tool palettes to the specified file. Exports both UI information and palette contents. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Finds the palette that contains the specified catalog item in the corresponding AcTcScheme. The catalog item can refer to a palette or a tool. If the palette is found, the return value is non-zero. If the palette is not found, the return value is zero.
Returns the palette set if it is present in the scheme. If the function succeeds, the return value is the pointer to the palette set. If the function fails, the return value is null.

Imports the tool palettes from the specified file and adds them to the Tool Palettes window. Imports both UI information and palette contents. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Reads the scheme-persistent data from the XML DOM node. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Refreshes the palette (AcTcPalette) that is associated with the UI palette, depending on the refresh scope that is passed. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Saves the view-persistent data to the XML DOM node. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Shows, hides, or restores the palette set in the scheme, depending on the ShowOption value that is passed. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Removes the palette set from the scheme, deletes the palette set object, and destroys the associated window. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

CAcTcUiToolPalette is the container for palette view (CAcTcUiPaletteView). The palette view is embedded as a child window in the tool palette window's client area. CAcTcUiToolPalette overrides the base class functions to customize the behavior of the base class. The tool palette can contain only one palette view.
This class lets clients organize available tool palettes in logical groups.
Adds the item pointed to by pPalette to the group and returns its index.

This function clones a group and returns the newly created group in pClone. The caller is responsible for deleting the cloned group. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Deletes all palettes and sub-groups from this group. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Deletes all palettes from this group. This function does not delete sub-groups. Use the DeleteAllItems() function to delete both palettes and groups. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Deletes the tool palette pointed to by pPalette from this group. If the tool palette appears in more than one group, and the bRecursive flag is set to true, this function deletes the tool palette from this group and all sub-groups. If bRecursive is set to false, the palette is removed only from this group. The caller is responsible for deleting the pPalette pointer. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Finds a group by name. Nested group names can be specified using a nested path with each level separated by front or back slash (Ex. GroupSubGroupSubSubGroup). If bRecursive is true it searches the groups recursively till it finds a group which matches the specified nested path. Returns true if the group was found, false otherwise.
Finds the palette by name. The search is not case sensitive. Returns true if the palette was found, false otherwise.
Returns the index of the active palette in the group.
Gets the XML node that contains the group's custom data. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.

Sets pPalette to point to the CAcTcUiToolPalette item at position iIndex. This function fails if the type of the item at iIndex is not CAcTcUiToolPalette. The IsItemPalette() function can be used to verify the type of the desired item before calling this function. If this function succeeds, its return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Returns the number of items in the group. This number includes both palettes and sub-groups.
Returns the name of the group.
Inserts the item pointed to by pPalette at the position indicated by iIndex, and returns the index of the newly added item.

A tool palette group can contain either tool palettes or other tool palette groups. This function can be used to find the type of item at an index. Returns true if the item at the specified index is a tool palette, or false if it is a group. iIndex should be in the range from zero to one less than the number of items.

This function loads a group definition from the XML node represented by pUnk. Tool palettes whose IDs are referenced in the XML node should be loaded before this function is called. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Removes pPalette from the group. The caller is responsible for deleting the pointer. The behavior of this overload is identical to that of the corresponding overload of the DeleteItem() function.
Resets the item by re-initializing its members to default values and deleting its children. If this function succeeds, it returns value is non-zero. Otherwise, this function returns zero.

This function saves this group's definition to the XML node represented by pUnk. Only the IDs of the group's tool palettes are saved to the XML node. The tool palettes themselves must be saved separately. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

Sets the tool palette at position nIndex as the active palette. This function fails if the item at nIndex is a group, rather than a tool palette. Use the IsItemPalette() function to get the type of an item before calling this function. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.
Sets the name of the group. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

CAcTcUiToolPaletteSet is the container for one or more tool palettes (CAcTcUiToolPalette). CAcTcUiToolPaletteSet customizes the base class by implementing features specific to the tool palette set and modifying the standard base class behavior as necessary. The constructor is protected. The palette set pointer for the tool palette window can be obtained using AcTcUiGetToolPaletteWindow.

Writes the palette set information to the specified XML node. Writes both the UI data and palette set contents. The content data are the palette catalog items associated to the palette set. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Finds the palette by name. The search is not case sensitive. Returns true if the palette was found, false otherwise.

Gets the active palette group name, including the nesting path if the group is nested inside another group. The general format is GroupSubGroup...GroupName. If the active palette group is nested inside another group, pszGroup contains the whole nesting path. For example, if the active palette group name is Bolts and this group is inside another group called Nuts and Bolts, then the name is Nuts and BoltsBolts. The name can have multiple nesting levels.
Returns a pointer to the All Palettes group. The All Palettes group includes all palettes in the palette set, presented in a flat list without hierarchy or duplicates.

This function queries the UI scheme associated with the palette set. The return value is a pointer to the UI scheme. Returns null if the function fails or if the palette set is not asssociated with a scheme.

Gets the root tool palette group associated with the palette set. If bCreate is false, and no tool palette group exists in the palette set, this function returns null. If bCreate is true, and no tool palette group exists in the palette set, this function creates the tool palette group. Returns a pointer to the tool palette group associated with the palette set.

Reads the palette set information from the specified XML node. This function reads both the UI data and palette set contents. It creates a palette catalog item objects to read the content of each palette in the set and associates the palette with the palette window. It does not add the palette catalog items to the workspace catalog. The caller is responsible for adding the palette catalog items to the workspace catalog or deleting them when this palette set is deleted. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Removes the tool palette at index iIndex from the palette set. Returns true if successful. Otherwise, returns false.

Finds the specified palette and sets it as active palette. If the palette is in a group which is not active it sets that group as active group. Returns true if the palette was set active. Returns false if the palette could not be found.

Sets the active palette group name, which should include the nesting path if the group is nested inside another group. The general format is GroupSubGroup...GroupName. pszGroup must contain the whole nesting path if the group is a nested inside another group. For example, if the active palette group name is Bolts and this group is inside another group called Nuts and Bolts, then the name is Nuts and BoltsBolts. The name can have multiple nesting levels. If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Sets the display of the tool palette set window. If the function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. If the function fails, the return value is zero.
Virtual method that receives the theme modification event.

Use this function to get if the data object can be pasted in the tool palette. Returns true if the data object contains data for pasting to the view, or false if the data object does not contain data which can be pasted.

Writes the palette information to the specified XML node. Writes both the UI data and palette contents. The content data is the palette catalog item associated to the palette window. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
This function queries the UI scheme associated with the palette. The return value is a pointer to the UI scheme. Returns null if the function fails or if the palette is not asssociated with a scheme.
Returns the pointer to the palette view window, which displays the tools. The return value will be NULL if there is an error.

Reads the palette information from the specified XML node. This function reads both the UI data and the palette contents. It creates a palette catalog item object to read the palette content and associates it with the palette window. It does not add the palette catalog item to the workspace catalog. The caller is responsible for adding the associated palette catalog item to the workspace catalog or deleting it when this palette is deleted. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Use this function to paste an object to the tool palette.

By default, the tool palette creates a CAcTcUiPaletteView view object. This function can be used to substitute a custom view derived from CAcTcUiPaletteView. When a custom view is set, any existing view is destroyed. After a custom view is set, the CAcTcUiToolPalette object on which this function is called assumes ownership of the memory pointed to by pView. The caller must not delete the passed view pointer. The window of the passed view should not be created before calling this function. The framework will create it when needed. pView should be a pointer to either CAcTcUiPaletteView or a class derived from CAcTcUiPaletteView. The ideal way to set the custom view is to override the virtual CAdUiPalette::Create(CAdUiPaletteSet* pParent) method, and then call the base class CAcTcUiToolPalette::Create() method to create the palette. Alternatively, the custom view also can be set by handling the WM_ONCREATE message and calling this function before calling the base class handler. In either case, it is important to call the base class methods for default processing. If this function succeeds, the return value is non-zero. Otherwise, the return value is zero.

The CAcUiAngleComboBox class provides a specific implementation of CAcUiComboBox that automatically provides the AC_ES_ANGLE flag for data validation of AutoCAD angles. Data will be converted to the units value provided by the system variable AUPREC and AUNITS, which are also governed by the UNITS command. Please see CAcUiComboBox for the complete set of member variables and functions that are provided.
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

The CAcUiAngleEdit class provides a specific implementation of CAcUiEdit that automatically provides the AC_ES_ANGLE flag for data validation of AutoCAD angles. Data will be converted to the units value provided by the system variable AUPREC and AUNITS, which are also governed by the UNITS command. Please see CAcUiEdit for the complete set of member variables and functions that are provided.
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.
Calls the inherited method ensuring AC_ES_ANGLE is set.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

This class specializes CAcUiMRUComboBox for dimensioning arrowhead selection. The arrowhead control displays bitmaps representing the standard twenty AutoCAD dimensioning arrowhead styles, which are always present in the list (note that an item corresponding to 'Origin2' may be selectively excluded). By default no optional or additional items are present or added. The cargo associated with each item is the AutoCAD index for the associated stock arrowhead (0 to 19). When MRU items are added to the list, they are automatically assigned a unique cargo value greater than AutoCADs index for a user-defined arrowhead style.

Called to add a user-defined arrowhead to the list. Generates a unique MRU cargo value in the manner of GenerateCargoFromMRU(). Returns AddItemToMRU() passing the given name and generated cargo value.
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.
Called to determine the height, in pixels, of each item in the list. Adjusts the value returned by the inherited method, ensuring enough space to render the arrowhead bitmaps.
This method is the MFC handler for LPDRAWITEMSTRUCT

This method is called to draw the image associated with an item, based on the item's cargo, in the given DC and rectangle. Draws an arrowhead bitmap, using the AutoCAD arrowhead index indicated by the given cargo, fit within the given rectangle.

This method is called to determine the text associated with one of the additional items. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE otherwise. By default, name is set to 'Other...' for Other2. For Other1, if m_bUseOther1 is TRUE, then name is set to the popup-style message 'User Arrow...'; otherwise, name is set to the item-style message 'User arrow'.
Returns a value indicating if the 'Origin2' item should be included when the list is re-generated.
Loads or reloads the images used by items in the combo box. You can call this method in a themed environment after a theme change.

This method is called to add stock items to the list. Adds stock AutoCAD arrowheads to the list (that is, from Default to None). If the Other1 additional item is not to be used, a stock item corresponding to a user-defined arrowhead is added to the list (Other1 is assumed to be used in a derived class to trigger definition of user-defined arrowheads). If SetUseOrigin2(TRUE) has been called, then an item corresponding to 'Origin2' will be included.
Sets an internal flag indicating if the 'Origin2' item should be included when the list is re-generated.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

CAcUiBitmapButton inherits from the CAdUiBitmapButton class for use with AutoCAD. It does not specialize any behavior of CAdUiBitmapButton, but is provided for the AcUi library. Refer to CAdUiBitmapButton for complete details of the member functions and member data that are part of this derived class.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

CAcUiBitmapStatic inherits from the CAdUiBitmapStatic class for use with AutoCAD. It does not specialize any behavior of CAdUiBitmapStatic, but is provided for the AcUi library. Refer to CAdUiBitmapStatic for complete details of the member functions and member data that are part of this derived class.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

This class specializes CAcUiMRUComboBox for color selection. The color combobox displays color swatches representing selections from AutoCAD's palette. The stock items always present in the control reflect color numbers 1 through 7. Both of the optional items are used: Option1 displays 'ByLayer' and Option2 displays 'ByBlock'. MRU items display 'Color nnn' where nnn is the associated color number. The cargo associated with each item indicates an AutoCAD color number (1 to 255), ByBlock is associated with 0, and ByLayer with 256. The Other1 item is enabled and triggers the AutoCAD Color selection dialog. If Other2 is enabled it displays as 'Windows...' and by default triggers the Windows Color Selection Common Dialog. If the user selects an item from either of these dialogs, the selection appears in the MRU list and becomes the current item in the control.
Generates a name for a new color, based on the given AutoCAD color number. Returns AddItemToMRU() passing the generated name and color index.

This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized, usually to zero or FALSE. The constructor sets m_bUseOption1, m_bUseOption2 and m_bUseOther1 to TRUE and initializes m_cargoOption1 and m_cargoOption2 to AutoCAD's ByLayer and ByBlock color indices (in other words, 256 and 0). m_hPalette is set to AutoCAD's current color palette and m_blockColorIndex defaults to 7.
Called to determine the height of each item in the list, in pixels. By default, returns a value calculated from the height of an OR bar (|) using the control's current font.

This method is called to draw the image associated with an item, based on the item's cargo, in the given DC and rectangle. Draws a color swatch, using the AutoCAD color index indicated by the given cargo, filling the given rectangle.
Gets corresponding item index by calling FindItemByCargo() and passing colorIndex.

This method is called to translate a color index to a color value. The value returned may vary based on operating system and display drivers. The value might be returned as a palette-relative color (in other words, a PALETTERGB) or an RGB triple.
Performs a lookup in the palette indicated by m_hPalette (if not NULL) or AutoCAD's color palette. Returns the index of the nearest color or -1 on error.
This method returns the color index used by the current layer of the currently open AutoCAD drawing. On error, -1 is returned.
Gets item's color index (or -1), by a call to GetItemCargo(), passing item.

Called by OnSelectOther() to prompt for a new AutoCAD color. The default implementation acts as a wrapper for acedSetColorDialog(). On success, colorIndex should be set to the desired AutoCAD color number and the routine should return TRUE; otherwise, returns FALSE.

This method is called to determine the text associated with one of the additional items. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE otherwise. By default, name is set to 'Other...' for Other2. For Other1, if m_bUseOther1 is TRUE, then name is set to the popup-style message 'User Arrow...'; otherwise, name is set to the item-style message 'User arrow'.

Called by OnSelectOther() to prompt for a new Windows color. On success, color should be updated with the desired color and the routine should return TRUE; otherwise, returns FALSE. The default implementation uses a CColorDialog to obtain a new color.

This method is used to translate a color index into a color value. By default, if logPalette is not NULL and colorIndex is in range for the given palette definition, then the RGB value in the definition corresponding to colorIndex is returned. Otherwise, the value corresponding to the color in AutoCAD's current palette is returned (obtained by a call to acedGetRGB(), passing colorIndex).
This method is called to add stock items to the list. Adds the stock colors to the list (i.e. color numbers 1 through 7).

This method is called to process selection of an additional item when the control's listbox closes. If the event is processed, the handler should set newSel to the index of the item that should be made current and return TRUE. It is possible (and expected) that the handler will have modified the list. If not processed, the handler should return FALSE. The combobox displays a color selection dialog via GetWindowsColor() (if isOther2 is set) or GetOtherColorIndex(). If either method returns TRUE, a new color is added to the MRU set via AddColorToMRU(), newSel is set to the new item's index and the routine returns TRUE. Otherwise FALSE is returned.
This method is used internally by DrawItemImage() to draw a multi-colored image for the Additional list items.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

This class specializes CAcUiMRUComboBox for color selection. The color combobox displays color swatches representing selections from AutoCAD's palette. The stock items always present in the control reflect color numbers 1 through 7. Both of the optional items are used: Option1 displays 'ByLayer' and Option2 displays 'ByBlock'. MRU items display 'Color nnn' where nnn is the associated color number. The cargo associated with each item indicates an AutoCAD color number (1 to 255), ByBlock is associated with 0, and ByLayer with 256. The Other1 item is enabled and triggers the AutoCAD Color selection dialog. If Other2 is enabled it displays as 'Windows...' and by default triggers the Windows Color Selection Common Dialog. If the user selects an item from either of these dialogs, the selection appears in the MRU list and becomes the current item in the control. Generally, you should use one of the classes derived from CAcUiComboBox that add persistency flags to the ComboBox Control class to verify specific AutoCAD data types: CAcUiStringComboBox Persistently adds the AC_ES_STRING flag CAcUiSymbolComboBox Persistently adds the AC_ES_SYMBOL flag CAcUiNumericComboBox Persistently adds the AC_ES_NUMERIC flag CAcUiAngleComboBox Persistently adds the AC_ES_ANGLE flag

If the control returned by calling GetEditBox() returns non-NULL and represents a CAcUiEdit (or a derived class, as determined by run-time type information), then this routine returns a pointer to the edit control. Otherwise, the routine returns NULL. Returns a pointer to an AutoCAD-specific edit control, or NULL on error
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.
If the control returned by AcUiEditBox() is not NULL, then the edit control's Convert() is called.

If the control returned by AcUiEditBox() is not NULL, then the edit control's ConvertData() is called. Otherwise, this routine simply returns TRUE. Returns TRUE if the conversion succeeded, and FALSE otherwise.
If the control returned by AcUiEditBox() is not NULL, then the edit control's SetRange() is called.

If the control returned by AcUiEditBox() is not NULL, then the edit control's Validate() is called. Otherwise, this routine simply returns TRUE. Returns TRUE if the control's content is valid, and FALSE otherwise.

If the control returned by AcUiEditBox() is not NULL, then the edit control's ValidateData() is called. Otherwise, this routine simply returns kAcUiError_None. Returns an appropriate error code if the string represents invalid content, or kAcUiError_None if valid.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

CAcUiDialog specializes the CAdUiDialog class for use with AutoCAD. Refer to CAdUiDialog for complete details of the member functions and member data that are part of this derived class. See 'Built-In MFC User Interface Support' in the ObjectARX Developer's Guide for an explanation of the distinction between CAdUi and CAcUi classes.
Returns a pointer to AutoCAD's main window.
Returns a string identifying the root of AutoCAD's registry entries.
Constructs a CAcUiDialog object and enables or disables tool tips based on the AutoCAD TOOLTIPS system variable.
This ClassWizard-generated override simply invokes the inherited method.

This routine is provided to notify the application if floating windows (non-modal windows) should be enabled or disabled. Calls to this routine are expected to be cumulative (in other words, two calls in succession that pass FALSE must be matched with two calls that pass TRUE for floating windows to be re-enabled). By default, this routine notifies AutoCAD, affecting dockable and non-modal windows.

This routine is provided to notify the application if document switching (between MDI windows) should be enabled or disabled. Calls to this routine are expected to be cumulative (in other words, two calls in succession that pass FALSE must be matched with two calls that pass TRUE for switching to be re-enabled). By default, this routine returns AutoCAD's current MDE activation state.

This function is used to find the full path of the context help file for the application given a base name. It simply calls AcUiFindContextHelpFullPath, which uses the AutoCAD search path to find the file. Override this to use a different search path. Returns TRUE if full path found.

This routine is provided to interrogate the application and determine if document switching (between MDI windows) is enabled. If so, the routine returns TRUE. Otherwise, it returns FALSE. By default, this routine returns AutoCAD's current MDE activation state.
Prior to calling the inherited method, this override sets the DIASTAT system variable to FALSE and informs AutoCAD that a command has been canceled (in case MULTIPLE is active).

This MFC-defined method is called during dialog initialization. The default handler calls OnInitDialogBegin(), then the inherited OnInitDialog() and then OnInitDialogFinish(). If tips are allowed then the tip windows are created via a call to SetUseTips(). If m_hIcon is NULL then a default icon is loaded (i.e. the first icon found in the application's executable file). The method returns the value returned from the call to the inherited OnInitDialog(), which is normally TRUE to allow Windows to set focus to the first control in the dialog or FALSE if the routine sets focus to some other control.
Prior to calling the inherited method, this override sets the DIASTAT system variable to TRUE.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

The CAdUiDockControlBar class inherits almost all the standard behavior of the CAdUiDockControlbar class. It implements the overridable CanFrameworkTakeFocus(). This overridable is called by the docking system when AutoCAD requests the focus. The CAdUiDockControlBar implementation allows AutoCAD to get the focus only if the mouse pointer is outside the control bar area. Otherwise, the control bar keeps the focus. This is the way the AutoCAD docking tools usually behave, so derive from CAcUiDockControlBar instead of CAdUiDockControlBar to get the same behavior.

Called by the docking system when the frame window asks to get the focus back. The default implementation returns false, leaving the focus to the control bar. If your control bar returns true from this call, the frame window will take the focus.

Handles the private message that is sent by AutoCAD to find out if it should take the focus, or leave it with the currently active window. This function should return true if the focus should stay where it is.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

CAcUiDropSite inherits from the CAdUiDropSite class for use with AutoCAD. It does not specialize any behavior of CAdUiDropSite, but is provided for the AcUi library. Refer to CAdUiDropSite for complete details of the member functions and member data that are part of this derived class.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

The AcUi system provides the CAcUiEdit class to extend the basic CAdUiComboBox class and add AutoCAD-specific data validation. This class adds input validation that is specific to AutoCAD, and provides a Tooltip-like tool for truncated text items: TextTips. This class takes bit flags to add desired validation behavior, based on the following types of input: Numeric, String, Angular, and Symbol names. Generally, you should use one of the classes derived from CAcUiEdit, that add persistency flags to the Edit Control class to verify specific AutoCAD data types: CAcUiStringEdit Persistently adds the AC_ES_STRING flag CAcUiSymbolEdit Persistently adds the AC_ES_SYMBOL flag CAcUiNumericEdit Persistently adds the AC_ES_NUMERIC flag CAcUiAngleEdit Persistently adds the AC_ES_ANGLE flag
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.
For numeric or angular styles, this member retrieves the control's text, passes the text to ConvertData() and updates the control with the converted text (assuming there was no conversion error).

For numeric or angular styles, this member converts the text passed in and returns TRUE (assuming there was no conversion error). For string and symbol styles no conversion is performed; the routine simply returns FALSE. Returns TRUE if the conversion succeeded; otherwise, returns FALSE.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler will process the following notifications/requests: kAdUiNotify_RestoreFocus: If the control requested focus be restored (usually during validation failure) the handler will set focus to the control, select the entire contents, and reply kAdUiReply_Ok. kAdUiNotify_Validate: The control's contents will be converted and validated via calls to ConvertData() and ValidateData(). If validation does not produce an error then kAdUiReply_Valid is returned, otherwise kAdUiReply_NotValid is returned. All other requests are processed by calling the inherited method. Returns a reply code. In general kAdUiReply_Nothing indicates the message was ignored, kAdUiReply_Ok indicates the message was handled.
Indicates that the value in the edit box has changed.
Flag to check if there were changes in the text.

AcUi extends combobox support to automatically manage a MRU (most recently used) list within the control. The basic functionality is provided by the class CAcUiMRUComboBox (derived from CAcUiComboBox). A companion class, CAcUiMRUListBox, provides DrawTip support for the combobox's ComboLBox. This is necessary due to the MRU combobox implementation as an owner-draw control. The MRU controls display a list of items containing a small image followed by some text. Each item also manages a unique value, referred to as cargo, and maintained as standard Windows ITEMDATA within the control. To be useful, items should not have empty text or text consisting solely of white space. As well, application-defined cargo values should generally be greater than or equal to zero; negative values have special significance within the control (refer to the values in the enumeration ACUI_MRU_CARGO). To use these classes, the combobox control being subclassed should be non-editable and have the owner-draw, fixed item height and use-strings style bits set. Automatic sorting is not recommended. In other words, ensure CBS_DROPDOWNLIST, CBS_HASSTRINGS and CBS_OWNERDRAWFIXED are set, and CBS_SORT is clear. The MRU comboboxes display a list of up to six MRU items, as defined by the constant ACUI_MAX_COMBOBOX_MRU. Following the MRU items are up to two optional items. These are followed by stock items for the list. When the combobox list is dropped down, up to two additional items may be added to the list; selecting either of these triggers an event in the control that is usually overridden to provide a pop-up dialog. When the combobox list closes, these two items are automatically removed. For example, a hypothetical control might display the following when the list is dropped down: User 1 User 2 ByLayer Item 1 Item 2 Item 3 Other... In this case, User1 and User2 are MRU items that were previously added to the list. ByLayer represents an optional item (the second optional item is suppressed). Item1, Item2, and Item3 represent stock items that are always present in the list. Other... represents an additional item added when the list was dropped down, and removed when the list closes. Selecting the Other... item triggers an event that lets the user add additional MRU items.
Refreshes the control's contents, adding MRU items, any optional items, and all stock items (via a call to OnAddItems()).

On success, the item will be inserted at the front of the MRU list; If the MRU is full, the oldest item will scroll off. AddItems() will be called to refresh the control for display. Returns the index of the item (if inserted or found), or -1 on error.

The CAcUiTrueColorComboBox class specializes CAcUiMRUComboBox for color selection. The color combo box displays color swatches representing the colors given to it as AcCmColor objects. The stock items present in the control reflect color numbers 1 through 7. Both optional items are used: Option1 displays BYLAYER and Option2 displays BYBLOCK. MRU items display the string generated by AcCmColor::colorNameForDisplay(). The cargo associated with each item is an index to a table of AcCmColor objects that this class maintains, with AcCmColor representations of BYBLOCK and BYLAYER already in the table by default. The m_cargoOther1 data member is enabled and triggers the AutoCAD Color Selection dialog box. If m_cargoOther2 is enabled, it displays as 'Windows...' and by default triggers the Windows Color Selection common dialog. If the user selects an item from either of these dialog boxes, the selection appears in the MRU list and becomes the current item in the control.

Otherwise, it returns the value that corresponds to the color in AutoCAD's current palette. If color is a true color, this function returns the RGB value of the color.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler process the following notifications/requests: kAdUiNotify_AppMainWindow Sets the CWnd pointer passed by address in lParam to the application's main window. kAdUiNotify_AppResourceInstance Sets the HINSTANCE passed by address in lParam to the application's default resource instance. kAdUiNotify_Generic Passes the controlId and lParam to OnNotifyGeneric() and returns the result. kAdUiNotify_UpdateTip Passes the CWnd passed in lParam to OnNotifyUpdateTip() and returns the result. kAdUiNotify_HideWindow Hides the dialog and forwards the request to the dialog's parent. kAdUiNotify_ShowWindow Forwards the request to the dialog's parent then restores the dialog. kAdUiNotify_Change Passes the controlId and lParam to OnNotifyControlChange() and returns the result. kAdUiNotify_NotValid Passes the controlId and FALSE to OnNotifyControlValid() and returns the result. kAdUiNotify_Valid Passes the controlId and TRUE to OnNotifyControlValid() and returns the result. kAdUiNotify_CommandState Updates m_commandState with the value in lParam (cast to ADUI_COMMAND_STATE) and forwards the message to the dialog's parent. For each of these notifications, unless indicated otherwise, the default method returns kAdUiReply_Ok. All other requests are ignored and return kAdUiReply_Nothing. Returns a reply code appropriate to notifyCode. In general kAdUiReply_Nothing indicates the message was ignored, kAdUiReply_Ok indicates the message was handled.

This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the dialog's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the control handles the message (i.e., returns non-zero) then the reply from the control is returned. Otherwise, if the control does not exist or ignores the message (i.e., returns zero) then the reply from the dialog's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general, zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyDialog : public CAdUiBaseDialog { ... protected: //{{AFX_MSG(CMyDialog) ... afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam); //}}AFX_MSG DECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP() };In the class implementation, a corresponding message map entry needs to be made: const UINT aduiMessage = AdUiMessage(); BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyDialog, CAdUiBaseDialog) //{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyDialog) ... ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(aduiMessage, OnAdUiMessage) //}}AFX_MSG_MAP END_MESSAGE_MAP()The new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyDialog::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam) { UINT controlId = AdUiNotifyId(wParam); ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = AdUiNotification(wParam); ADUI_REPLY reply; reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam); if (!reply) reply = CAdUiBaseDialog::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam); return reply; }

This MFC-defined method is called during dialog initialization. The default handler calls OnInitDialogBegin(), then the inherited OnInitDialog() and then OnInitDialogFinish(). If tips are allowed then the tip windows are created via a call to SetUseTips(). If m_hIcon is NULL then a default icon is loaded (i.e. the first icon found in the application's executable file). The method returns the value returned from the call to the inherited OnInitDialog(), which is normally TRUE to allow Windows to set focus to the first control in the dialog or FALSE if the routine sets focus to some other control.
