This method is called during the completion of the default OnInitDialog(), after a call to the base class OnInitDialog(). The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default routine does nothing.

This method is provided to handle a notification that a control has changed, outside of the usual Windows or MFC framework. In AdUi, edit controls will notify their AdUi containers when their contents change using this mechanism (similar to sending EN_CHANGE). Derived controls can be made to explicitly notify their containers by calling AdUiNotify() passing the container, kAdUiNotify_ControlChange, the control's ID and an optional lParam. By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

A dialog receives this notification when an AdUi control determines that it has transitioned from containing valid data to non-valid, or vice-versa. Derived controls can be made to explicitly notify their containers by calling AdUiNotify() passing the container, kAdUiNotify_Valid or kAdUiNotifyNotValid and the control's ID (pass zero for lParam). By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

This method is provided to handle a generic, application-defined notification. By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

Typically, when an AdUi control detects the cursor moving over the control, it sends tip update notifications to its AdUi container. By default, a dialog will respond by determining if tips are enabled and if so, querying the control for the type of tip that should be displayed. If the control requests a TextTip or a DrawTip then the dialog's m_pTextTip is given a chance to update and the routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok; otherwise any currently displayed TextTip or DrawTip is hidden and kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned.

This method processes TTN_NEEDTEXT notifications (for example, requests for Common Control ToolTip text). The default handler determines the control for which text is needed and queries the control for the type of tip supports. If the control requests a ToolTip then the text is obtained from the control. Finally, if the control acknowledges the text request and returns a non-empty string, then a ToolTip is displayed, presenting the text, and the routine returns TRUE. Otherwise, the method returns FALSE.
This MFC-defined method is called after the window has been destroyed. The default method calls SetUseTips(), passing FALSE, to de-allocate any text or tool tip windows.
This routine returns the result of calling the inherited method, after re-establishing any resources that may have been swapped out by DoModal() or Create().

This method loads the bitmap, re-calculates the bitmap image size and adjusts the button to the new image size (if m_bAutoSizeToBitmap is TRUE). If m_bmpResId is not empty then the bitmap is loaded using the resource ID. If m_bmpResId is empty then the button's text is expected to contain a string representing the bitmap resource ID. AutoLoad then use the button's text to locate and load the bitmap resource and, if successful, will adjust the button's text to accommodate tool-tip text. Normally, CAdUiBitmapButton responds to tool-tip text requests by supplying the button's text. AutoLoad facilitates this by replacing the button's text with the text remaining after extracting the bitmap resource ID. If the button's text contains the bitmap resource ID followed by an OR Bar then the text following the OR Bar will become the button's text after AutoLoad() is called. AutoLoad() strips the leading text up to the OR Bar, leaving the remainder as the button's text. For example, if the button was created with the text 'MYBMP|My button', then after AutoLoad() the text 'My button' will remain.

This function is called by LoadBitmap() to load an image from a resource. The member is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler calls LoadBitmapResource() passing strResId, m_bmp and NULL as parameters. The function returns the result from LoadBitmapResource().

This routine is called to refresh or alter the bitmap image, obtained from a resource. The member is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler calls LoadBitmap() passing strResId as a parameter. If successful then if auto-sizing is enabled SizeToBitmap() is called, then the inherited OnReload() is invoked. The function returns TRUE on success and FALSE otherwise.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler will process the kAdUiNotify_GetToolText request/notification which routes the request to OnGetToolText(), treating lParam as a pointer to a CString that will receive the tool text. If OnGetToolText() returns TRUE then DoAdUiMessage() returns kAdUiReply_Ok otherwise kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. All other requests are ignored and return kAdUiReply_Nothing. Returns a reply code appropriate to notifyCode. In general kAdUiReply_Nothing indicates the message was ignored, kAdUiReply_Ok indicates the message was handled.

This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the control's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (i.e. returns non-zero) then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (i.e. returns zero) then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. Example This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyComboBox : public CAdUiComboBox {...protected://{{AFX_MSG(CMyComboBox)...afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam);//}}AFX_MSGDECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP()};In the class implementation, a corresponding message map entry needs to be made: const UINT aduiMessage = AdUiMessage();BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyComboBox, CAdUiComboBox)//{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyComboBox)...ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(aduiMessage, OnAdUiMessage)//}}AFX_MSG_MAPEND_MESSAGE_MAP()The new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyComboBox::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam){ UINT controlId = AdUiNotifyId(wParam); ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = AdUiNotification(wParam); ADUI_REPLY reply; reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam); if (!reply) reply = CAdUiComboBox::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam); return reply;}

Controls usually notify their parents when the need to be drawn, requesting a background color. The mechanism provides a handy spot for AdUi to acquire and subclass the child controls of a combobox. If m_bSubclassedControls is FALSE then the default routine proceeds as follows: The control requesting color is inspected to determine if it is an edit or a listbox.If the corresponding member (either m_pComboEBox or m_pComboLBox) is NULL then a default object is dynamically constructed and assigned; the related auto-delete flag will be set. The control is subclassed.m_bSubclassedControls is set TRUE when all required child controls have been subclassed, based on the combobox style. The routine returns the result of calling the inherited OnCtlColor() method. Returns the handle of a brush used to paint a control's background.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a DrawTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler ensures m_tipItem is valid, m_tipRect isn't empty and the control is actually owner-drawn. If so, then a WM_DRAWITEM request is processed by the control, using the relevant item, and drawing into the given DC.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a TextTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The control has the option of drawing the text, altering the device context attributes, etc. If the routine returns TRUE then the caller assumes the request was completely handled. Otherwise if the routine returns FALSE then the caller proceeds with default processing and renders the text on its own. By default, if m_tipItem is valid then the control will draw the text and return TRUE, otherwise the method just returns FALSE. The routine accounts for the selection state of the relevant item and adjusts the foreground and background colors appropriately.

This routine is called to determine the size and placement of a DrawTip or TextTip window. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text and determines if it entirely fits within the item's rectangle in the control. If so the routine returns FALSE, otherwise a tip rectangle that can encompass the entire text is calculated, placed over the relevant item's rectangle, and the routine returns TRUE. Returning FALSE or an empty rectangle indicates that no tip should be displayed.

This routine is called to query the control for the type of tip window it supports. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. A control can return one of the following codes: kAdUiReply_Nothing No tip window is required or supported by the control. kAdUiReply_DrawTip The control is owner-draw and supports an owner-draw text tip (such as a DrawTip). kAdUiReply_TextTip The control can support a TextTip. kAdUiReply_ToolTip The control requests a standard ToolTip. The default handler updates m_tipItem via a call to GetItemAtPoint(), passing the designated point. If a relevant item is found then the control requests a DrawTip if owner-draw and a TextTip otherwise.

This routine is called by the default AdUi Message handler to process tip text requests. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text (if any) and returns TRUE. On entry this routine usually receives an empty string. It's perfectly acceptable to simply return TRUE, indicating that the request was handled and that the control has no text to display. The result will be to suppress tip display. Returns TRUE if the request was handled, FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called to determine if the cursor position still pertains to the current tip displayed for the control. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler returns TRUE if the point lies within the relevant item's rectangle, and FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_MOUSEMOVE. To override this method, a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method. If the cursor position passed in differs from the point tracked in m_lastMousepoint, then a kAdUiNotify_UpdateTip notification is sent to the control's AdUi Parent window, informing it to update a tip window on behalf of the control (if necessary). Afterwards, m_lastMousePoint is updated with the given cursor position.

Call this method to specify an object to subclass the combobox's listbox control. The routine updates m_pComboLBox and m_bAutoDeleteLBox. Before assigning the new data members, the current listbox object will be automatically deleted if the current auto-delete setting is TRUE. In other words, this method will remove the current listbox object before updating with a new object. Passing NULL for the new control is allowed (the current control will just be removed). When a listbox control is assigned via a call to ListBox(), if the listbox control's AdUi Parent has not been set then the control will inherit the AdUi Parent of the combobox. When a new control is assigned it will not be immediately subclassed. The default override for OnCtlColor() handles this.

This class derives from CWnd. It provides functionality to host two controls separated by the splitter bar and takes care of resizing the hosted controls when they are resized using the splitter bar.
Given two CWnd pointers, this method hosts them in the coupled group with a splitter bar in between.
Returns true if the splitter is enabled, or false if it is not.
Gets the theme used by the group control.
Returns a double value that represents the current ratio between the top window and the whole window of the coupled group.

This function lets the caller set one of the two control windows in the group to be minimized. If bMinimized is true, the control pointed to by pWnd is set to be minimized, and the other control in the group is set to be maximized. If bMinimized is false, both windows are set to be maximized. The controls are redrawn during the next resizing event, such as a mouse drag or an OnSize() event.
Controls the display of the splitter control. The splitter control is displayed when bSplitterEnabled is set to true and hidden when it is set to false. The default value is true.
Sets the theme for the coupled group control to the current palette background color and draws the splitter control with the current border color.
Sets the top-to-whole coupled group control ratio, which controls the top and bottom window control sizes.

CAdUiDialog derives from CAdUiBaseDialog. The class provides a straightforward, general-purpose set of member functions that allow for sizable modal dialogs and persistent data storage by dialog. This dialog class provides functionality in three essential areas: resizing, coordinate persistency, and data persistency. CAdUiTabMainDialog and CAdUiTabChildDialog both derive from CAdUiDialog. See 'Built-In MFC User Interface Support' in the ObjectARX Developer's Guide for an explanation of the distinction between CAdUi and CAcUi classes.
This class is for the internal use of AutoCAD only and may be removed at any time. This class is essentially a straight port of CAdUiBaseDialog, except for the constructor.
Returns a pointer to AutoCAD's main window.
Returns a string identifying the root of AutoCAD's registry entries.
Constructs a CAdUiDialogBar object and enables or disables tool tips based on the AutoCAD TOOLTIPS system variable.

This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the control's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If it is not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present, then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (in other words, returns non-zero), then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (in other words, returns zero), then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general, zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. Example This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyComboBox : public CAdUiComboBox {...protected://{{AFX_MSG(CMyComboBox)...afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam);//}}AFX_MSGDECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP()};In the class implementation, a corresponding message map entry needs to be made: const UINT aduiMessage = AdUiMessage();BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyComboBox, CAdUiComboBox)//{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyComboBox)...ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(aduiMessage, OnAdUiMessage)//}}AFX_MSG_MAPEND_MESSAGE_MAP()The new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyComboBox::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam){ UINT controlId = AdUiNotifyId(wParam); ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = AdUiNotification(wParam); ADUI_REPLY reply; reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam); if (!reply) reply = CAdUiComboBox::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam); return reply;}

This function will dynamically add a control to the dialog. This function is only necessary when a developer is creating controls on the fly that are not part of the dialog resource template. If resizing is not an issue, the function should not be used. Since the dialog manager engine which handles moving and resizing controls uses the resource template as it's base for determining which controls will be handled, when a control is created programmatically the developer should inform the dialog manager. Initial control coordinates are seeded from the template therefore it is important that the dialog manager obtain the initial coordinates for every control attached to the dialog. When adding the control, a small amount (about fifty) bytes of memory are allocated on the global heap. If this allocation fails, then the AddControl function will return FALSE. If the control is going to be resized, make the Move/Stretch call immediately after the AddControl() call. Example: CWnd pSpecial; if (pSpecial.Create ('EDIT'...IDC_SPECIALEDIT...) == FALSE) return FALSE; // A control was just created, tell the base class about it. // AddControl(&pSpecial); // This control will 'float' with the dialog as it is resized // in both width and height // MoveControlXY ( IDC_SPECIALEDIT, 100, 100 );

The AutoLoad API provides a method that synchronizes a control that may be moved or resized as part of its base class. For instance, a bitmap button (CAdUiBitmapButton) is defined as an owner-draw control in the dialog template. The base class OnInitDialog will obtain the coordinates for this button and 'lock' them down as a baseline against which all control x/y deltas are applied. However, the control itself has a post-creation call that might adjust the size therefore skewing the coordinates recorded by the dialog manager. In the case of CAdUiBitmapButton, it adjusts its rectangle by the coordinates of the bitmap it is passed. AutoLoadControl does this by removing the original coordinates and persistency information from the registry and reapplying these values to the newly sized control. Returns TRUE if the control was valid and added to the dialog. Returns FALSE if pControl was invalid or if memory could not be allocated

This function will force a control to repaint. To avoid flicker, the dialog manager resizing engine queues controls for a one-time repainting using DeferWindowPos. In certain cases, especially when a descendant dialog is manipulating control coordinates itself or direct control graphic manipulation occurs (such as BitBlts or DrawTexts), it is necessary to ensure that a control gets properly invalidated. Returns TRUE if the pControl dialog control is valid for the dialog and the flag was successfully set. Returns FALSE if the either of these conditions fail.

This function will force a control's position and size. Whenever a control is manipulated, the dialog manager engine must be informed. Examples where ForceControlResize becomes useful is for such things as folding/unfolding dialogs or controls which are conditionally relocated at runtime.

This function retrieves the list view column sizes. List view column sizes are stored in the profile section of the registry under the dialog name that is initialized when calling SetDialogName under a special ListView-key unique to each control in the dialog. This should be called subsequent to the base class CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog call. When called successfully, the list view column widths previously visible when the user clicked OK are applied to the list view. Returns TRUE if the pList control is valid, the LVN_NOCOLUMNHEADER style bit is OFF, and the registry can be accessed. Returns FALSE if any of these conditions fails. Example: // A dialog called Layers contains a list view. We want the // list view column headers to be persistent across sessions. // void CMyLayerDialog::OnInitDialog ( ) { SetDialogName ('MyLayer'); CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog(); // Fix our list view values GetColumnSizes(GetDlgItem(IDC_LAYER_LISTVIEW)); ... return TRUE; } void CMyLayerDialog::OnOK() { SaveColumnSizes(GetDlgItem(IDC_LAYER_LISTVIEW)); CAdUiDialog::OnOK(); }

This routine returns a pointer to a CSize, representing the most recent elastic offsets calculated by the internal dialog manager. The values are typically recalculated when the window is re-sized and control positions are adjusted.

This function retrieves developer-defined settings associated with the dialog. The values can be set using the SetDialogData() member function. Returns TRUE if the value was successfully retrieved to the registry or FALSE otherwise. For example: VOID CMyDialog::OnInitDialog(){ SetDialogName('MyDialog'); CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog(); // Get profile values CAdUiCombo *combo = (CAdUiCombo*)GetDlgItem(IDC_SELECTOR); DWORD dwVal; GetDialogData('Selection',&dwVal); combo->SetCurSel(dwVal); GetDialogData('FullPartial',&dwVal); CheckDlgButton(IDC_FULLPARTIAL,dwVal);}VOID CMyDialog::OnOK(){ // Save off the default selection value of the combobox CAdUiCombo *combo = (CAdUiCombo*)GetDlgItem(IDC_SELECTOR); SetDialogData('Selection',combo->GetCurSel()); // Save off the status of full/partial checkbox SetDialogData('FullPartial',IsDlgButtonChecked(IDC_FULLPARTIAL));}
This function gets the help string tag for help file lookup for dialog level help (F1 HELP).
This function returns in the argument the dialog key used to access coordinate info in the registry.

This function allows the developer to inspect the dialog name that the CAdUiDialog would use when writing to the profile section of the registry. Generally, a developer would simply 'fix' a name by using the SetDialogName member function.
This method is called by the default OnGetMinMaxInfo() routine to obtain extents information.
This method is used to obtain access to the internal dialog manager object, or to test if it exists. Returns a pointer to an internal dialog manager object, or NULL if none exists.
This method obtains the display extents for the dialog from the registry.
This function causes the dialog to be locked at a given height. No resizing of the height is allowed.
This function causes the dialog to be locked at a given width. No resizing of the width is allowed.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's position upon resizing. The control will move in a lMovePct percentage of the delta. For example, a control whose X position in the dialog begins at 10 and whose lMovePct is defined as 100 will change to 20 when the dialog is resized by 10 pixels in width. In the same example, this control X coordinate will change to 15 if lMovePct is defined as 50. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's position upon resizing. The control will move in a lMovePct percentage of the delta in either the X or Y direction or both. This function combines the behavior of the MoveControlX and MoveControlY functions. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's position upon resizing. The control will move in a lMovePct percentage of the delta. For example, a control whose Y position in the dialog begins at 10 and whose lMovePct is defined as 100 will change to 20 when the dialog is resized by 10 pixels in height. In the same example, this control Y coordinate will change to 15 if lMovePct is defined as 50. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.
For internal use only. This override is called when the Cancel button is clicked or ESC key is pressed, and results in the dismissal of the dialog.
Called to process help when the F1 key is pressed. By default this method does nothing.

For internal use only. This method provides a MFC Message Map handler for WM_GETMINMAXINFO. If the dialog has been set to enable AdUi processing of resizing messages via the message map, then GetElasticMinMaxInfo() is called. The override also calls the inherited handler.
This method is called during the start of the default OnInitDialog(), prior to a call to the base class OnInitDialog(). This override prepares the dialog for resizing.
This method is called during the completion of the default OnInitDialog(), after a call to the base class OnInitDialog().This override does nothing.
For internal use only. In addition to calling the inherited method, this override also updates the registry with the dialog's current resizing state.
For internal use only. This override is called when the dialog is shown.

For internal use only. This method provides a MFC Message Map handler for WM_SIZE. If the dialog has been set to enable AdUi processing of resizing messages via the message map, then SetElasticSize() is called, passing a CSize constructed from cx and cy, and FALSE. The override also calls the inherited handler.

In the case of CAdUiBitmapButton, it adjusts its rectangle by the coordinates of the bitmap it is passed. This function saves the column widths for a given list view control to the profile section of the registry under the dialog name which is initialized when calling SetDialogName. A developer should make this call when dismissing the dialog on an OnOK. The values may be retrieved and applied via the GetColumnSizes() member function. We want the // list view column headers to be persistent across sessions. // void CMyLayerDialog::OnInitDialog ( ) { SetDialogName ('MyLayer'); CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog(); // Fix our list view values GetColumnSizes(GetDlgItem(IDC_LAYER_LISTVIEW)); ... return TRUE; } void CMyLayerDialog::OnOK() { SaveColumnSizes(GetDlgItem(IDC_LAYER_LISTVIEW)); CAdUiDialog::OnOK();}

This function is an alternative to making individual calls to StretchControlX, StretchControlY, MoveControlX, and MoveControlY. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. This function always returns TRUE. Use the DLGCTLINFO table from the dialogManager.h header file to define the table. For reference, the structure is defined as: typedef struct _dlgControlTag { DWORD id; DWORD flags; DWORD pct; } DLGCTLINFO, *PDLGCTLINFO; id The control ID. flags A bitwise flag combining one or more of the following:MOVEXMOVEYMOVEXYELASTICXELASTICYELASTICXY pct Percentage of the appropriate delta for either moving or resizing depending on the flag contents. Example: static DLGCTLINFO dcMenuGroup[] = { {IDC_STATIC1, ELASTICXY, 100}, {IDC_LIST_MLOAD, ELASTICXY, 100}, {IDC_GRP_UNLOAD, MOVEX, 100 }, {IDC_EDIT_MLOAD, ELASTICX|MOVEY, 100}, {IDC_GRP_REP_ALL, MOVEXY, 100}, {IDC_MENU_LOAD, MOVEXY, 100}, {IDC_GRP_BROWSE, MOVEXY, 100}, {IDC_STATIC2, MOVEY, 100}, {IDC_STATIC3, ELASTICX | MOVEY, 100},};void CAsdkDialog::OnInitDialog (){ SetDialogName('Asdk:SampleDialog'); CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog(); // .... other stuff SetControlProperty (&dcDlgCtls, sizeof(dcDlgCtls)/sizeof(DLGCTLINFO)); // .... other stuff return TRUE;}

This function saves developer-defined settings associated with the dialog. The values can be retrieved using the GetDialogData() member function. If the value name valueName or key does not exist, it will be created. Returns TRUE if the value was successfully written to the registry or FALSE otherwise. For example: VOID CMyDialog::OnInitDialog(){ SetDialogName('MyDialog'); CAdUiDialog::OnInitDialog(); // Get profile values CAdUiCombo *combo = (CAdUiCombo*)GetDlgItem(IDC_SELECTOR); DWORD dwVal; GetDialogData('Selection',&dwVal); combo->SetCurSel(dwVal); GetDialogData('FullPartial',&dwVal); CheckDlgButton(IDC_FULLPARTIAL,dwVal);}VOID CMyDialog::OnOK(){ // Save off the default selection value of the combobox CAdUiCombo *combo = (CAdUiCombo*)GetDlgItem(IDC_SELECTOR); SetDialogData('Selection',combo->GetCurSel()); // Save off the status of full/partial checkbox SetDialogData('FullPartial',IsDlgButtonChecked(IDC_FULLPARTIAL));}
This function sets the help string tag for help file lookup for dialog level help (F1 HELP).

This function sets the maximum size that a dialog can be resized to. Generally, there will be no need to call this function. The dialog's maximum extents are, by default, obtained from the maximum extents defined by the values GetSystemMetrics() returns when passed system constants SM_CXSCREEN and SM_CYSCREEN.

This function sets the minimum size that a dialog can be resized to. Generally, there will be no need to call this function. The dialog's minimum extents are, by default, the size obtained from the dialog resource template.

This function sets the name of your dialog in the registry. You must make this unique (in other words, use your registered developer prefix as a portion of the name), since it will use a shared area of the user profile registry space. Given that developers usually create their applications using the registered developer prefix, the following method is recommended: module-name:dialog-name For example, if your ARX application is named AsdkSample and you have a dialog entitled 'Coordinates', you would name it AsdkSample:Coordinates, notCoordinates.
This routine is intended to be called as a helper to OnSize().
This function will turn on or off persistency for the dialog. Persistency means the storage of developer defined dialog information to the profile section of the registry.
This function allows the dialog to set up the application root key to be able to save persistency information later.
Call this routine as needed to update the parent's internal dialog manager with new information regarding a tab control's size.
This member is used to write persistent dialog data to the registry. The default OnOK() handler calls this routine. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE otherwise.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's size upon dialog resizing. The control will resize in a lElasticPct percentage of the delta. For example, a control whose width is 100 pixels and whose lElasticPct is defined as 100 will change to 150 when the dialog is resized by 50 pixels in width. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's size upon dialog resizing. The control will resize in a lMovePct percentage of the delta in either the X or Y direction or both. This function combines the behavior of the MoveControlX and MoveControlY functions. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.

This function allows setting the behavior of a control's size upon dialog resizing. The control will resize in a lElasticPct percentage of the delta. For example, a control whose height is 100 pixels and whose lElasticPct is defined as 100 will change to 150 when the dialog is resized by 50 pixels in height. This function call is generally made in a dialog's OnInitDialog member function. Returns TRUE if the id is valid, FALSE otherwise.

Called by the docking system before the context menu of the control bar is displayed, to give you the opportunity to add your own menu options, and/or to remove the existing default menu options. There are two default menu options: ID_ADUI_ALLOWDOCK: (Value 1). This command allows the user to enable/disable the docking capability of the control bar. If disabled, the control bar is made floating and cannot be docked. ID_ADUI_HIDEBAR: (Value 2). This command hides the control bar, or closes it if the flag ADUI_DOCK_DESTROY_ON_CLOSE is set when you construct your control bar. Make sure that the custom options you will add to the context menu will not have one of the two values above.
Called to change the height of the bar when docked. This applieas when multiples dialogs are ebing docked to the same vertical space.

Returns the state of the Allow docking menu item for a CAdUiDockControlBar. This state corresponds to the users ability to dock the control bar by double clicking on title bar or dragging to frame edge (on or off).
Indicates whether the control bar is anchored.
Checks the internal state of the control bar object. This function is compiled only in debug mode (with the _DEBUG macro defined).

This is the class constructor. It takes a parameter that can be a combination of the following values: ADUI_DOCK_CS_STDMOUSECLICKS: If set, this flag instructs the control bar to display a default context menu when the user right-clicks on the control bar. You can also add your own options to this menu. If not set, no context menu will appear by default. ADUI_DOCK_CS_DESTROY_ON_CLOSE: If set, the control bar is destroyed when the user closes it. The default behavior is to hide the control bar.
Override of a base class method. See the Microsoft documentation for the CControlBar class for details.

Called by the docking system when the frame window asks to get the focus back. The default implementation returns false, leaving the focus to the control bar. If your control bar returns true from this call, the frame window will take the focus.
Alternate method to create the control bar window.

Called by the docking system during the control bar creation process. You will override this method if you want to create additional elements in your control bar. The default implementation creates a close button that allows the user the hide the control bar.
This method is an alternative to RestoreControlBar(). You will use this method instead if you do not want that the docking system to handle the size, position, and state of your control bar.
Call this method after the creation of the control bar, to set its docking capabilities.

This method returns the current docking style. The possible return values are: Value Meaning 0 No flags - the control bar will not dock CBRS_ALIGN_TOP Allows docking at the top of the client area CBRS_ALIGN_BOTTOM Allows docking at the bottom of the client area CBRS_ALIGN_LEFT Allows docking on the left side of the client area CBRS_ALIGN_RIGHT Allows docking on the right side of the client area CBRS_ALIGN_ANY Allows docking on any side of the client area CBRS_FLOAT_MULTI Allows multiple control bars to be floated in a single mini-frame window

Called by the docking system to let you set a minimum size for the control bar. When the control bar is in a floating state, these values will be used as constraints when the user attempts to resize the frame.
Retrieves the current size and position of a control bar.
This is GetHorzDockSize, a member of class CAdUiDockControlBar.
Returns the cached docking rectangle that persists in the fixed profile across AutoCAD sessions.
Returns the cached floating rectangle that persists in the fixed profile across AutoCAD sessions.
Returns the width and height of the title bar.
Retrieves the class ID identifying a control bar.

Retrieves the rectangle reserved for your window inside the control bar area. This rectangle is the equivalent of the control bar client area, minus the space occupied by the bar handle, close button, and margins.
This is GetVertDockSize, a member of class CAdUiDockControlBar.

Initialize the floating size and position of the control bar. You will not need to call this method if you restore your control bar using the method RestoreControlBar(), which will take care of the floating position for you.
Indicates the state of the control bar. Returns TRUE if the control bar is floating, FALSE if it is docked.

Handler for the WM_COMMAND message, associated with the ID_ADUI_ALLOWDOCK command. You will handle this message if you want to do add specific processing to the 'Allow Docking' command. The default processing change the internal flag giving docking rights. If the control bar is docked and the docking state becomes not allowed by this command, the control bar is undocked. Call the CAdUiDockControlBar implementation of you implement this handler.

Called by the docking system when the user requests the control bar to be anchored. You can override this method to perform additional work when anchoring the control bar. If you override this method, make sure to call the base class OnAnchor() method to complete the handling of this event.

Called by the docking system when the user requests the control bar to be anchored on the left. You can override this method to perform additional work when anchoring the control bar on the left. If you override this method, make sure to call the base class OnAnchorLeft() method to complete the handling of this event.

Called by the docking system when the user requests the control bar to be anchored on the right. You can override this method to perform additional work when anchoring the control bar on the right. If you override this method, make sure to call the base class OnAnchorRight() method to complete the handling of this event.

Called by the docking system when the user requested the control bar to be hidden or closed. You can override this method to perform additional work when hiding or closing the control bar. If you override this method make sure to call CAdUiDockControlBar::OnClosing() to perform a correct hiding or closing of the control bar.

Handler for the WM_COMMAND message. The default implementation handles this message to get the click on the control bar close button. You don't need to handle this message since the default implementation calls the virtual method OnClosing() that you can override.

Handler for the WM_CONTEXTMENU message. You don't need to handle this message since the default implementation triggers the virtual method AddCustomMenuItems() that you can override to customize the default contextual menu.

Handler for the WM_CREATE message. The default processing passes the pointer to the inherited method and, if successful, passes it to CreateControlBar(). Call the CAdUiDockControlBar implementation if you implement this handler.
Handler for the WM_ERASEBKGND message. The CAdUiDockControlBar implementation fills the client rectangle with the COLOR_BTNFACE system color

Handler for the WM_COMMAND message, associated with the ID_ADUI_HIDEBAR command. You will handle this message if you want to do a specific processing of the 'Hide command. Call the CAdUiDockControlBar implementation if you implement this handler.

Handler for the WM_PAINT message. You don't need to handle this message since the default implementation triggers the virtual method PaintControlBar() that you can override to customize the appearance of the control bar.
Handler for the WM_SETTINGCHANGE message. The default implementation handles this message to update the size of the window.

Called by the docking system when the user is resizing the floating control bar. Overriding this method allows the developer to control this size. This method is called in response to the Windows message WM_SIZING.
Handler for the WM_WINDOWPOSCHANGED message. You don't need to handle this message since the default implementation triggers the virtual method SizeChanged() in which you can handle this event.
Called by the docking system whenever it is necessary to repaint the control bar. You will override this method if you want to customize the look of your control bar.

This method takes care of restoring the control bar to the on screen position in the previous session. This is the preferred method to set the state of a control bar. If the control bar is created for the first time, then the parameter indicates where the control should be docked. By default, it is docked on the left side of the framework. This method will also recognize the floating position if the control bar was floating when the last session ended.

Sets the state of the Allow docking menu item for a CAdUiDockControlBar. This state corresponds to the users ability to dock the control bar by double clicking on title bar or dragging to frame edge (on or off).
This is SetHorzDockSize, a member of class CAdUiDockControlBar.
Sets the theme to be used.

Sets the identifier associated with a control bar. Since a control identifier needs to be unique, class IDs are used for that purpose. You can generate a class ID using the system utility GUIDGEN. A good place to call this method is right after you called the Create() method. It must be called before RestoreControlBar() because the persistency system relies on the control bar IDs.
This is SetVertDockSize, a member of class CAdUiDockControlBar.

Called by the docking system whenever the size or the state of the control bar has changed. The default implementation does nothing. You have to override this method in order to get your window to fit inside the control bar. The flags parameter may be any combination of the following: ADUI_DOCK_NF_SIZECHANGED The size has changed. ADUI_DOCK_NF_STATECHANGED The state has changed from docked to floating or vice-versa. ADUI_DOCK_NF_FRAMECHANGED The geometry of the frame containing the control bar has changed.
Virtual method that receives the theme modification event.
Calling this method provokes all the control bars docked on a same row to be resized to the same size. If the control bar is the only one in its row, this call has no effect.

This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method cleans up all the internal data that have been allocated during the creation and through the execution of the control bar code.
This class is for the internal use of AutoCAD only and may be removed at any time.
This is the class constructor. It initializes m_bZOrderChanged to false.
Returns a Boolean value indicating whether AutoCAd can take focus away from this frame.
Returns a Boolean value indicating whether this frame can take focus.
Returns the type of the bar contained within this frame.

CAdUiDrawTipText is used internally by the AdUi messaging system to inform a control that a TextTip needs re-painting. The control has the option of changing attributes of the tip window's device context, drawing the text, etc.
This is the class constructor. The constructor initializes all of the data members from the supplied arguments.
This class specializes CAdUiBitmapStatic to provide buttons that enable Static Display by default.
This is the class constructor. It enables Drag & Drop by setting m_bEnableDragDrop to TRUE.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. By default it does nothing.

This class specializes CEdit to provide an edit control that supports AdUi Messaging. The class may be used anywhere a CEdit may be used. Since it provides the additional container-side support for AdUi registered messages, CAdUiBaseDialog (or a derived class) is recommended for use with CAdUiEdit.
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler will process the following notifications/requests: kAdUiNotify_GetTipSupport lParam is treated as a pointer to a CPoint containing the cursor's current position on the display and passed to OnGetTipSupport(). The reply from OnGetTipSupport() is returned. kAdUiNotify_GetTipText Routes the request to OnGetTipText(), treating lParam as a pointer to a CString that will receive tip text. If OnGetTipText() returns TRUE then DoAdUiMessage() returns kAdUiReply_Ok otherwise kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. kAdUiNotify_GetTipRect lParam is a pointer to a CRect to receive display co-ordinates for the tip window, passed to OnGetTipRect(). If OnGetTipRect() returns TRUE then the handler returns kAdUiReply_Ok, else kAdUiReply_Nothing. kAdUiNotify_HitTipRect lParam is a pointer to a CPoint containing the cursor's current position on the display, and is passed to OnHitTipRect(). If OnHitTipRect() returns TRUE then the handler returns kAdUiReply_Ok, else kAdUiReply_Nothing. kAdUiNotify_DrawTip lParam is treated as a pointer to a CDC and passed to OnDrawTip(). The routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok if the pointer is not NULL and kAdUiReply_Nothing otherwise. kAdUiNotify_DrawTipText lParam is treated as a pointer to a CAdUiDrawTipText and passed to OnDrawTipText(). The routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok if the pointer is not NULL and OnDrawTipText() returned TRUE, otherwise kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. All other requests are ignored and return kAdUiReply_Nothing.

This member gets the container CWnd to which the control should forward AdUi notifications and requests. It returns the window tracked by m_aduiParent or, if that member is NULL, returns the control's parent window.

This method is called to obtain content extents for DrawTips. The routine determines the extents of a string in the control. This method may be overridden in derived classes, allowing fonts to be swapped or adjustments to be made to the returned values. The default routine calls the GetTextExtent() method, passing the given text, width, and height parameters.
This routine is called to inspect the style mask. Returns the contents of m_styleMask.
This routine determines the extents of a string in the control, based on the control's current font.
This routine is called to test the bits in the style mask. Returns TRUE if all bits in the mask are set in m_styleMask, FALSE otherwise.

This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the control's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (it returns non-zero) then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (it returns zero) then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general, zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. Example: This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration, an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyEdit: public CAdUiListCtrl {protected://{{AFX_MSG(CMyEdit)afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam);//}}AFX_MSGDECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP()};In the class implementation, a corresponding message map entry also needs to be made: const UINT aduiMessage = AdUiMessage();BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyEdit, CAdUiListCtrl)//{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyEdit)ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(aduiMessage, OnAdUiMessage)//}}AFX_MSG_MAPEND_MESSAGE_MAP()Of course, the new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyListCtrl::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam){ UINT controlId = AdUiNotifyId(wParam); ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = AdUiNotification(wParam); ADUI_REPLY reply; reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam); if (!reply) reply = CAdUiEdit::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam); return reply;}

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a DrawTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler does nothing, since owner-draw list controls repaint an entire row at a time and not just individual sub-items. A derived class could override this method to inspect m_tipItem and m_tipIndex and render an appropriate tip.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a TextTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The control has the option of drawing the text, altering the device context attributes, etc. If the routine returns TRUE then the caller assumes the request was completely handled. Otherwise if the routine returns FALSE then the caller proceeds with default processing and renders the text on its own. By default, if m_tipItem is valid then the control will draw the text and return TRUE, otherwise the method just returns FALSE. The routine accounts for the selection state of the relevant item and adjusts the foreground and background colors appropriately.

This routine is called to determine the size and placement of a DrawTip or TextTip window. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text and determines if it entirely fits within the item's rectangle in the control. If so the routine returns FALSE, otherwise a tip rectangle that can encompass the entire text is calculated, placed over the relevant item's rectangle, and the routine returns TRUE. Returning FALSE or an empty rectangle indicates that no tip should be displayed.

This routine is called to query the control for the type of tip window it supports. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. A control can return one of the following codes: kAdUiReply_Nothing No tip window is required or supported by the control. kAdUiReply_DrawTip The control is owner-draw and supports an owner-draw text tip (such as a DrawTip). kAdUiReply_TextTip The control can support a TextTip. kAdUiReply_ToolTip The control requests a standard ToolTip. The default handler updates m_tipItem via a call to GetItemAtPoint(), passing the designated point. If a relevant item is found then the control requests a DrawTip if owner-draw and a TextTip otherwise.

This routine is called by the default AdUi Message handler to process tip text requests. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text (if any) and returns TRUE. On entry this routine usually receives an empty string. It's perfectly acceptable to simply return TRUE, indicating that the request was handled and that the control has no text to display. The result will be to suppress tip display. Returns TRUE if the request was handled, FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called to determine if the cursor position still pertains to the current tip displayed for the control. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler returns TRUE if the point lies within the control's client area, and FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_MOUSEMOVE. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method. If the cursor position passed in differs from the point tracked in m_lastMousepoint, then a kAdUiNotify_UpdateTip notification is sent to the control's AdUi Parent window, informing it to update a tip window on behalf of the control (if necessary). Afterwards, m_lastMousePoint is updated with the given cursor position.
This member sets the container CWnd to which the control should forward AdUi notifications and requests. Calling the method updates m_aduiParent.
This routine is called to assign a validation style mask. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler assigns the value to m_styleMask.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

CAdUiFileDialog specializes CFileDialog much the same way as CAdUiBaseDialog specializes CDialog. The class provides basic support for tip windows (ToolTips and TextTips) and AdUi message handling in a common file dialog. With the exception of the constructor and the following methods, refer to CAdUiBaseDialog for documentation, substituting CAdUiFileDialog and CFileDialog in references to CAdUiBaseDialog and CDialog. The following CAdUiBaseDialog methods are not provided in this class: Create(), DisplayData(), DoDialogHelp(), EnableMultiDocumentActivation(), ExchangeData(), IsMultiDocumentActivationEnabled(), SetAppRootKey(), and ValidateData().
This method is called to obtain a pointer to the application's main window. By default this is AfxGetApp()->m_pMainWnd.
By default this routine returns the handle of the resource provider that was in effect when the AdUi DLL was loaded (as determined by AfxGetResourceInstance()).
By default, this method returns m_rootKey and is initially NULL. A derived constructor or an override for this method should set m_rootKey to a value appropriate to the application.
Call this method to indicate an AutoCAd interactive command is starting. Example: BeginEditorCommand(); if (DoMyInteractiveCommand()) CompleteEditorCommand(); else CancelEditorCommand();

Constructs a CAdUiFileDialog object. This routine constructs a file dialog, passing arguments to the base class constructor. AdUi initialization performed is similar to the CAdUiBaseDialog constructor.

Call this method upon returning from an interactive command that was canceled in the Drawing Editor. This function is intended for use only after a call to BeginEditorCommand(). This routine sets the command state to kAdUiCommand_canceled and then calls the dialog's OnCancel() method to terminate the dialog. Example: BeginEditorCommand(); if (DoMyInteractiveCommand()) CompleteEditorCommand(); else CancelEditorCommand();

Call this method upon return from an interactive command that was completed in the Drawing Editor. This method is intended for use after a a call to BeginEditorCommand(). This routine restores the dialog and sets the command state to kAdUiCommand_Completed. Example: BeginEditorCommand(); if (DoMyInteractiveCommand()) CompleteEditorCommand(); else CancelEditorCommand();

Called to process help when the F1 key is pressed. This override examines the dialog's help tag, and if empty returns FALSE, indicating the event was not processed. Otherwise OnDialogHelp() is called and this routine returns TRUE.

This method returns the result of calling the inherited DoModal() routine. Prior to calling the inherited method, document switching and floating windows are disabled, and an alternate dialog resource instance (if any) is swapped in. Afterwards resources are restored and document switching and floating windows may be re-enabled.

Call this method to determine if an interactive command was canceled in the Drawing Editor. This is useful when a dialog runs a sub-dialog, which in turn runs a command. If the sub-dialog's command was canceled and the sub-dialog terminated the calling dialog will probably want to terminate as well. Returns TRUE if the last interactive command was canceled, FALSE otherwise. Example: CMyDialog subDialog; subDialog.DoModal(); if (subDialog.EditorCommandcanceled()) OnCancel();

This routine is provided to notify the application if floating windows (non-modal windows) should be enabled or disabled. Calls to this routine are expected to be cumulative (in other words, two calls in succession that pass FALSE must be matched with two calls that pass TRUE for floating windows to be re-enabled). By default, this routine does nothing.

This function is used to find the full path of the context help file for the application given a base name. It simply calls AdUiFindContextHelpFullPath, which uses the OS search path to find the file. Override this to use a different search path. Returns TRUE if full path found.
Returns the context help file name.
Returns the full path to the context help file.
Returns the 4 character context help prefix
This function gets the help string tag for help file lookup for dialog level help (F1 HELP).
Returns the icon assocciated with this dialog.
Called to retrieve the name assigned by the SetDialogName member function.
Call this method to inspect the setting of m_bUseTips. The method returns TRUE if tip windows are allowed and FALSE otherwise.
Call this method to restore or hide the dialog and any parent dialogs.

This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the control's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (i.e. returns non-zero) then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (i.e. returns zero) then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. Example This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyComboBox : public CAdUiComboBox {...protected://{{AFX_MSG(CMyComboBox)...afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam);//}}AFX_MSGDECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP()};In the class implementation, a corresponding message map entry needs to be made: const UINT aduiMessage = AdUiMessage();BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyComboBox, CAdUiComboBox)//{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyComboBox)...ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(aduiMessage, OnAdUiMessage)//}}AFX_MSG_MAPEND_MESSAGE_MAP()The new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyComboBox::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam){ UINT controlId = AdUiNotifyId(wParam); ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = AdUiNotification(wParam); ADUI_REPLY reply; reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam); if (!reply) reply = CAdUiComboBox::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam); return reply;}
This MFC-defined routine returns the handle of a brush used to paint a control's background. This override currently returns the value obtained by calling the inherited method.
Called to process help when the F1 key is pressed. By default this method does nothing.
This is an override for the MFC context help handler that specializes context help. It also provides an alternative to MFC dialog level help (F1 help).

This MFC-defined method is called during dialog initialization. The default handler calls OnInitDialogBegin(), then the inherited OnInitDialog() and then OnInitDialogFinish(). If tips are allowed then the tip windows are created via a call to SetUseTips(). If m_hIcon is NULL then a default icon is loaded (i.e. the first icon found in the application's executable file). The method returns the value returned from the call to the inherited OnInitDialog(), which is normally TRUE to allow Windows to set focus to the first control in the dialog or FALSE if the routine sets focus to some other control.

This method is called during the start of the default OnInitDialog(), prior to a call to the base class OnInitDialog(). The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default routine does nothing.

This method is called during the completion of the default OnInitDialog(), after a call to the base class OnInitDialog(). The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default routine does nothing.

This method is provided to handle a notification that a control has changed, outside of the usual Windows or MFC framework. In AdUi, edit controls will notify their AdUi containers when their contents change using this mechanism (similar to sending EN_CHANGE). Derived controls can be made to explicitly notify their containers by calling AdUiNotify() passing the container, kAdUiNotify_ControlChange, the control's ID and an optional lParam. By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

A dialog receives this notification when an AdUi control determines that it has transitioned from containing valid data to non-valid, or vice-versa. Derived controls can be made to explicitly notify their containers by calling AdUiNotify() passing the container, kAdUiNotify_Valid or kAdUiNotifyNotValid and the control's ID (pass zero for lParam). By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

This method is provided to handle a generic, application-defined notification. By default, the dialog does nothing and replies kAdUiNotify_Nothing. The method should return a reply appropriate to the application. By convention, kAdUiReply_Nothing usually indicates the notification was ignored, while kAdUiReply_Ok indicates it was handled.

Typically, when an AdUi control detects the cursor moving over the control, it sends tip update notifications to its AdUi container. By default, a dialog will respond by determinig if tips are enabled and if so, querying the control for the type of tip that should be displayed. If the control requests a TextTip or a DrawTip then the dialog's m_pTextTip is given a chance to update and the routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok; otherwise any currently displayed TextTip or DrawTip is hidden and kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned.

This method processes TTN_NEEDTEXT notifications (for example, requests for Common Control ToolTip text). The default handler determines the control for which text is needed and queries the control for the type of tip supports. If the control requests a ToolTip then the text is obtained from the control. Finally, if the control acknowledges the text request and returns a non-empty string, then a ToolTip is displayed, presenting the text, and the routine returns TRUE. Otherwise, the method returns FALSE.
This MFC-defined method is called after the window has been destroyed. The default method calls SetUseTips(), passing FALSE, to de-allocate any text or tool tip windows.
This routine returns the result of calling the inherited method, after re-establishing any resources that may have been swapped out by DoModal() or Create().

This MFC-defined method is called to alter a message prior to dispatching it to TranslateMessage(). The default handler activates the ToolTip (for example, m_pToolTip, if not NULL) and relays the message to the tip. The value returned by the call to the inherited PreTranslatMessage() is returned, which is normally TRUE if the message was translated and should not be dispatched or FALSE if the message was not translated and should be dispatched.
Sets the context help file name.
Sets the full path for the context help file.
Sets the 4 character help prefix for this class
This function sets the help string tag for help file lookup for dialog level help (F1 HELP).
Set the icon for this dialog.
This function assigns a name to the dialog. If a help tag has not been specified then this name will be used as the help tag.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. By default it does nothing.

CAdUiGroupCtrl class is ownerdrawin group control class that has a header on the top with a title, bitmap buttons and chevron button. Chevron button when clicked, minimizes or maximizes the control. This control can host a CWnd control in the client region. Bitmap button can be used to display different views in the CWnd in the client region or display a different window.

This method adds bitmap buttons to the group control header, specifying the bitmap name, callback function pointer, and tooltip. It returns a cookie to the caller, which can be used to delete the bitmap button. The callback function is defined in the following typedef: typedef void (*AdUiBmpBtnFcnPtr)(CWnd*);The AdUiBmpBtnFcnPtr() method is a function pointer that a client needs to implement for each of the header buttons. This method is called when its corresponding header button is clicked. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Method to add window and its title to the group control. This method can be called n number of times to add n windows.
Returns the integer value of the group control header height.
Returns true if the group control's header is hidden, or false if it is shown.
Returns true if the group control is currently minimized, or false if it is maxmized.
Returns the index of the window that is currently displayed in the group control.
Returns a DWORD indicating the current window style of the group control.
Gets the theme used by the group control.
Returns the title for the group control.
Adds or removes styles on the group control.
This method removes a button from the header of the group control. Returns true if the button is deleted; otherwise, returns false.
Sets the font style to bold and calls the CWnd base class SetFont() method. Also calls SetFont() on all the child windows that are added to the group control.
Sets the height for the group control's header. The default value for the height is 18 pixels.
Controls the display of the group control's header.
Sets the minimized or maximized state of the group control.

Sets the window selection currently displayed in the group control. When adding multiple windows to the group control, clients can control the window that is currently displayed by setting a different index.
Sets the window style for the group control.
Sets the theme for the group control based on the theme that is passed in.
Sets the title for the group control.
Sets whether the group control uses the dialog theme (also known as the light theme) or the current palette theme.
Displays the window represented by the input CWnd pointer in the client area of the group control. Returns true if successful; otherwise, returns false.
Returns whether the current group control uses the dialog theme (also known as the light theme) or the current palette theme.

This class specializes CHeaderCtrl to provide a control that supports AdUi Messaging. The class may be used anywhere a CHeaderCtrl may be used. Most often, CAdUiHeaderCtrl represents the sub-classed header contained in a list control (CAdUiListCtrl).
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE. m_tipItem will be set to -1.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler will process the kAdUiNotify_GetToolText request/notification, which routes the request to OnGetToolText(), treating lParam as a pointer to a CString that will receive the tool text. If OnGetToolText() returns TRUE, then DoAdUiMessage() returns kAdUiReply_Ok. Otherwise, kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. All other requests are ignored and return kAdUiReply_Nothing. Returns a reply code appropriate to notifyCode. In general, kAdUiReply_Nothing indicates the message was ignored, and kAdUiReply_Ok indicates the message was handled.

This member gets the container CWnd to which the control should forward AdUi notifications and requests. It returns the window tracked by m_aduiParent or, if that member is NULL, returns the control's parent window.

This method is called to obtain content extents for DrawTips. The routine determines the extents of a string in the control, based on an item index and some text. This method may be overridden in derived classes, allowing fonts to be swapped or adjustments to be made to the returned values. This method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages via the control's message map. If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (i.e. returns non-zero) then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (i.e. returns zero) then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a DrawTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler ensures m_tipItem is valid, m_tipRect isn't empty and the control is actually owner-drawn. If so, then a WM_DRAWITEM request is processed by the control, using the relevant item, and drawing into the given DC.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a TextTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The control has the option of drawing the text, altering the device context attributes, etc. If the routine returns TRUE then the caller assumes the request was completely handled. Otherwise if the routine returns FALSE then the caller proceeds with default processing and renders the text on its own. By default, if m_tipItem is valid then the control will draw the text and return TRUE, otherwise the method just returns FALSE. The routine accounts for the selection state of the relevant item and adjusts the foreground and background colors appropriately.

This routine is called to determine the size and placement of a DrawTip or TextTip window. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text and determines if it entirely fits within the item's rectangle in the control. If so the routine returns FALSE, otherwise a tip rectangle that can encompass the entire text is calculated, placed over the relevant item's rectangle, and the routine returns TRUE. Returning FALSE or an empty rectangle indicates that no tip should be displayed.

This routine is called to query the control for the type of tip window it supports. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler updates m_tipItem via a call to GetItemAtPoint(), passing the designated point. If a relevant item is found then the control requests a DrawTip if owner-draw and a TextTip otherwise.

This routine is called by the default AdUi Message handler to process tip text requests. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. It's perfectly acceptable to simply return TRUE, indicating that the request was handled and that the control has no text to display. The result will be to suppress tip display. Returns TRUE if the request was handled, FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called to determine if the cursor position still pertains to the current tip displayed for the control. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler returns TRUE if the point lies within the relevant item's rectangle, and FALSE otherwise.

This class specializes CListBox to provide a control that supports AdUi Messaging. The class may be used anywhere a CListBox may be used. Since it provides the additional container-side support for AdUi registered messages, CAdUiBaseDialog (or a derived class) is recommended for use with CAdUiListBox. CAdUiListBox provides features that allow the class to be used to sub-class a listbox included in a combobox (such as a ComboLBox). When used in concert with a CAdUiComboBox the listbox is able to track the combobox and, in the case of an owner-draw control, either delegate drawing to the combobox or provide its own drawing routines.
This is the class constructor. A new object will have all members initialized to zero or FALSE. The member m_tipItem will be set to -1 and m_bComboBoxDraw will be set TRUE.

Otherwise the default handler simply returns zero. Returns the relative position of the two items described in the COMPAREITEMSTRUCT structure.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_DELETEITEM. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. Otherwise the default handler does nothing.

This virtual method is provided to handle AdUi registered messages. Override DoAdUiMessage() to provide your own processing and/or call the inherited method. The default handler will process the following notifications/requests: kAdUiNotify_GetTipSupport lParam is treated as a pointer to a CPoint containing the cursor's current position on the display and passed to OnGetTipSupport(). The reply from OnGetTipSupport() is returned. kAdUiNotify_GetTipText Routes the request to OnGetTipText(), treating lParam as a pointer to a CString that will receive tip text. If OnGetTipText() returns TRUE then DoAdUiMessage() returns kAdUiReply_Ok otherwise kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. kAdUiNotify_GetTipRect lParam is a pointer to a CRect to receive display co-ordinates for the tip window, passed to OnGetTipRect(). If OnGetTipRect() returns TRUE then the handler returns kAdUiReply_Ok, else kAdUiReply_Nothing. kAdUiNotify_HitTipRect lParam is a pointer to a CPoint containing the cursor's current position on the display, and is passed to OnHitTipRect(). If OnHitTipRect() returns TRUE then the handler returns kAdUiReply_Ok, else kAdUiReply_Nothing. kAdUiNotify_DrawTip lParam is treated as a pointer to a CDC and passed to OnDrawTip(). The routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok if the pointer is not NULL and kAdUiReply_Nothing otherwise. kAdUiNotify_DrawTipText lParam is treated as a pointer to a CAdUiDrawTipText and passed to OnDrawTipText(). The routine returns kAdUiReply_Ok if the pointer is not NULL and OnDrawTipText() returned TRUE, otherwise kAdUiReply_Nothing is returned. All other requests are ignored and return kAdUiReply_Nothing.

This is an MFC-defined handler for Owner-Draw paint requests. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler creates a device context in memory and selects the button's font into the DC. The DC uses a bitmap equivalent in size to the button's window rectangle. To actually draw the button the virtual member DrawButton() is called. When DrawButton() returns the bitmap in memory is copied to the drawing device context and the button's font is selected out of the DC.

This method draws the frame for a normal three-dimensional pushbutton. If isDefault is TRUE a black border will surround the frame and the frame's rectangle will be shrunk one pixel from each side. If isSelected is TRUE then the frame is drawn as if the button is pressed, and raised otherwise.

This method draws the frame for a Tool Style three-dimensional pushbutton. If isSelected is TRUE then the frame is drawn as if the button is pressed, appearing slightly sunken. Otherwise, if isFocused is TRUE then the frame is drawn as if the button is in focus or pointed at, appearing slightly raised. Otherwise a flat frame is drawn.

This method draws a bitmap in the given device context. The pixel at the upper-left corner of the bitmap is used as a mask color. Pixels in the bitmap that differ from the mask color will replace those in the DC; masked pixels are ignored. If isDisabled is TRUE then non-masked pixels will all be drawn gray in the DC.

This function is used to inspect the button's FastDraw setting. While the setting is enabled, the default DrawItem() routine will create a device context in-memory and draw to it, then copy the results to the DC it would normally draw to (usually the display). The technique usually results in faster output and reduced flicker. If the FastDraw setting is enabled then the method will return TRUE, otherwise FALSE.

Call this function to inspect the button's PointedAt Effects setting. The term PointedAt Effects refers to the manner in which the button reacts when the mouse moves over the control. While enabled, IsPointedAt(), OnMouseMove(), OnPointedAt() and OnTimer all participate in providing effects. If PointedAt Effects are enabled, this function will return TRUE, otherwise FALSE.

This function is used to inspect the button Static Display setting. If the Static Display setting is enabled then the first method will return TRUE, otherwise FALSE.
This function is used to inspect the button Tool Display setting. If the Tool Display setting is enabled then it will return TRUE, otherwise FALSE.
