If you need to override the default processing then add a handler for AdUiMessage() in your derived class's message map. The default handler inspects the control ID encoded in wParam. If not zero and a child control corresponding to the ID is present then the message is forwarded to the control. If the child control handles the message (i.e. returns non-zero) then the reply from the child control is returned. Otherwise, if the child control does not exist or ignores the message (i.e. returns zero) then the reply from the button's DoAdUiMessage() is returned. Returns a reply code appropriate to the message. In general zero indicates the message was ignored and non-zero indicates the message was handled. Example This example illustrates some of the steps needed to override OnAdUiMessage in a derived class. In the class declaration an entry in the message map needs to be added, as follows: class CMyButton : public CAdUiOwnerDrawButton {...protected://{{AFX_MSG(CMyButton)...afx_msg LONG OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam);//}}AFX_MSGDECLARE_MESSAGE_MAP()};In the class implementation a corresponding message map entry also needs to be made: const UINT AdUiMessage = AdUiMessage();BEGIN_MESSAGE_MAP(CMyButton, CAdUiOwnerDrawButton)//{{AFX_MSG_MAP(CMyButton)...ON_REGISTERED_MESSAGE(AdUiMessage, OnAdUiMessage)//}}AFX_MSG_MAPEND_MESSAGE_MAP() Of course, the new handler will also need to be defined: LONG CMyButton::OnAdUiMessage (WPARAM wParam, LPARAM lParam){UINT controlId = LOWORD(wParam);ADUI_NOTIFY notifyCode = (ADUI_NOTIFY)HIWORD(wParam);ADUI_REPLY reply;reply = DoSomethingWithThisMessage(notifyCode, controlId, lParam);if (!reply)reply = CAdUiOwnerDrawButton::OnAdUiMessage(wParam, lParam);return reply;}

This method is intended to initialize the control following creation or subclassing, usually based on defaults set in the constructor. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. If you override this method you are encouraged to call the inherited method from your routine. The default routine applies the control's current Drag & Drop and PointedAt Effects enable settings. Returns TRUE if initialization is successful, FALSE otherwise
This routine is called from OnDropFiles() to handle Drag & Drop notifications. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler does nothing.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a DrawTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler ensures m_tipItem is valid, m_tipRect isn't empty and the control is actually owner-drawn. If so, then a WM_DRAWITEM request is processed by the control, using the relevant item, and drawing into the given DC.

This routine is called to have the control paint the contents of a TextTip. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The control has the option of drawing the text, altering the device context attributes, etc. If the routine returns TRUE then the caller assumes the request was completely handled. Otherwise if the routine returns FALSE then the caller proceeds with default processing and renders the text on its own. By default, if m_tipItem is valid then the control will draw the text and return TRUE, otherwise the method just returns FALSE. The routine accounts for the selection state of the relevant item and adjusts the foreground and background colors appropriately.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_DROPFILES to handle Drag & Drop notifications. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls OnDragDrop(), passing hDropInfo, then calls the inherited method.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_GETDLGCODE. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler returns the code obtained by calling the inherited method. If Static Display is enabled, the return code is modified to reflect static, rather than pushbutton, behavior. Returns a code indicating the type of input the control processes.

This routine is called to determine the size and placement of a DrawTip or TextTip window. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text and determines if it entirely fits within the item's rectangle in the control. If so the routine returns FALSE, otherwise a tip rectangle that can encompass the entire text is calculated, placed over the relevant item's rectangle, and the routine returns TRUE. Returning FALSE or an empty rectangle indicates that no tip should be displayed.

This routine is called to query the control for the type of tip window it supports. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. A control can return one of the following codes: kAdUiReply_Nothing No tip window is required or supported by the control. kAdUiReply_DrawTip The control is owner-draw and supports an owner-draw text tip (such as a DrawTip). kAdUiReply_TextTip The control can support a TextTip. kAdUiReply_ToolTip The control requests a standard ToolTip. The default handler updates m_tipItem via a call to GetItemAtPoint(), passing the designated point. If a relevant item is found then the control requests a DrawTip if owner-draw and a TextTip otherwise.

This routine is called by the default AdUi Message handler to process tip text requests. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler retrieves the relevant item's text (if any) and returns TRUE. On entry this routine usually receives an empty string. It's perfectly acceptable to simply return TRUE, indicating that the request was handled and that the control has no text to display. The result will be to suppress tip display. Returns TRUE if the request was handled, FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called to determine if the cursor position still pertains to the current tip displayed for the control. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler returns TRUE if the point lies within the relevant item's rectangle, and FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_KILLFOCUS. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method and inspects the button to determine if it is the default control in the containing dialog. If so, the Default Button style is removed and the handler attempts to locate a sibling OK button (IDOK) that is owner-drawn. If found, the sibling is given a Default Button style.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_MOUSEMOVE. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method. If the cursor position passed in differs from the point tracked in m_lastMousepoint, then a kAdUiNotify_UpdateTip notification is sent to the control's AdUi Parent window, informing it to update a tip window on behalf of the control (if necessary). Afterwards, m_lastMousePoint is updated with the given cursor position.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_NCDESTROY. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler stops the timer and then calls the inherited method.

This routine is called from IsPointedAt() to notify the button of a status change. The default OnMouseMove() and OnTimer() methods also call this routine. The method is declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default handler simply invalidates the control's window, triggering a repaint.

This method is intended to re-initialize the control in response to a kAdUiNotify_Reload notification. The default handler simply returns TRUE. Returns TRUE if re-initialization is successful, FALSE otherwise.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_SETFOCUS. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method and inspects the containing dialog, attempting to locate the default control in the dialog. If found, the Default Button style is removed from the control if it is owner-drawn. The focused button (i.e. this) is then given a Default Button style.

Handles WM_THEMECHANGED messages. The WM_THEMECHANGED message is broadcast to every window following a theme change event. Examples of theme change events are the activation of a theme, the deactivation of a theme, or a transition from one theme to another. To override this method, a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler refreshes the theme handle for the owner-drawn button.

This routine is called via the message map to process WM_TIMER. To override this method a derived class must provide its own message map entry. The default handler calls the inherited method, then compares nIDEvent to m_timerEvent. If the events match then the routine assumes it's processing a timer event associated with a PointedAt Effect. The handler checks if the mouse is still over the control. If so the timer is restarted, otherwise IsPointedAt() is called, passing FALSE as a parameter to notify the control it is no longer pointed at.

This member function is called by the framework to allow other necessary subclassing to occur before the window is subclassed. The default implementation opens the theme handle for the owner-drawn button before calling the base class implementation.

This method is intended to re-initialize the control at some point after being displayed. The method sends a kAdUiNotify_Reload notification to the control and returns TRUE if the reply is kAdUiReply_Ok, and FALSE otherwise.
This member sets the container CWnd to which the control should forward AdUi notifications and requests. Calling the method updates m_aduiParent.

This function is used to change the m_bEnableDragDrop data member setting. When this function is called m_bEnableDragDrop will be updated and code will be called to actually enable or disable Drag & Drop for the button. While enabled, OnDropFiles() and OnDragDrop() will be able to participate in Drag & Drop notifications.

This function is used to change the button's FastDraw setting. When the method is used m_bEnableFastDraw will be updated. While the setting is enabled, the default DrawItem() routine will create a device context in-memory and draw to it, then copy the results to the DC it would normally draw to (usually the display). The technique usually results in faster output and reduced flicker.

This function is used to change the PointedAt Effects setting. The term PointedAt Effects refers to the manner in which the button reacts when the mouse moves over the control. When this function is called m_bEnablePointedAt will be updated and code will be called to actually enable or disable effects for the button. While enabled, IsPointedAt(), OnMouseMove(), OnPointedAt() and OnTimer() all participate in providing effects.
This function is used to toggle the value of m_bIsPointedAt. When the second method is called m_bIsPointedAt is updated and OnPointedAt() is called, passing isPointedAt as a parameter.
This function is used to toggle the value of m_bIsStatic. When this function is called the m_bIsStatic member is updated.
This function is used to toggle that tool button status. When this function is called the m_bIsToolButton member is updated.
Sets the theme to be used by the owner draw button

This method stops the timer and, if the indicated interval is not zero, restarts it. The timer is started using the event given in the member m_timerEvent. On success m_timerId will contain a non-zero timer handle.
This method stops the timer and sets m_timerId to zero.
Virtual method that receives the theme modification event.
This is the class destructor. It has been declared virtual for use by derived classes. The default method does nothing.

The CAdUiPalette class represents a palette window. A palette window exists in a hierarchy consisting of a parent palette set that contains one or more palette windows. The CAdUiPalette class supports the following palette style constant: Style Constant Value Meaning PS_EDIT_NAME 0x00000001 Supports editing of palette set name through in-place editing

This function is called by the palette set before it displays its context menu. Overriding this function allows derived classes to make adjustments to the menu that the base class context menu implementation will display. The override returns a value of false to indicate that the base class implementation of the context menu should not be used, in which case desired derived class behavior is implemented within the override.To proceed with the base class implementation, the function should return true.
Appends the specified palette to the end of the palette set. Returns its zero-based index in the palette set or -1 if the palette was not added.
Sets a flag as to whether or not global opacities ought to be used.
Called when the auto-rollup state of the palette set changes. Override this function in the derived class to receive notification each time the auto-rollup state of the palette set changes.
Returns true if the palette set has the PSS_AUTO_ROLLUP style set; otherwise, returns false.

Override this method to control input focus. The palette set will at times be asked to give up the input focus. Returns false to indicate that the palette set needs to keep the input focus, or true to indicate that the palette set doesn't need input focus.
Returns true if the palette set has the PSS_CLOSE_BUTTON style set; otherwise, returns false.
Creates the palette set window. Returns true on successful palette set creation; otherwise, returns false.
Returns true if the palette set has the PSS_EDIT_NAME style set; otherwise, returns false.
Returns a pointer to the currently active palette.
Returns the zero-based tab index of the currently active palette.

When a palette set is docked, a 'grabber bar' is drawn within the window's client area. This can cause problems for positioning palette set elements. Use this method to get the adjusted palette set client rect. For example, if the palette set is docked on the side of the application frame, this method will return a rect whose top coordinate is 13 rather than 0. Palette set elements should be positioned within this 'adjusted' client rect.
Returns true if auto rollup is enabled. Returns false if it is disabled or if the the auto-rollup style is not set for the palette set.

This function returns the amount of vertical space, in pixels, that should be reserved at the bottom of the palette set client area for the palette set's own use. Override this function if the derived palette set class needs to keep some client-area real estate for its own use, in effect decreasing the size of the palettes contained in the palette set. The base class implementation returns zero.
Gets the full window rectangle of the palette set. This function retrieves the rectangle of the unrolled palette set even if the palette set is currently rolled up.
Returns the global rollover opacity value.
This function provides a maximum size for the palette set in size. Override it to provide a different maximum size.

This function provides a minimum size for the palette set in size. Override it to provide a different minimum size. The minimum horizontal size of the client area of a palette set is determined by taking the greater of the largest minimum horizontal size returned by a palette in the set and the minimum horizontal size returned by the palette set's GetMinimumSize() function. The minimum vertical size of the client area of a palette set is determined by taking the sum of the largest minimum vertical size returned by a palette in the set and the minimum vertical size returned by the palette set's GetMinimumSize() function.
Returns the name of the palette set.
Returns the current opacity for the palette set. Valid values are in the range 0 to 100, where 0 is completely transparent and 100 is completely opaque.
Returns a pointer to the palette whose tab index was passed in nIndex; or returns null if there is no palette at that index.
Returns the number of palettes in the palette set.
Returns the palette set style, which is a combination of the CAdUiPaletteSet palette style constants.
Returns the zero-based tab index of the palette specified by pPalette or -1 if the specified palette is not found.
Gets the theme being used by the palette set
Returns the icon for the current palette theme and the specified size.

This function returns the amount of palette set client area vertical space, in pixels, that should be reserved at the top of the client area for the palette set's own use. Override this function if the derived palette set class needs to keep some client area real estate for its own use, in effect decreasing the size of the palettes contained in the palette set. The base class implementation returns zero.
Returns a pointer to the primary font in use by the palette set. This may differ from the font returned by CWnd::GetFont().
Returns true if pt is within the window rectangle of the palette set; otherwise, returns false.

Inserts the specified palette into the palette set at the position specified by iIndex. Returns the zero-based palette tab index of the inserted palette; or returns -1 if the palette was not inserted.
Returns true if global opacities are permissible.

Be sure to call the base class (CAdUiPaletteSet) implementation of this method before loading derived class saved data. Returns true if the load was successful; otherwise, returns false.

The implementation should return true to approve the new name and false to reject it.

Returns true if the palette has the PS_EDIT_NAME style set; otherwise, returns false.

The minimum horizontal size of the client area of a palette set is determined by taking the greater of the largest minimum horizontal size returned by a palette in the set and the minimum horizontal size returned by the palette set's GetMinimumSize() function. Returns the name of the palette.

Returns true if the name in pEdit is valid; returns false if it is not valid. It can also be used as an output parameter to highlight problems involving invalid names in the edit box. The implementation should return true to approve the new name and false to reject it.

Returning false gives the palette the opportunity to avoid being deactivated. Returns true to indicate that it is OK to deactivate the palette; returns false to indicate that it is not OK to deactivate it.
Called by the palette set when this palette is about to become active. Override this function to inform the derived palette that it is being activated.

Sets this palette's containing palette set.
Sets the palette style. The only valid palette style to set is PS_EDIT_NAME.

This class is a general purpose class used to deal with pathnames, both standard DOS style (long) pathnames and UNC pathnames. The class does not deal with URLs. The class has methods for parsing a pathname and setting up the data in the object. It also has methods for extracting components of the path and for modifying the path.

DescriptionGetFullPathAdds a new extension regardless of any existing extension. This method will never produce a '..' error. Returns an error if the resulting path would be invalid, or if the path is not a file.
Adds a new extension if there is no existing extension, or if the existing extension doesn't match the argument.
Appends a string to the end of the path. This routine doesn't check whether the path ends in a slash. Returns an error if the resulting path would be invalid.
Appends a component separator to the end of the path followed by sString. This method will never produce a '//' error. Returns an error if the resulting path would be invalid.
Appends a component separator to the end of the path. Does nothing if the path already ends in a slash and returns an error if the resulting path would be invalid.
This function copies all of the information from source into the object on which it is called.
Modifies the case of the basename (name.ext) to be all lowercase.
Modifies the case of the basename (name.ext) to be all uppercase.
Reinitializes the data without destroying the object.
Checks whether this path points to an existing file or directory. Returns false if the path is empty.
Finds or creates (as required), the volume descriptor for the specified local name (drive letter, etc.)
Returns the rightmost component of the path (a directory name or file extension). If the path terminates in a slash, returns NULL.

Returns a display name for this path. Abbreviation rules are applied to reduce the length of the display name if its length is greater than maxchars. Set maxchars to zero to avoid abbreviating. Your program is responsible for freeing the string strResult. Examples: If maxchars is -1, then the path is not truncated. If maxchars is < 12 and != -1, then effective maxchars is 12.
Returns the string to right of last period in the rightmost component. Returns NULL if this is not a file.
Returns the string to left of last period in the rightmost component. Returns NULL if this is not a file.
Deprecated. Returns the file system type of a volume.
Gets a filesystem type object based on the specified volume.
Returns the full path starting with the local volume name. Relative paths are fully resolved.
Returns the UNC path if this object represents a remote drive, otherwise returns NULL.

This function returns the last character in str. For a single-byte character set, it returns the last byte. For a Unicode character set, it returns the last Unicode character (16 bit). For a double-byte character set, it returns the lead byte of the last character.
Returns the parent path of the current path. For example, c:foo is the parent of c:foobar.
Returns the pathname as a string.
Returns the path type of this pathname (file, dir, device special, or empty).
Generates a unique pathname based on the provided pathname. The file is created and closed; you will need to delete this file if it is not wanted.
Returns the volume descriptor of this pathname.
Returns true if path string passed to the object had a prefix.
Returns true if the path is a device name.
Returns true if the path_type is NO_PATH.
Returns true if the path_type is file or dir (otherwise trim/append is not supported).
Indicates whether the path represents a virtual file/directory.
Takes a path and tries to open it to be read-only. Returns true if the open succeeded, and false otherwise.
Takes a path and tries to open it to be write-only. Returns true if the open succeeded, and false otherwise.

This method parses a string, validates the format and fills in the data. Parse() actually calls ParseRelative() with the current document path (if any) or the current application path as the relative path.
Parses a string and attempts to find a matching file by operating system (OS) rules, that is, whatever the current OS search path is. This method works like an implicit ParseRelative() call.

This method parses a string, validates the format and fills in the data. The third parameter indicates whether an absolute path will be accepted or cause an error. NOTE: This routine will recognize device names and proceed accordingly.
Returns true if the two paths refer to the same object.
Tries to remove the file pointed to by this path. Returns true if the operation succeeds, and false otherwise.
This method removes the extension, if present, including the period ('.') before the extension.
If there is an extension and it matches the argument, the extension is removed.
Strips leading and trailing spaces from the file name.
Tries to rename the file pointed to by this path. Returns true if the operation succeeds, and false otherwise.
Adds a new extension or replaces any existing extension. This method will never produce a '..' error. Returns an error if the resulting path would be invalid, or if the path is not a file.
Adds a new extension if there is no existing extension, or replaces the existing extension if it doesn't match the argument.

Removes the last component from the path, leaving the path terminated with a slash. If this is a partial (relative) path, and there is no slash remaining (the trimmed path would be empty), the method returns an error.
Removes the last component, including the beginning slash. Returns an error if removing the slash would leave an empty path.
Removes a trailing component separator. If the last character is not a slash, nothing is done. The method returns an error if removing the slash would leave an empty path.

If the string starts with optional whitespace followed by a double quote, and it ends with a double quote followed by optional whitespace, then the double quotes and optional whitespace are trimmed off.

Returns true if the path string passed to the object was an absolute path.
Returns true if the path string passed to the object contained a leading separator (for example, 'file.txt').

This class provides the functionality for AdUi pop-up tip windows, specifically TextTips and DrawTips. AdUi provides three types of tip windows - ToolTips, TextTips and DrawTips. ToolTips represent stock Windows Tool-Tips, as provided by the Common Controls DLL installed on the user's system. TextTips are text-based tip windows that pop-up over a control, usually to reveal data that the user would otherwise have to scroll into view. DrawTips are an extension of TextTips; the control underneath the tip is usually responsible for painting the contents of the tip (analogous to an owner-draw tip). Most applications rarely involve this class directly; AdUi usually handles all of the requirements. AdUi uses its internal messaging system to negotiate between containers and controls and decide when and how to display a tip.

The following sections discuss working with dimension styles in ObjectARX.

Dimension style families are sets of dimension styles (AcDbDimStyleTableRecords) that are related to one another by name. The child dimStyles are named with a numeric suffix. There are five suffixes based on the dimension entity's type. For example, for a parent dimStyle named 'TESTSTYLE', the valid suffixes are: TESTSTYLE$0 Linear child of TESTSTYLE (both rotated and aligned types) TESTSTYLE$2 Angular child of TESTSTYLE (both 2-line and 3-point types) TESTSTYLE$3 Diameter child of TESTSTYLE TESTSTYLE$4 Radius child of TESTSTYLE TESTSTYLE$6 Ordinate child of TESTSTYLE TESTSTYLE$7 Leader child of TESTSTYLE (used for tolerance entities (AcDbFcf) also) The key points about how dimStyle families work in the AutoCAD environment are as follows:Child dimStyle selection does not happen automatically in the AutoCAD APIs. If you programmatically create a dimension (such as (entmake), acdbEntMake(), or create a new dimension object via the ObjectARX API), you get exactly what you specify.AcDbDatabase has some helpful methods for child style manipulation; see getDimstyleChildData(), getDimstyleChildId(), and getDimstyleParentId().A named dimStyle is chosen for the particular dimension based on the type of the dimension. The parent dimStyle is used unless a child exists. (If a child dimStyle is the current dimStyle, it will be used no matter what type of dimension is being operated upon. But DDIM tries to make sure child styles are not current.)Overrides are computed based on the current dimStyle and not the child dimStyle, in cases where it is different (if overrides were computed against the child, all differences between the parent and child would become overrides and the style would effectively be the parent dimStyle.)This override computation process occurs when a dimension is first created by any of AutoCAD's dimension creation commands. It also happens during DIMSTYLE APPLY and DIM UPDATE operations.Dimension entities in pre-Release 14 DWG files may not have a dimension style. When AutoCAD edits such dimensions for the first time it assigns them the current dimStyle with family logic, so that if the appropriate child style exists, it is used.dimStyle families are only related by name. No persistent form of inheritance exists. As far as AutoCAD is concerned, child and parent dimStyles are completely unrelated. Edits made to parent dimStyles will have no effect on child dimStyles.The command line interface to dimStyles is completely dumb about families. You can make a child style current on the command line (DIMSTYLE RESTORE or DIM RESTORE). You can make a child without making a parent on the command line, etc. To the command line UI, parents and children are indistinguishable. They are autonomous dimStyles.

Dimension style overrides can be applied to any of the AcDbEntity types that reference an AcDbDimStyleTableRecord. These are: AcDbAlignedDimensionAcDbRotatedDimensionAcDbDiametricDimensionAcDbRadialDimensionAcDb2LineAngularDimensionAcDb3PointAngularDimensionAcDbOrdinateDimensionAcDbLeaderAcDbFcf Dimension overrides applied to an object of any of these classes are stored as xdata under the 'ACAD' appId in a special subsection. The subsection starts with a group code 1000 (AcDb::kDxfXdAsciiString) with the string 'DSTYLE', followed by all the dimension override data bracketed inside a pair of group code 1002s (AcDb::kDxfXdControlString) (the first being a '{' and the other a '}'). Dimension variables in general are called dimvars, and this data is commonly called 'per-entity dimvar overrides' or just dimvar overrides. Within the group code 1002 brackets is a chain of dimvar group-code/data-value resbuf pairs, one pair for each dimvar being overridden. The first resbuf in each pair is the DXF group code for the dimvar, as found in the Table below. Since the group code is an integer it has a restype of AcDb::kDxfXdInteger16 (group code 1070). The second resbuf in each pair is the value for that dimvar. Data values for dimvars may be strings, integers, reals, or objectIds. As with resbufs in general, the value of the resbufs restype indicates how to read the data in the resval. Please refer to the Table below. As an example, here is a dimension style override list that will override the DIMTAD and DIMGAP variables. The list is shown in AutoLISP format with indenting for clarity. ('ACAD' (1000 . 'DSTYLE') (1002 . '{') (1070 . 77) (1070 . 1) (1070 . 147) (1000 . 0.2) (1002 . '}'))In this example the group code 77 is DIMTAD, which is overridden to be 1. Then DIMGAP (group code 147) is set to 0.2. The following code sample uses acutBuildList() to create this resbuf chain and to set overrides for DIMTAD and DIMGAP on the entity pointed to by pEnt, assuming pEnt points to an AcDbEntity of one of the types listed above and is open for writing: resbuf* pRb = acutBuildList( AcDb::kDxfRegAppName,'ACAD', AcDb::kDxfXdAsciiString,'DSTYLE', AcDb::kDxfXdControlString, '{', AcDb::kDxfXdInteger16, 77, AcDb::kDxfXdInteger16, 1, AcDb::kDxfXdInteger16, 147, AcDb::kDxfXdReal,0.2, AcDb::kDxfXdControlString, '}', RTNONE);Acad::ErrorStatus es = pEnt->setXdata(pRb);acutRelRb(pRb);It is very important the xdata you set onto an object have the proper sequence of resbufs. Each override must have both the DXF group code resbuf and the associated value resbuf. In addition, the value must be the correct data type (string, real, or int) and must be within the allowable range for that dimvar. If any of these conditions are not met, AutoCAD may terminate. Also, the 1000 'DSTYLE' and the following 1002 '{' '}' set must be present, and there must only be one set of all of these. Remember that xdata is obtained and replaced on a per-appId basis. To modify any dimension overrides, work with the complete list of xdata for the 'ACAD' appId, which may have other data, including other dimension overrides. So, be sure to obtain whatever xdata may already be present for the 'ACAD' appId (use the object's xData() method with the string 'ACAD'). Add or remove only the dimension override information you need, making sure that if dimension override information already exists you don't duplicate any of the xdata that's already there (including the 'DSTYLE' string and the 1002 '{' '}' bracket pairs). Place new overrides in between the existing 1002 bracket pair, and put the complete modified list back into the object via the object's setXData() method. If not done correctly, AutoCAD may terminate. On the New Tab Page, there are neither any drawing views nor drawing database. Hence, a lot of functions and related palettes need to be hidden when switching in to NewTab Page. Again when switching back to your drawing document, we need to restore those functions and related palettes. AcApDocManagerReactor is used to trace a document create, switch, and destroy state. You can use this class to achieve your request. For example, if one palette needs to be hidden in New Tab Page, that palette needs to create a reactor class that inherits from AcApDocManagerReactor and check pActivatedDoc in the active document function. If pActivatedDoc is null, it means that the active document is the New Tab Page, which hides the palette in this function. When pActivatedDoc is not null, you need to restore this palette.

The New Tab Page is a non-dwg document. If the current active document is a New Tab Page, there are no drawing database and drawing views related to the New Tab Page. Hence, when you implement new code that might be running on the New Tab Page, you should be careful before doing any get and modify current drawing database and drawing view functions. To check the current active document for:C++ : If curDoc() is NULL, we are on the NewTabPage. Do not try to get and modify current drawing database and drawing view..NET: If ApplicationServices.Application.DocumentManager.MdiActiveDocument is null, we are one the NewTab Page. Do not try to get and modify current drawing database and drawing view.

This function creates a new AcRxClass object, fills it in with all the appropriate information to be ready to be added to the ObjectARX run-time class tree, and then adds the newly created AcRxClass object to the AcRxClass object dictionary (accessible via the acrxClassDictionary macro). proxyFlags can be a bit-wise combination of any of the AcDbProxyEntity or AcDbProxyObject enum values, such as AcDbProxyEntity::keraseAllowed. If it is not NULL, the func argument must point to a function that can provide a new logical application name for the custom class. The function pointed to by the callback pointer will be called when the custom class is being saved to a DWF or DXF file. The callback function uses the following template: typedef void (*AppNameChangeFuncPtr)(const AcRxClass* classObj, char*& newAppName, int saveVer);It is passed a pointer to the AcRxClass object for the custom class, a reference to a char* to be set to the address of the new logical application name string, and the DWG version that is being saved. The callback function should dynamically allocate a string buffer using acutNewString(), or equivalent, to ensure that the string's memory is allocated in the host application's heap; copy the new logical application name string into the buffer, and set the newAppNamechar* reference to point to this new string buffer. After the callback returns, the host application uses the new logical application name in the DWG or DXF file created by the save operation. No change is made to the logical application name in the source DWG file. The host application is responsible for freeing the memory used by the new logical application name string. This function is used by the rxInit() function of classes that are to be added to the ObjectARX run-time class tree.

Information about how to update existing ObjectARX applications to work with AutoCAD 2025 is provided here. AutoCAD 2025 is a binary compatibility release and ObjectARX applications developed for AutoCAD 2021, AutoCAD 2022, or AutoCAD 2023 shouldn't need to be recompiled. Applications developed for AutoCAD 2020 and earlier releases will need to be recompiled. The following sections list API changes made to this release. If your application uses any of these APIs, you will need to update your code accordingly.

This function will attempt to find and open an AcDbTextStyleTableRecord with the name contained in AcDbStyleName. The AcDbStyleId argument is set to the objectId of the AcDbTextStyleTableRecord object that is used. Returns Acad::eOk if successful. This class organizes matching calls to accessAcDbObjectForWrite and revertAcDbObjectFromWrite to ease their use. All the caller supplies is a reference to an AcDbObject pointer. Using the Liang-Barsky algorithm, this function clips or trims a PyGe.LineSeg2d to the bounding box defined by min/max coordinates. It returns a tuple (bool, PyGe.LineSeg2d). It returns True if the segment is inside the box and has been clipped to a valid line segment. It returns False only if the segment is completely outside the box, or has been clipped to a zero-length point (intersection at a corner).

This function clips or trims a PyGe.CircArc2d to the bounding box defined by min/max coordinates. It returns a tuple (bool, list[PyGe.CircArc2d]). It returns True if the segment is inside the box and has been clipped to a valid line segment. It returns False only if the segment is completely outside the box, returns multiple CircArc2ds in the case of reentry

Parameters: The algorithm accepts parameters to control the output shape: concavity: A relative measure of concavity. A value of 1 provides a detailed shape, while Infinity results in a convex hull. lengthThreshold: Determines when a segment is too short to be considered for further detailization, helping to simplify the shape. Returns a Point3dArray
